Luckily the knife flies low, hits him in the chest and bounces off his jacket, thanks to the cloak's anti-piercing benefit. Four more lemurs appear in the window.

beats.headline: Anything but the Nightgaunts
beats.text: A wheel spins to choose the opponents of the next level, and one of its four choices is the Nightgaunt Precipice. Donut hopes for the foxes. Carl holds his breath and hopes for anything but the Nightgaunt choice: his cloak's description specifically warned that Nightgaunts would be enraged by the sight of it, and he doesn't want to have to get rid of it. Click, click, click. The wheel stops on the second choice.

beats.headline: A Nightgaunt sees the cloak
beats.text: Combat starts by a dilapidated farmhouse, and a warning with it: Carl's equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt. The System explains that a Nightgaunt is a real creature, semi-intelligent, peaceful, vegetarian and nocturnal, which the game uses as a demon because, well, look at them. Mordecai had warned Carl the cloak would aggravate this kind of mob, but Carl had not realized how passionately. The demon never plays a single card. It glares at the cloak and screeches one last time, until a giant cat picks it up in his jaws and shakes it to death.

beats.headline: A garment taunt
beats.text: Among the achievements is LBC. Every girl needs the perfect little black dress, practically weaponised when worn properly, and Carl did the same thing with a cloak: he taunted an opponent with a garment, in this case a Nightgaunt, because he is wearing a cloak made out of the flesh of one of its friends. The reward is a Gold Talk of the Town Box. Carl remembers how insane the cloak drove the creature. That time it was a good thing: it kept the monster from using its deck.

entities.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk
aka: Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk

tagline.text: A toe ring is what the gold shoe box gives Carl, at a time when what he needs is shoes.

The Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk gives Carl three Strength and three levels of Powerful Strike, which multiplies his damage when he fights without a weapon. It sits on the index toe of his right foot, and it is uncomfortable, as promised.
Upgraded once by a scroll, Carl's toe ring now gives ten Strength and five levels of Powerful Strike.

description.text: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. Imbues wearer with +3 Strength and gives +3 to the skill Powerful Strike. Also, it’s a toe ring. It’s probably uncomfortable and it makes you look like one of those hippie assholes who sit around in a field juggling and hula-hooping all day.

Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. (Upgraded) The item has been upgraded once. Imbues wearer with +10 Strength and gives +5 to the skill Powerful Strike. Also, it’s a toe ring. It’s probably uncomfortable and it makes you look like one of those hippie assholes who sit around in a field juggling and hula-hooping all day.

beats.headline: A toe ring, not shoes
beats.text: Carl's ten boxes pop out of his inventory and float before him in single file. The ninth glows gold and is labelled a shoe box, and it holds a toe ring. A goddamned toe ring. He needed shoes, damnit, not a toe ring. He is so irritated by the prize that he almost misses the last box opening.

beats.headline: On the index toe
beats.text: Carl reads it: three Strength, three to Powerful Strike, and the reminder that it is a toe ring. Mordecai rates the skill. Each level multiplies his damage when he isn't wielding a weapon, so at level three every kick or punch does three times what it would; with his Unarmed Combat and Pugilism skills his fists already do more damage than the cudgel or the poker, and a monk class might suit him. Carl sits down and slips the ring on. It adjusts itself onto the filthy, bloody index toe of his right foot. As the description warned, it is uncomfortable.

beats.headline: Upgraded off the wheel
beats.text: On Tito's prize wheel the needle hangs on the last spot before Nothing! and settles on green: a Scroll of Upgrade, to be read within twenty minutes. Mordecai warned him last time not to take anything off first. Carl reads it, his foot buzzes, and the toe ring glows. Ten Strength now, up seven, and five to Powerful Strike. With a base of seven in the skill and one more from his gauntlet, his damage is multiplied by thirteen.

beats.headline: Diminishing returns past fifteen
beats.text: In a training room on the sixth floor, a skill all his gear should lift to sixteen stays at fifteen. Armour and weapon enhancements lose effectiveness past fifteen, as Mordecai warned. The gauntlet's one point of Powerful Strike and the toe ring's five will still carry Carl past it, but he will probably need to reach twelve or so on his own first, and each level beyond comes with diminishing returns.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling comes out of a gold apparel box beside a nightgaunt cloak, and Mordecai gasps the moment the two appear.

The trollskin shirt gives Carl seven levels of Regeneration and negates melee debuffs such as Stun, Knockback, Disarm and Out-of-Breath. Mordecai calls it one of the best under-armour garments for tanking, the sort of thing found in a Platinum or Legendary box.
A Scroll of Upgrade has added three Dexterity to Carl's trollskin shirt, a decent upgrade if not a great one.

description.text: Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling. The wearer of this shirt gains +7 to the Regeneration skill. In addition, all melee-based damage debuffs such as Stun, Knockback, Disarm, and Out-of-Breath are negated. The shirt is also quite stylish. Maybe a little too stylish. Unlike most monster-skin apparel items, this shirt will not grant a negative reaction amongst trolls. In fact, lady trolls might just want to haul you away for some one-on-one time if they see you in this.

beats.headline: Mordecai gasps at it
beats.text: The eighth of Carl's ten boxes is a gold apparel box, bigger than the ones before it and glowing with a golden light. It holds two items, a nightgaunt cloak and a trollskin shirt, and beside him Mordecai gasps the moment they appear. Carl hopes that is a good thing.

beats.headline: Better. Much better
beats.text: The cloak is extremely valuable, says Mordecai, but the shirt is better. Much better. A level-seven Regeneration skill brings Carl back to full health in as little as two minutes after taking damage, and finding it was a lucky break. Carl pulls off his jacket and slips on the short-sleeved shirt. It is cool to the touch and fits itself to his skin. The jacket goes back on over it, then the cloak, and achievements arrive for wearing loot and magical gear for the first time.

beats.headline: No Take Down
beats.text: Rot stickers, little black raviolis that run on walls and ceilings, stick to a crawler and explode, and every blast inflicts Take Down, which is supposed to knock you on your ass. The shirt negates it. Once the fighting is done and a potion lets him sort his inventory by value, Carl notes the list leaves out what he is wearing, and suspects the shirt would be at the top of it otherwise.

beats.headline: Three points of Dexterity
beats.text: After a neighbourhood boss, the best prize in the boxes is a Scroll of Upgrade, which has been good to Carl so far. Applied, all it does is add three Dexterity to his trollskin shirt. That is decent, since he meant to put a couple of points into Dexterity anyway, but it is not a great upgrade.

tagline.text: The Goblin Pass comes out of a silver goblin box as a goblin-shaped skull that flies at Carl's left inner forearm and brands itself there, showing through his jacket as well.

The Goblin Pass is a tattoo that removes goblin hostility and grants free passage through goblin territory. The catch is that fairy-class creatures, the goblins' natural enemies, deal twenty percent more damage to whoever carries it.

description.text: Goblin Pass. It’s a tattoo! On your forearm! Now you’ll never get a good job! Note: Pass tattoos cannot be hidden unless you purchase a coverup sleeve. Will show through any armor you may wear. Removes automatic goblin hostility. Allows for free passage through goblin-controlled territory in the dungeon. Warning: holding a Goblin Pass will cause natural goblin enemies, such as fairy-class creatures, to deal 20% more damage against you. Still, it looks kinda badass.

beats.headline: Branded, not stored
beats.text: The seventh of Carl's boxes is a silver goblin box: five sticks of dynamite, a lighter, and a Goblin Pass. The pass takes the form of the goblin-shaped skull on the box's lid and, instead of adding itself to his inventory, flies at his left inner forearm. Through his leather jacket it burns like a brand. The brand appears on the outside of the jacket too, the pain quickly abates, and the jacket is otherwise undamaged.

beats.headline: He never wanted one
beats.text: Carl puts his hand on the symbol branded onto his jacket and an infobox pops up. A tattoo, on his forearm; now he will never get a good job. It cannot be hidden without a coverup sleeve and shows through any armour. It ends automatic goblin hostility and allows free passage through goblin territory, and fairy-class creatures will deal twenty percent more damage against him. Carl grumbles that the system didn't give him a choice. He has no tattoos and never really wanted one.

beats.headline: Shown to three goblins
beats.text: Down an abandoned alley that smells of machines, oil and pineapple, Carl tells Donut they are not killing the goblins if they don't have to. Three level two goblins come at them with pineapple sticks. He lifts his arm, shows the tattoo and claims free passage. Their dots turn from red to white and they lower their weapons. One asks where he got the mark. Before Carl can answer, Donut tells them he blew up one of their filthy tractors and smeared three of their friends all over the cobblestones.

beats.headline: Twenty percent harder
beats.text: The clurichauns are fairy-class mobs, and their description says so: twenty percent more damage against him, due to his goblin pass. Running, buzzed and laughing at nothing, Carl takes a slingshot rock off the head. His health bar drops further than it should, the damage enhanced by his stupid goblin tattoo.

beats.headline: Nearly a sleeve
beats.text: A Gold Apostate box slaps another tattoo onto Carl's left upper arm, his largest yet: a flaming ball of snakes, one head reaching down to curl round the spiderweb tattoo on his elbow. With this, the spiderweb and the goblin pass, he practically has a whole sleeve on his left arm.

tagline.text: A Standard Healing Potion comes in a small red glass bottle with a cork and raises the drinker's health by at least half. Put on the hotlist, it is drunk without actually drinking.
A healing potion comes with a timer: drink a second before the first one's fifteen seconds are up, and the drinker is poisoned.
Healing potions hurt the dead: a note in the Cookbook says a smoke curtain soaked in one and left to dry mass-kills undead.
Healing potions come in grades, standard, fine and gold standard among them, and Carl keeps a gold-standard one loaded in his new toe ring, set to trigger on its own at two percent health.

description.text: Standard Healing Potion. Increases your health by at least 50%. Doesn’t cure poison or other health-seeping conditions such as succubus-inflicted gonorrhea. So remember to wrap it up, bucko.

beats.headline: A gift from Mordecai
beats.text: Mordecai produces a single glass bottle, small, about a third the size of a Coke bottle, red with a cork in it: a gift from him to Carl. Carl examines it, adds it to his inventory, which now has a Potions and Healing submenu, and pulls it back into his hand with a mental click. Put it on your hotlist, Mordecai tells him, and you will drink it without having to actually drink. Then his boxes open: one bronze adventurer box holds two more potions of healing, and another one more.

beats.headline: Kiwi juice and poison
beats.text: Donut is soaked in blood and barely alive. The Heal Critter scroll will not work on her, and Carl does not know where her potion countdown stands: she took a mana potion a few minutes ago. So he tests on himself. The quick slots won't let him take a second potion. He drinks one by hand, his first time physically drinking one, and it tastes oddly like kiwi juice. Then he drinks a second before the fifteen-second timer is done. You have been poisoned! Poison effect nullified.

beats.headline: Against the undead
beats.text: The Cookbook's explosives section carries a note from Crawler Sinjin of the fifteenth edition: a level 3 sapper's table lets you infuse bombs, and a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in a healing potion and left to dry mass-kills undead like you wouldn't believe. Crawler Forkith of the twentieth confirms it. It works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad.

beats.headline: Napalm for vampires
beats.text: Mordecai has an idea before they leave: two potion balls, dipped in the red water of the Emberus shrine at the back of the room. The system labels them Holy Goopers. Blessed water, a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant: Emberus is a light-based god, and against vampires the mixture acts like napalm. Hit them with it, he says, then have Donut max out her Torch spell.

beats.headline: Into the fog
beats.text: A park several blocks wide is filled with red dots and roiling fog, and Sister Ines, who can tell whether a mob is undead, says all of them are. Levitating for a view, Carl tosses a potion ball filled with a fine healing potion into a dense patch of red. Three of the mobs die, easily and soundlessly, for very little experience, and he tells the others they are good to go.

beats.headline: Set to two percent
beats.text: Carl's new Legendary toe ring, which must go on his left pinky toe and says so twice, can store one potion that triggers itself when his health meets a condition. He grits his teeth, slips the ring on, and is prompted to choose. He picks a gold-standard healing potion, set to trigger if his health reaches two percent.

tagline.text: A Pet Biscuit is dry pet food that feeds a pet-based class for a full day. Pets find them delicious and will gobble them on smell, so they come out of an inventory one at a time.
A pet biscuit tossed into a cage turns a beaten danger dingo's dot from red to white. Donut, who still eats them, calls feeding hers to a dingo a betrayal most foul.
Pet biscuits are how Mongo is trained, because he is very food motivated.

beats.headline: Ten, then five hundred
beats.text: The first of Carl's ten boxes, a bronze pet box stencilled with a hedgehog-like animal, holds a scroll of Heal Critter and ten pet biscuits, a small pile of what looks like dry cat food. The last, the Legendary Pet Box, holds five hundred more and one enhanced biscuit. Regular biscuits feed pet-based classes for a full day, Mordecai explains. Pets find them delicious; they smell them and gobble them up, so only pull one out at a time.

beats.headline: A betrayal most foul
beats.text: Outside the kobold boss room, beaten danger dingoes lie in cages. Carl has no Heal Critter scrolls left, but he has a ton of pet biscuits, which Donut still eats despite being a regular crawler. He tosses one into a cage. CARL WHAT ARE YOU DOING. THAT IS MY FOOD. The dingo pulls itself up painfully, sniffs, eats the tiny biscuit and turns its back, and its dot blinks white. They repeat it for all fourteen.

beats.headline: Pecked like a chicken
beats.text: The baby mongoliensis comes out of its cage thrashing and trying to bite. Carl has to sit on the ground holding it in both hands while Donut pulls a few pet biscuits from her inventory. It slows, eyeing the food, and when he eases his grip it pecks at them like a chicken. Its dot stays red. Carl, it's a boy, Donut cries, and promises Mongo a bow tie. He bites her on the nose.

beats.headline: A very food-motivated dinosaur
beats.text: Several hours of dog commands follow. Attack, come and even lie down work really well; stay is another story. Mongo is very food motivated and loves pet biscuits, which makes him easier to train. After a full day he no longer charges at everything he sees. He snarls and hops, but waits for Donut's command, which has somehow evolved from attack to sic 'em.

beats.headline: Get over it
beats.text: Donut lets Mongo back out onto the street and he forms in front of them with a pop, screeching in outrage and hopping in circles round them. Oh, get over it, says Carl, and tosses him a pet biscuit. Mongo snatches it in midair and growls as he chews, placated, then takes his place at Carl's right side as Donut leaps to Carl's shoulder. He really is well-trained, Carl tells her.

relations.note: she eats them herself

tagline.text: The Poker is the second weapon the dungeon hands Carl, out of a Bronze Weapon Box. It is literally a fireplace poker, a wrought-iron stick with a screw-on point at the end.
Tried against a level-four cockroach, the Poker is knocked out of Carl's hand at the first stab, and he shoves the useless thing into his inventory.

beats.headline: Bronze Weapon Box, four of ten
beats.text: Carl's first ten boxes pop out of his inventory and float in front of him single file, opening by tier. The third, a Bronze Weapon Box, gives him a toad cudgel. The fourth is another Bronze Weapon Box, and this one isn't much better: a Poker. It is literally a fireplace poker, a wrought-iron stick with a screw-on point at the end. After it come one more bronze box, then the silver ones and the gold.

beats.headline: Knocked out of his hand
beats.text: A Scatterer Brood Guardian, a level-four cockroach, charges, and the toad cudgel bounces off its head. Carl quickly switches to his poker to see if that's better. It charges again and he stabs with the iron stick; its giant head knocks the poker right out of his hand, and it goes flying. This place has the shittiest weapons. He kills the roach with his feet. Then he retrieves the poker, decides the damn thing is useless, and shoves it into his inventory.

entities.name: Scroll of Heal Critter
entities.role: A pet heal, good for one reading

tagline.text: A Scroll of Heal Critter came out of Carl's very first box, a bronze pet box, with ten pet biscuits: a single rolled-up piece of paper.
Read on Donut, a Scroll of Heal Critter does nothing and evaporates with an error message: No Valid Target Available.
A Heal Critter scroll fizzles out where something blocks magic, and Mongo, bleeding, has to heal on his own.

beats.headline: First out of the first box
beats.text: The first of Carl's ten boxes is bronze, with a strange, hedgehog-like animal stencilled on the top: Bronze Pet Box. It pops open on its own and disappears in a puff of smoke, leaving a single rolled-up piece of paper and a small pile of what looks like dry cat food. Text appears over each: Scroll of Heal Critter. Pet Biscuit X 10. The items go into his inventory, and before he can open it to read the scroll's description, the next box appears.

beats.headline: No valid target
beats.text: The cat is soaked in blood, but alive. Carl worriedly watches her health, waits ten frustrating seconds for the Winner! graphic to clear, and finds what he is looking for in his inventory: a scroll of Heal Critter. He reads it, but it doesn't work on her, and it evaporates from his menu with an error message. No Valid Target Available. You just wasted a valuable scroll, dumbass. He can't cast his heal spell on her either, so he pulls a healing potion instead.

beats.headline: Another off a kobold
beats.text: Carl had no Heal Critter scrolls left in the cage room, where the beaten dingoes got pet biscuits instead. Now the dingoes are gone, and he picks through the slagged, smoldering remains of the kobolds in the main room, looting a few spiked helmets and gold coins here and there. One of them has a scroll of Heal Critter and a handful of pet biscuits.

beats.headline: It fizzles
beats.text: The monster blocks magic, Carl tells Mordecai, and Mordecai answers that it likely means no spells, no scrolls. Mongo rushes into the kitchen screaming, bleeding from dozens of places where the other two clockwork Mongos exploded. Donut's heal spell has stopped working. She rushes to him, his health about halfway down, and glows as she tries a Heal Critter scroll. The spell fizzles out. His health is going back up on its own, Carl tells her; stop wasting scrolls, they won't work. Do you want some lemonade, Bonnie asks again.

relations.note: it does not work on her

tagline.text: The Toad Cudgel is the first weapon out of Carl's boxes, from a Bronze Weapon Box: a stick shaped like a three-quarter-length baseball bat by someone with only a vague idea of what baseball is.
Carl likes the Toad Cudgel better than the poker, but its rounded end bounces off a giant cockroach without doing much damage, and he has to bend awkwardly to use it.

description.text: Toad Cudgel. Big stick for bonking. Bonk toad. Bonk mob. Bonk girlfriend and drag back to cave by hair.

beats.headline: A stick, from a weapon box
beats.text: Carl's loot boxes open by tier, one after another. The third is a Bronze Weapon Box, and the label over its prize reads Toad Cudgel. The toad cudgel is a stick. It looks like a three-quarter-length baseball bat shaped by someone who only had a vague idea of what baseball was. The box after it is another weapon box, and the fireplace poker inside is not much better.

beats.headline: Big stick for bonking
beats.text: While the cat is still inside her blob, Carl looks over the rest of his loot and puts the fingerless gloves on. Of the two weapons he likes the feel of the cudgel more than the poker, which feels like it would bend and break the moment he hit something. The AI describes the cudgel in a caveman voice. He wonders whether the metal pot is still out there. It would be better than this.

beats.headline: Bounced off a roach
beats.text: Carl knows he does less damage this way than with his hands, but he does not want to fight a level-four brood guardian bare-handed, so he pulls the toad cudgel while Donut hits the roach with three magic missiles. When it charges again he swings the cudgel down at its head. The rounded edge bounces off, the bug hisses and falls back, and the hit doesn't appear to do much. He has to bend awkwardly to use it, too, and he switches to the poker to see if that is better.

tagline.text: The Tome of Magic Missile came out of Donut's silver adventurer box with a pile of pet biscuits, and she had taught herself the spell by the time Mordecai noticed. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it once.

beats.headline: Taught herself already
beats.text: Mordecai activates Donut's menus, and five boxes line up in front of her: three bronze ones with a couple of healing potions and torches, then a silver adventurer box holding a book and a pile of pet biscuits. The note over the book reads Tome of Magic Missile. The legendary box holds a single small, jeweled tiara. While Carl asks whether boxes are custom tailored, Donut glows a bright red. Ah, Princess Donut, says Mordecai, I see you taught yourself the Magic Missile spell already. Tomes permanently teach you the spell; scrolls just cast it once.

tagline.text: In the first safe room, a silver Adventurer Box gives Carl a silver ring worth a point of Constitution, which brings the stat up to ten.
A boss box has added a second ring of constitution, worth two points, which Carl wears on his left ring finger. His Constitution score comes up to twelve.

beats.headline: Silver box, silver ring
beats.text: In the first safe room, with a cup of cold, pure water at a booth, Carl spends several minutes sifting through his boxes. Potion, potion, torch, and bandages that stop Bleed effects, which are new. All the same stuff, except for a silver ring in the silver Adventurer Box he got for finding his first safe room. It gives him plus one to Constitution, bringing the stat up to ten. In the same sitting Donut's gold box gives her a little silver butterfly charm.

beats.headline: Another ring of constitution
beats.text: After the baby-killing achievements and the two Asshole Boxes, which put a tattoo on Carl's goddamned neck, the boss box gives him another ring of constitution, this one plus two. He puts it on his left ring finger, and his score comes up to twelve. The gold Looter Box beside it holds a single item, a skill potion.

beats.headline: Four rings at once
beats.text: Three dead crawlers lie together, and one of them, a human named Nica, still wears two rings, each plus two to strength. Donut can't wear them, so Carl rubs the blood off and puts them on himself beside his two constitution rings, which makes four rings in all. Just like that, his strength is back to an acceptable level. He takes no joy in looting fellow crawlers.

tagline.text: The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly is a little silver butterfly that jingles on Donut's collar. It makes her a better jumper and a little smarter, and winged fairies are no longer automatically hostile to her.

Donut has worn the butterfly charm since the first floor, but to order the guards of Point Mongo around she has to wear a settlement charm on her collar instead; the butterfly can go back on if fairy-class mobs turn up.

description.text: Talisman of the Slate Butterfly. Those who remember and commemorate the sad tale of the Slate Butterfly are given a boon by the fairies of the world. That story even made me cry. Adds +4 to the Light on Your Feet skill. Adds +1 to Intelligence. Winged fairies will no longer be automatically hostile toward you.

beats.headline: A bell for a cat
beats.text: Donut's gold magic item box, for being one of the first hundred crawlers to level Magic Missile to three, holds twenty-five mana potions and a collar charm: a little silver butterfly with a ring to attach it, which jingles when it moves. Donut squeaks with delight. Carl points out that people put bells on cats so the birds and squirrels can hear them coming. It's adorable, Donut says, and she is wearing it. With her Light on Your Feet raised from three to seven, she bounds to the top of the play area's plastic tubes and has the zoomies for ten minutes.

beats.headline: Plan Pied Piper
beats.text: The soccer-mom fairies who run the moonshine room are winged, so Donut can turn their dots white. She teleports in between the two of them, and they fall under her charm at once. Get back to work, one shouts at the clurichauns: this is a client, not an enemy. The other forty or so are not airborne fairies and stay red, so it is plan B, which Donut insists is called Plan Pied Piper. She walks the two fairies toward Carl, telling them about a horrible slaughter, and invites everyone to come and see.

beats.headline: One charm too many
beats.text: Donut likes her butterfly charm. Fairies like her, it is pretty, and it is part of her fit. She has had it since the first floor, it was instrumental against the first Krakaren, and it keeps her Light On Your Feet at ten. But the system only lets her wear so many magical items, and to order the guards of Point Mongo around she has to wear the new settlement charm with its tiny turquoise gem. Carl tells her she can always switch back if they come across some fairy-class mobs.

tagline.text: Goblin Dynamite is a red stick that sweats, so volatile that a loud noise might set it off without the wick. The System advises keeping it in inventory until it is wanted.
Goblin dynamite wears down as it is handled: every stick in Carl's pile reads out of fifty, and all of them are already at Detonation Imminent or Danger.
Pustule sells goblin dynamite by the case, twenty-five sticks for five hundred gold, beside hobgoblin sticks at twenty for two thousand.

description.text: Goblin Dynamite. This stuff is especially volatile. It’s so volatile, you probably don’t even need to light the wick to set it off. It’s so volatile, even loud noises might set it off. Keep it in your inventory until you’re ready to use it. Be gentle and don’t squeeze too hard or else you might get the… BOOM!

beats.headline: Sweating, then BOOM
beats.text: Carl has had five sticks since a silver goblin box. Outside a room that Donut says smells like hundreds of socks, she tells him to light a torch and throw it in. He has a better idea. The red stick is wet and sticky on the outside, as if it is sweating, and its description warns that even loud noises might set it off; the AI waits two full seconds before shouting the last word in his head. Carl lights the long wick with his Zippo, throws the stick into the room as hard as he can, and runs.

beats.headline: A few steps short
beats.text: It blows when it hits the ground, with Carl only a few steps from the door. The concussion sends him flying; he bounces and slides on the stone floor, the wooden door splinters, and a jagged hunk of it ricochets off his head. Stinking smoke pours through the entrance, blood seeps from a deep cut in his scalp, and a DANGER LOW HEALTH warning flashes red before it abates. The one throw earns him three explosives skills, a Silver Goblin Box for killing more than ten mobs with an explosive, a Gold Crowd Control Box for more than fifteen with the same attack, and an achievement for damaging a boss.

beats.headline: Loaded into a rat
beats.text: Running from Frank and Maggie, Carl tests an idea: a corpse's inventory takes items like a chest, and a lit smoke bomb stays lit inside a dead rat's grid. His goblin dynamite all reads out of fifty, every stick at Detonation Imminent or Danger, and the worst drops from ten to nine with his most careful handling. He adds that one unlit, lights one at thirteen and adds it too. If Frank loots the rat, it will literally blow up in his hands.

beats.headline: On the Maestro's show
beats.text: The Maestro's show plays the rest. Frank and Maggie were frozen in the safe room, and their teenaged daughter Yvette had been hiding under her mother's stealth field the whole time. At the rat, Maggie yells at Frank not to loot it. He does it anyway, and pulls out one item, the lit stick. He drops it in surprise and all three turn to run. The shrapnel takes Yvette down, and Frank too; a dislodged hunk of rock shears his hand right off. Carl understands that the girl's injuries were his doing.

beats.headline: Bounced back at him
beats.text: Giant zombies close in round an empty pool in the dark. Carl retracts the xistera, lights two sticks of goblin dynamite and throws one each way. The second rebounds off a shape at least twelve feet tall and rolls back toward him, hissing. He hops backward into the pool and lands on the rotting corpse of the Divider. Both sticks blow, killing most of the monsters and the last city elf, and the bloated corpse blows too, throwing him unconscious onto a roof across the street.

beats.headline: Ten sticks, one button
beats.text: The tenth and last stick of goblin dynamite goes on an exposed joist outside the building where the lich waits, fixed with a sticky detonator charge. One stick of hobgoblin pus allows up to ten simultaneous detonations with a single press. Carl hands Katia a pencil-like detonator and makes her keep it in her inventory: if they die, or if he says so, she presses the button. No questions.

relations.note: the rat-corpse trap

entities.name: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces
aka: Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces

tagline.text: Carl's kneepads slip on like knee bracers, made of skin and fur, with needle-thin spikes about eight inches long that pop out only when they are needed. They add ten percent Damage Reflect to all his equipped armour and cancel momentum-based attacks.

description.text: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces. Adds 10% Damage Reflect to all equipped armor. Cancels all Momentum-based attacks. Made of skin and fur and the spiky things from the back of Thorn Cadavers, these kneepads are both good protection and they’re stylish. Stylish, that is, if your knees are cosplaying as hedgehogs.

beats.headline: Something on his legs
beats.text: In a tutorial guild after the Hoarder, the last of Carl's boxes is a gold crowd control box: three scrolls, five Iron Skin potions, and the kneepads. They are the real prize. It isn't pants, but it is something on his legs. He pulls his feet through them like slip-on bracers; they look much too small and adjust themselves. The spikes are thin and needle-like, about eight inches each, and retract until they are needed. Donut asks Mordecai whether the dungeon has a worst-dressed award. Sort of, he says.

beats.headline: The slime kills itself
beats.text: Near the northern edge of the Hoarder's neighbourhood, Carl punches a level two green slime the size of a pig and sinks into it up to the elbow. His right fingerless glove dissolves off his hand and the right arm of his leather jacket melts away. The slime kills itself on his Damage Reflect. His arm comes out red, bubbling and screaming with pain.

beats.headline: Not enough knee
beats.text: Locked in close with Gore-Gore, the mantaur engineer, Carl is too tight to kick, so he knees him with a spiked kneepad. He can tell the power just isn't there, and he has to punch twice more to get clear. When Gore-Gore's three razors tear across Carl's face, the mantaur grunts in surprise as the damage reflection hits him.

beats.headline: Spikes for a ghoul
beats.text: The engine ploughs through a tunnel packed with ghouls, and pieces of them shower into the cab. Carl smashes a gnashing head with his fist and it explodes. Another chomps painfully onto his leg. He pushes it down, the kneepads activate, and the spikes kill it. The train whines and noticeably slows while Donut screams and slices with her claws.

beats.headline: Outside the kangaroo
beats.text: Carl shoves his arms into the stinking kangaroo costume and pulls its head over his own. There is a loud click and an achievement. His jacket stays on the inside, his cloak flaps round his neck, and his boxers and kneepads are now on the outside of the costume.

beats.headline: Tiny on a dachshund
beats.text: Elle is a goblin, Jacobus a starfish, and Carl a long-haired dachshund with a German accent and no thumbs. His boxers have resized themselves and sit awkwardly on his hips. Jacket, cloak and bandanna remain; none of his rings do, and the xistera and the gauntlet have unequipped themselves. The kneepads remain, tiny on his back legs.

tagline.text: A Neighborhood Map is the scrap of paper a neighborhood boss drops, persistent loot any crawler can take. Touched, it fills in about a square mile of the minimap, red dots and all.
A neighborhood map fills in the minimap round where it was dropped, and the one Carl looted from a dead goose shows him where a living boss sits as well.

beats.headline: A scrap of paper
beats.text: The Hoarder drops a single piece of loot, a scrap of paper called a Neighborhood Map. It doesn't disappear when Carl loots it, and Donut grabs one for herself. The moment he touches it, about a square mile of his minimap fills in: hardly any red dots now, several tutorial guilds, and at the edge of the square the large, pulsing X of a crawler's corpse, Rebecca W, level 3, killed less than two hundred metres from the safe room. All bosses drop persistent loot, Mordecai explains; a neighborhood boss drops a neighborhood map.

beats.headline: Inside the square
beats.text: Carl looks up at his map for blue dots and finds none, and works through what it can and cannot show him. Outside the area of the neighborhood map, red dots don't appear unless he is right on top of them, though NPCs always show within a couple of hundred metres. Could other crawlers hide from him? Another thing to worry about.

beats.headline: Donut picks it up
beats.text: Carl falls onto the corpse of the Divider as his dynamite blows, the corpse bursts, and he lands unconscious on a roof across the street. She grabs the neighborhood map, leaps out of the pool, finishes off the last three monsters with two magic missiles and Mongo, then leaps up to the roof and uses a heal scroll on Carl.

beats.headline: Where the boss sits
beats.text: Outside the town gates the Chariot goes together in four minutes, a four-chamber missile tube newly mounted beside Carl's swivel seat. Thanks to the neighborhood map they received from the dead goose, he can also see the boss's location: about half a mile east of town, settled atop a sand dune, a cyborg death bird recharging for the night. She's too close, he says: they need to go west, a mile and a half away.

tagline.text: A Potion of Iron Skin raises the drinker's physical armour by a hundred percent for five minutes. Carl has five, from a gold crowd control box.

beats.headline: Five in a gold box
beats.text: In a tutorial guild after the Hoarder, Carl opens his last three boxes. The gold crowd control box holds his kneepads, three scrolls, and five Potions of Iron Skin. Each raises his physical armour by a hundred percent for five minutes. The kneepads are the real prize; the potions go into his inventory.

beats.headline: The blast on his thigh
beats.text: Rot stickers swarm the walls and ceilings, little black raviolis that stick to you and explode like a sledgehammer. Donut is quick enough on Carl's shoulder that none have reached her, but just in case, he makes her drink one of his Iron Skin potions and drinks one himself. A rot sticker lands on his inner thigh and detonates before he can get it, and that time he does fall down. Without the potion, his leg might have been blown clear off. A well-timed missile from Donut saves him.

beats.headline: Drunk on the way out
beats.text: With Frank and Maggie able to go completely stealth, Carl and Donut jump out of the safe room and make for the closest main artery. Carl downs an Iron Skin potion and makes Donut drink one. The hallway is too thin and bumpy for the chopper, and one rot sticker blast could turn the bike into a bomb, so they run.

tagline.text: A Scroll of Confusing Fog fills a room with a mist that only the mobs can see. Carl has three, out of a gold crowd control box.
How long Confusing Fog lasts depends on the reader's intelligence. With Carl's intelligence of three it gave fifteen seconds; Donut reading the same scroll would get a hundred and twenty.

beats.headline: Gold crowd control box
beats.text: The gold crowd control box holds a pair of kneepads, three Scrolls of Confusing Fog and five Iron Skin potions. By its description the scroll fills the room with a mist that only the mobs can see, and the potion doubles Carl's physical armour for five minutes. The real prize is the kneepads. They aren't pants, but at least he has something to put on his legs.

beats.headline: Fog in the gym
beats.text: The Juicer twists at the waist and throws a weight at Carl's head, and it bursts into flames as it flies. Carl reads a scroll as the others descend on him. A thick, wet fog fills the room, blinding him for a moment before it fades to half opacity for him; water beads over everything and the ground turns slick. The troglodytes can't see a thing and run into each other and the scattered equipment. When it clears he reads a second. That one too lasts barely fifteen or twenty seconds, and with his ankle caught in a machine's wire he reads his last.

beats.headline: Wasted on a low intelligence
beats.text: Mordecai goes over the gym fight. Carl wasted those Confusing Fog scrolls. Next time, the party member with the highest intelligence should read any scrolls: with an intelligence of three, Carl made the fog last fifteen seconds, and Princess Donut's intelligence would have made it last a hundred and twenty seconds per scroll. Damn, says Carl.

beats.headline: Fog in the hallway
beats.text: In a hallway, a monster is finishing forming, the last of a black and purple mist twirling round it, and Yolanda is standing over a fallen man. Fog, Carl yells. Donut has read his mind and activates her scroll of Confusing Fog at the same moment. The wall of fog billows into the hallway as the creature drops to all six legs. It spins toward them, impossibly fast, cleaving through the cloud like a boat cutting through waves.

beats.headline: Six lions and a shell
beats.text: All six Mold Lions pounce at once in a dark street. Carl slams down Protective Shell, and on his word Donut casts the last scroll of Confusing Fog. A goblin smoke bomb he threw earlier caught the wind and came to nothing; the fog has no such problem. The lions bounce off the shell like fireflies off a bug zapper and ricochet away howling into the spreading fog. The shell lasts twenty seconds. Thanks to Donut's high intelligence, the fog stays a good two and a half minutes.

beats.headline: Three more, at last
beats.text: Two silver quest boxes each hold a thousand gold coins and a set of scrolls. One contains three Confusing Fog scrolls, which Carl likes much better than smoke bombs: the scrolls have saved them multiple times, and he has been out of them for a while. The other holds three Heal scrolls, for healing others without pouring potions down their throats.

tagline.text: The Tome of Wisp Armor comes out of Carl's boss box, a magic protection spell he cannot cast yet on three mana. Mordecai calls it quite valuable and says to hold onto it, or give it to the princess, who wants it before she knows what it is.
Carl has read the Tome of Wisp Armor rather than sell it. The spell wraps him in tendrils of light that turn aside most magic damage and, for a few minutes, anything trying to take over his mind.

description.text: Wisp Armor. Cost: 5 Mana. Target: Self Only. Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell. Requires 5 minute cooldown. Surrounds your body with tendrils of light. While ineffective against physical attacks, this spell negates 75% of incoming damage from magic-based attacks. Provides temporary immunity to mind-control effects. Higher skill levels increase both effectiveness and duration. It also makes you look all wispy and ethereal and druid-like. A great spell to have if you're a club kid or trying to bang a vegan.

beats.headline: Five mana, and he has three
beats.text: Carl's Bronze Boss Box, fifth of seven, gives him a Tome of Wisp Armor. It's a good find, Mordecai says, but it costs five mana to cast and Carl has three. Hold onto it until you decide what your build is going to be; it's quite valuable. Or give it to the princess. I'll take it, says Donut, who doesn't even know what it is yet. Carl reads the spell's description. A magic protection spell. That would be useful. He holds onto it for now.

beats.headline: Top of the list
beats.text: A Skill Potion from Carl's gold Looter Box adds a level to Determine Value. It does not tell him what anything is worth, but it lets him sort his inventory by value, and he does. The first item on the list is the Tome of Wisp Armor. The second is the Chopper. The list leaves out what he has equipped; he suspects his troll skin shirt would top it otherwise.

beats.headline: Enough intelligence, not yet
beats.text: With his stats settled, Carl has given himself enough Intelligence to read the Wisp Armor spellbook, and he doesn't do it quite yet. He is still on the fence about using it himself, giving it to Donut or selling it, and he wants to see what its actual monetary value is first.

beats.headline: Read on the way to an ogre
beats.text: Carl has held the tome to sell. Donut asks for it about once a day, and he has nearly relented, but he is meant to be the party's tank. Now there is no time to wait. Walking down the bleachers toward Apollon, the ice-cream-selling strongman, he activates the tome, puts Wisp Armor on his hotlist and drinks a mana regen potion to reach five points. Apollon hands him a cone of worms, compliments of Grimaldi. Carl casts the spell, sparkling lights twirling round him like comets, and swallows. When the parasite pulls at his mind, the armor leaves him his own for the next five minutes.

tagline.text: The Torch tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she applies it before Carl has time to read the description. It teaches her Torch, a curl of light that follows her around and grows stronger with use, and she thinks it is a stupid spell.

beats.headline: A stupid spell, apparently
beats.text: A spell book, Donut cries, opening her Bronze Boss Box, and she glows before Carl has time to read the description: she has already applied it. Then she cries out with rage. Mordecai, amused, tells the little one she really must examine these items before she equips or applies them. It's a stupid spell, Donut says. It's a very useful spell, says Mordecai, and tells Carl what it is: Torch. It makes a curl of light follow her around, and the more she uses it, the more powerful it gets. Carl agrees it's a good spell.

entities.name: Desperado Pass
entities.role: The tattoo that opens the Desperado Club

tagline.text: The Desperado Pass is a tattoo out of an Asshole's Box that brands itself on: a gold splotch glowing through the fur over Donut's right shoulder blade, and a dagger dripping blood on Carl's neck. It grants access to the Desperado Club and rules out a Vanquisher pass.
The Desperado Pass also precludes several classes for Carl and Donut, among them the Cleric and Paladin classes.
The Desperado Pass is what gets Carl and Donut past Clarabelle and into the members-only room of the Desperado Club.
Katia has a Desperado Pass now as well, a dagger tattoo that formed on her neck out of a loot box.

description.text: Desperado Pass. Great. Now you’re running with the type of kids who sit in the back of the bus. What would your mother say? This pass allows access to the Desperado Club. Warning: Holding a Desperado Pass negates the ability to obtain a Vanquisher pass.

beats.headline: Branded through the fur
beats.text: Achievements for killing an infant and more than twenty non-combatants pay out in Asshole's Boxes. Donut opens hers first. One holds a tattoo like the goblin pass Carl got earlier, and it brands itself over her right shoulder blade, a gold-coloured splotch glowing through her fur. She is enraged: a disqualifying mark, she is damaged. Carl touches it to read it. Desperado Pass, access to the Desperado Club, and a warning that it negates a Vanquisher pass. That is all it says. His own boxes hold the exact same items, though his tattoo appears on his neck, where he can't see it, burning as it goes on. Donut, examining it close, says it is a dagger dripping blood. Ghastly, she says.

beats.headline: Members of the club
beats.text: The description of the moonshine jugs says they are valuable, and Donut points at the dagger tattoo on Carl's neck. The Desperado Club, she says: maybe it will be on the next floor. She bets they will buy all the jugs because they are members of the club. They will be rich. Maybe, says Carl, if they have any jugs left when they are done.

beats.headline: Off limits
beats.text: Carl asks Mordecai about the tattoo on his neck, the Desperado Club. Nope, says Mordecai. Off limits. They will learn about the third floors soon enough. Sorry. Then he tells Carl he had better open his boxes before Zev gets here, because the cameras always turn off when kua-tin are around.

beats.headline: Fewer classes
beats.text: Picking Donut's class, Mordecai finds her list of 34 the shortest he has ever seen. It is a combination of four things, he works out: her racial choice, her stats, the Desperado pass they both have, which precludes several of the classes right off the bat, and the tiara on her head, which narrows it even further. There are still a few great choices on there, he says.

beats.headline: No clerics, no paladins
beats.text: Carl picks Primal, and his list of classes runs to over 650 choices. He would have even more without that tattoo on his neck, Mordecai says. The Desperado Club does not allow goody-two-shoes sorts, so there are no Cleric classes and no Paladin classes, along with a few monk classes, which is unfortunate, as they would have been worth a look.

beats.headline: Past Clarabelle
beats.text: The first room of the club's pub is open to any local, Mordecai says; you need no pass, and crawlers without one can pick up quests there to win themselves a tattoo. Past a red, glittering door, Clarabelle the crocodilian sits in front of the second. I see you two both have a pass, she says: the bar and dance floor are open, the casino isn't ready yet. Inside, Donut asks Mordecai whether he has a tattoo too. He had a pass early on, he says. They know him here now.

beats.headline: Something bad, and a tattoo
beats.text: Donut wants alcohol and dancing. Katia reminds them she has no pass to the club; she has told them several times. You need to do something bad and get a tattoo, says Donut. What did they do to get access, Katia asks. It doesn't matter, says Carl, cutting in: they received it after the incident with the goblin babies. Better she tries for the other club, Club Vanquisher, he says, though he does not know what it takes.

beats.headline: A dagger on Katia
beats.text: Katia receives ten loot boxes, and after showers they gather to watch her open them. She opens the first and looks at Carl, grinning. Sorry, Carl, she says, as the dagger tattoo forms on her neck. I know you wanted to get me into Club Vanquisher. Donut, poofed out, washed and smelling of lilacs, realizes what has just happened. Oh my god, yay. We can go dancing now.

relations.note: both are pass tattoos

entities.name: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet
aka: Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet

tagline.text: The Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet is Donut's first armour: silver fae-steel scale draped over her back half like a skirt, with a slot for her tail and two points of Dexterity. Not the best protection, its description admits, but it makes her backside look oh so pretty.
Donut's old crupper has made way for a chain mail one, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Its two points of Dexterity were great on the first floor and are laughably weak now.

description.text: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet. Boy is that a fucking mouthful. By the gods. +2 to Dexterity. Light and flexible, this scale armor is made from Fae Steel. While not as strong as Elven mail or even good Orcish steel, it's the strongest alloy that fairy folk can wear. It's not the best protection, but it'll make your ass look oh so pretty.

beats.headline: Her first piece of armour
beats.text: Donut's boss box holds her first piece of armour. After several minutes of fury over the tattoo on her back, she moves on, and with a pop silver scale appears draped over the back half of her body, reaching about halfway to the floor: like a skirt, almost, open under her stomach, with a slot especially for her tail. She turns in circles trying to look at it. How does it look? Does it cover the tattoo? It doesn't, Carl tells her, not even close, but it looks great.

beats.headline: Lifted for a tattoo
beats.text: Edgar has to tattoo Donut, quickly, and the best place is her right flank, over a patch about as big as his foot. Someone lift her camouflage suit and crupper for me, he says. Donut agrees only if Carl gets a matching one, and then the ghillie suit disappears, and the crupper. She turns her tail to Rosetta and refuses Carl's idea of a tramp stamp. Rosetta goes to work with scissors and then a razor, while Donut asks Edgar whether it could be a flower.

beats.headline: Retired for chain mail
beats.text: A box has given Donut a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Her old one, the Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, has been on her backside since the goblin-baby incident on the very first floor, and its plus two to dexterity was great at the time and is laughably weak now. She removes the old mail, briefly showing the shaved patch with its tattoo of a dog licking itself, and the new armour appears. It's much lighter, she says. More elegant.

relations.note: together they make her jingle when she walks

tagline.text: A Sapper's Table is a workbench sold in safe room stores, and Carl's new Demolitions Workshop menu will not open unless he is standing in front of one.

Carl has a Sapper's Table of his own now, out of a Gold Sapper's Box: a crafting table like his engineering and alchemy tables, where the explosives and traps he makes don't lose stability or go off early.
Carl's Sapper's Table stands in his crafting space, where he expects to spend most of his time, and he spends two upgrade coupons to take it to level three.
At level five, Carl's sapper's table is still better for building explosives from scratch than the bench in his new bomber's studio.

beats.headline: A menu that needs a table
beats.text: Carl's explosives skills have reached five, and he has a new one, IED, at level three. An entire new menu appears in his interface, titled Demolitions Workshop. He clicks on it and receives an error: he may only access this menu when he is standing in front of a Sapper's Table, a workbench he may purchase from a Safe Room store. Interesting. That is something to explore if they ever make it that far.

beats.headline: It nearly knocks him over
beats.text: Carl's trap achievement pays out a Gold Sapper's Box with two items in it. The first is a Sapper's table that practically knocks him over when it appears, a table just like his engineering and alchemy tables. Its description says explosives and traps created at it don't lose stability and can't be prematurely set off. The second item is ten proximity triggers, which only attach to a trap at a Sapper's Table.

beats.headline: Against one wall
beats.text: In the crafting space, Carl shoves the alchemy table against a wall, and it clicks loudly into place with upgrade menus over it; he loads it with every alchemy item he owns. Then the sapper's table goes against one wall and his engineering table against the other. He expects to spend most of his time at the sapper table, but for now he stands at the engineering one, laying out the Goo-inator 3000, the Gorgon Marital Aid and a dozen slightly-too-small goblin tools.

beats.headline: Level three
beats.text: At the saferoom in station 281, inside a glass-fronted donut shop, Carl asks the bopca, Nodd, for a black coffee and the crafting table menu. It is a long list, most of it useless, at about 25,000 gold a table. He slides one of his two free table coupons across for the one he has been looking for. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether this is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three. A note in the cookbook has already told him what a level-three table does: it lets you infuse bombs.

beats.headline: A copy, less scorched
beats.text: Carl's training room can teach him his workshop tables as well, and they need only be installed in his crafting studio. He finds Sapper's Table on the list and clicks it. A familiar level-five table pops up out of the ground, identical to his own, though less scorched, and his hand doesn't come away sticky with the residue the hobgoblin disco ball left. Instead of the usual multi-armed trainer, a badger with an eyepatch and a hook for a hand fades in, decides Carl is practically ready to teach him, and tells him the weapon he wants needs a different table altogether.

tagline.text: The Tome of Minion Army comes to Donut in a Beguiler Box. Its spell makes hostile enemies fight for her, but it costs fifty spell points, she has twenty-four, and the book will not let her read it.

Donut has read the Tome of Minion Army. The spell takes five minutes to cast and roots her in place while it does, and at level one each intelligent mob in its circle has a two percent chance to turn on its friends.
Donut has cast Minion Army at last, rooted for four minutes, and the demon birds caught low in its circle turned on each other.

beats.headline: Twenty-six points short
beats.text: Donut's Beguiler Box holds a tome called Minion Army. Its spell costs fifty spell points to cast and makes hostile enemies fight for you instead of against you. A great spell, but Donut currently has twenty-four points. She tries reading it anyway and it won't let her: apparently you can't teach yourself spells you can't cast. She pouts for a good minute straight. Don't worry, Carl says. They will trade it for something better, or keep it until she can use it.

beats.headline: Read at fifty-two
beats.text: Carl wakes from a nap to Donut's discovery. Her Intelligence is forty, her butterfly charm and new tiara add four, and the Good Rest and shower buffs add twenty percent to her base, which a bug keeps off the stat list but not off her spell points. Fifty-two. Of course she has read the tome already. The spell is simple on the surface and convoluted underneath: five minutes to cast, stuck in place while casting, a five-hour cooldown, intelligent mobs only, and at level one a two percent chance for each to turn on its friends.

beats.headline: Not the same as Conscript
beats.text: Doctor Bones is honing a spell whose effect on weak subjects lasts pretty much forever. Carl asks its name: Donut has one similar, called Minion Army, that she hasn't tried yet. Minion Army is a battlefield sabotage spell, quite effective, says Doctor Bones, but it has a long casting time and it is temporary. His is simply called Conscript. Carl feels a sudden revulsion. He has read about that spell, used a lot against crawlers on the ninth floor.

beats.headline: Rooted for four minutes
beats.text: Donut glows as she casts Minion Army for the first time. She has held it back since the first floor because it roots her in place, for four minutes now, and with Imani and Samantha enhancing it the two percent should be about five. A countdown appears over her, Rooted in Place, and the sluggalos charge the demons early. When the ice and the corpses settle she thinks she cast it for nothing, until the experience starts coming in: birds in the lower part of the tornado over the building are fighting each other.

tagline.text: Agatha leans on a shopping cart heaped with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow in its head among them. Her spray paint lives in it, in a blue IKEA bag, and she insists the paint is hers.

Carl's inventory history still lists everything that was in Agatha's cart while he held it: blankets, clothes, IKEA bags, spray paint, and three pieces of Valtay Corporation technology that sort to the very top by value.

Agatha already had this cart on Earth before the collapse. With the countdown running, she took her supplies out of her dimensional space, put them in the IKEA bag and shoved it to the bottom of the cart. Carl's inventory history still lists the three Valtay devices it carried.

beats.headline: A cart full of blankets
beats.text: Carl and Donut find the Meadow Lark party, and among them is an old woman wrapped head to toe in scarves under a red checkered trapper hat, leaning on a shopping cart filled to the brim with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow stuck in its head among them. Carl wonders how anyone got the wheelchairs and the cart down here. Agatha pulls a blue IKEA bag from the cart and sprays a smiley face on the wall. When Brandon tells her not to waste the paint, she says it is hers, and that he stole it from her.

beats.headline: Into Carl's inventory
beats.text: The borough boss is a rolling ball of tusklings, and it rushes past right where the party was standing, missing Agatha and her cart by inches while she cackles with joy. Carl orders her to sit down in the middle and not move, grabs the heavy cart from both sides, lifts it into the air and spends a few precious seconds putting it into his inventory. Thief, she cries. Thief. Yolanda promises he will give it back. Squeezed in with the six of them, Agatha goes on wailing about her damn shopping cart.

beats.headline: Given back, with suspicion
beats.text: The fight over, Agatha shuffles up to Carl shaking her fist, half her head caked in blood, and demands it back. He pulls the cart into existence a foot off the ground and it crashes down. She clutches an IKEA bag off the top and peers inside as if he might have stolen something, and pokes suspiciously at the flamingo. She could keep all of it in her own inventory, Carl points out. She hasn't gone through the tutorial, Yolanda says. She doesn't have an inventory yet.

beats.headline: Bully and a Thief
beats.text: Among the achievements after the borough boss fight, one confuses Carl for a moment. Bully and a Thief: he has stolen property from a fellow crawler who is a lower level than him. What's next, tough guy, the System asks, kicking puppies? The reward is a Bronze Asshole's Box. Then he realises he got it for taking Agatha's shopping cart.

beats.headline: Three items in the history
beats.text: Carl's inventory has grown a History tab. Sorted by value, its top three entries are things he has never seen: a Trans Tunnel 7C Orator Relay by Valtay Corp., a Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition and a Mag 3040 Valtay Corp Pulse Pistol. The relay is a communication device, and illegal. Then Donut sees a blue dot coming, and he knows where they came from: Agatha's cart, all of it, held in his inventory through the boss fight. She wheels it in, squeaking, and calls him a cart thief. He offers to fix the wheel. No need to fix her squeak, she says.

beats.headline: Still squeaking, still pushing
beats.text: Carl moves to step down the stairs, and they suddenly turn into a ramp. A familiar crawler is pushing a squeaking shopping cart toward them: Agatha, level eight now, still human, still without a class, with the pink flamingo standing at the front of the cart. I see you lot are still kicking, she cackles. The whole group watches open-mouthed as she heads for the stairwell. Imani moves to intercept her, and Carl holds out a hand to stop her. Don't, he warns.

beats.headline: The bottom of the cart
beats.text: A countdown reaches every asset: commencement, Earth System initialization, edifice collapse, and this is not a drill. Agent number 22, also known as Agatha, shakes her head and reads it again. The night is freezing, and she has put her failing human shell into torpor against the cold. She takes her supplies out of her dimensional space, pulls herself to her feet with old, shaking hands, places the items in the IKEA bag and shoves it to the bottom of her shopping cart. The collapse is under two Earth hours away. She has been here almost ten Earth years, waiting.

relations.note: in his inventory through the borough boss fight
three Valtay devices among its contents

tagline.text: A bracelet out of a silver Adventurer box adds two points to Donut's Dexterity, bringing it to twelve. It wraps snugly round her front leg.
Donut wears bracelets on all four legs now, and the plus-two Dexterity one is on a back leg.

beats.headline: Finally, melee damage
beats.text: Donut hisses with rage at the piles of torches that keep appearing in front of her; most of her haul is the same old crap. One exception is a bracelet from a Silver Adventurer box she received for finally dealing melee damage. It adds two to her dexterity, bringing it to twelve, and when she equips it, it wraps snugly round her front leg. A Silver Survivor's Box gives her a dozen Heal scrolls as well.

beats.headline: Room for an anklet
beats.text: Carl has pried a wooden anklet off a dead tree woman, and he wants to see if the game will let Donut wear it. He suspects it will: she already has one bracelet wrapped round her forward leg, though he can barely see it through all the fur. Donut looks at the anklet with distaste. Wood?

beats.headline: All four legs
beats.text: Donut's gold box pops out a sparkling silver bracelet with little purple gems, and she equips it at once. The obsidian bracelet that lets her cast Fireball moves to her right foreleg and the new one goes on the left. The fallen oak anklet stays tucked on one back leg and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the other. With bracelets on all four legs, she can't add any more. Doesn't it look divine?

tagline.text: The Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust are a hundred small, low-damage black throwing stars. Every monster hurt by one makes the set hit that monster type eight percent harder, compounded, but the stars are very fragile.
A star that takes a single chip loses its red enchantment. Fifty of Carl's shuriken became the spikes on the front of the redoubt for the borough boss, and only about twenty of those stayed unbroken.

description.text: Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust (x100) Small, low-damage throwing stars. These bad boys aren't anything special upon first glance. They're the same black stars you wannabe ninjas purchased at the knife shop and the swap meet when you were kids. The same throwing stars you'd drill into the drywall of your room until your mom caught you and took them away. And while these shuriken don't have the ability to turn you into a ninja, nor do they have the capacity to make your mom stop drinking, they are enchanted with a Bloodlust enhancement. For every monster you damage with a shuriken from this set, the damage against that monster type rises by 8%.

beats.headline: A pile of ninja stars
beats.text: The boss box holds a pile of ninja stars, a hundred of them, the same black stars every wannabe ninja once drilled into his bedroom drywall. They are enchanted with Bloodlust: for every monster damaged with one, the damage against that monster type rises by eight percent. Carl asks Mordecai whether that means eight percent of the original amount or eight percent compounded, because that is a big deal after a while. Huh, says Mordecai, and checks. Good news: it is compounded. The bad news is that the stars are very fragile. Carl suspects it is not that great an enchantment, with only a hundred of them to throw and collect.

beats.headline: Spikes on the redoubt
beats.text: Brandon reads the description and is awed: compounding damage means poke something two hundred times and it's literally millions of points. So he, Chris and Carl spend a good five minutes throwing fifty of the stars deep into the pitted wooden cover of the redoubt's front table, black spikes to pierce the boss each time it hits. Only about twenty stay unbroken. In the fight the star-covered tabletop lies broken, and a tuskling rolls onto the stars still glowing red, squealing, so Carl stamps it deeper into the wood. Its health drops slowly, then plummets as the exponential bonus kicks in.

beats.headline: Every star salvaged
beats.text: Imani drops a find on the floor in disgust, and Donut hops over and takes it into her own inventory. Everything, right? she asks, and Carl nods. He salvages all the ninja stars he can find and all the remaining pieces of the redoubt, and his inventory grows a new tab labelled Worthless Garbage. Then he spends a few minutes quietly looking round the arena for the remains of the party that went before them.

entities.name: Heal scroll
entities.role: A heal for whoever it is read on

tagline.text: A Heal scroll heals whoever it is read on, and there is no countdown between one scroll and the next, as there is with potions. Donut won a dozen from a Silver Survivor's Box, and Carl's bronze one brought five more.
A Heal scroll works on Donut, but read on Mongo it does nothing.

beats.headline: A dozen for nearly dying
beats.text: After the boss fight, Donut's boxes are mostly the same old crap, with a couple of exceptions. A Silver Survivor's Box, awarded for ending a boss battle with less than five percent of her health, gives her a dozen Heal scrolls. They are good to have: there is no countdown between reading one and the next, and even better, they can use them on each other. Those twelve are good, Mordecai says, and he suspects they are about to get a few more. Carl's own Bronze Survivor's Box, for having less than ten percent health when the boss died, brings five more, seventeen in all.

beats.headline: Not on Mongo
beats.text: Street urchins are attacking Mongo and Donut because of the wood and metal Carl stacked round the cat, and Donut is getting skewered. Carl reads a Heal scroll, one of those from the Survivor's Box, focusing on her. She glows, and the spikes squeeze out of her body and scatter on the floor like pine needles. He tries a second on Mongo, and it doesn't work. He can't use a potion on the pet either. Hang in there, buddy.

beats.headline: Onto the roof
beats.text: The Divider's corpse blows and throws Carl onto a roof across the street. Donut grabs the neighborhood map, leaps out of the pool and finishes off the last three monsters, two with magic missiles and the third with Mongo. Then she leaps to the roof where Carl landed and uses a heal scroll to bring his health back up. He stays unconscious for another three minutes despite being healed, and wakes staring at the sky, a level higher.

beats.headline: Topping off Katia
beats.text: Carl has eight scrolls of healing ready and Donut another six when the train runs into the ghouls. Gore blasts into the engine like a firehose, and Katia, who has been fine, is suddenly unconscious at half health and dropping: something is shocking her. Where the hell is that healer? Carl casts his heal scroll on Katia and her health returns to the top, though she stays unconscious and it keeps dropping. At ten percent he slams another to top her off, and when her health keeps dwindling with no debuff showing, he reads another, then another. He will soon be out.

beats.headline: One of the precious ones
beats.text: A rocket blows everything back across the room. Louis is screaming, burned and full of shrapnel. Firas has been blown across the room and is unconscious, but otherwise looks okay. Donut, astride Mongo, both unharmed at the back of the room, goes to Firas and uses one of their precious healing scrolls on him. Carl drops one of his last hobgoblin smoke curtains at his feet. Let's get out of here.

beats.headline: Misfire, then up
beats.text: Everything unfreezes after the goddess's visit, and beside Carl, Donut has gone rigid, unable to move, her health draining slowly, her title changed from Warlord to Champion. He tries to apply a healing scroll at once, but it misfires, and he has to wait. Outside, the ball has broken apart and thousands of bodies are flying up toward them. When Donut coughs, he slams on the healing scroll, and her health starts to rocket up.

beats.headline: Healing Chaco
beats.text: The parade passes Lamashtu the donkey with Grigori standing on her, and Carl meets the psychotic AI's eyes. Chaco is at Grigori's feet, his health still in the red. Never taking his eyes off Grigori's, Carl pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco and heals him. Grigori's eyes never leave his own, and he does not react. Then Carl points at the effigy of the Unwashed and speaks to the galaxy.

relations.note: it does not work on him
no countdown between scrolls, where potions have one

tagline.text: The Puddle Jumper tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she reads it before Carl can ask what it is. It teaches her Puddle Jumper, which teleports her and up to three others anywhere in her line of sight, for 20 mana, on a ten-second delay and a five-hour cooldown.

beats.headline: Read before the description
beats.text: Donut's Bronze Boss Box has given her yet another spell book, and she hasn't read it yet. She announces she was born a cat and will die a cat, and that Carl must choose a cat race too; when he says he is sticking with human, she does her approximation of a shrug and glows as she reads the tome. Did she at least read the description? Mordecai nods. Puddle Jumper, a good one: herself and up to three others, anywhere in her line of sight, further at higher levels, almost as good as Teleport at level 15. Twenty mana, a ten-second delay, a five-hour cooldown.

beats.headline: A wet pop between fairies
beats.text: The two biggest problems with Puddle Jumper are the cooldown and the mana. Once Donut is in that room she cannot teleport out for five hours, and the spell costs 20 of her 26 points. Carl stays behind; with his extra fairy aggro, nobody knows what would happen if they both showed themselves. Donut casts it, fades through the ten-second countdown and vanishes with a loud, wet pop, reappearing at the far end of the room right between the two laminak fairies as the clurichauns jump to their feet.

tagline.text: The Speedbump is Brandon's name for the portable fortress he, his brother and Carl built from goblin tables and gym equipment: angled, four feet high, drilled to go up in less than twenty seconds and come together in twenty more, and meant to wedge a rolling boss against the ceiling.
What survives of the Speedbump travels in pieces in Carl's inventory, and an angled section that is still intact serves him as a shield in a boss fight.

beats.headline: Almost five hours of building
beats.text: Brandon and his brother Chris are the facility's maintenance guys. Carl describes his idea, spreads out the looted goblin tools, and they go straight to work. It takes almost five hours to build the pieces of a portable, modular fortress: workshop tables on new legs from the weight equipment, weight benches bolted on like shutters, a roof of weight-rack cross bars, barbell poles to brace it. Brandon calls it the Speedbump. They practise until the main structure goes up in less than twenty seconds and the rest in twenty more. Fifty of Carl's shuriken go into the front table's wooden covering as spikes; only about twenty stay unbroken.

beats.headline: Wedged under the ball
beats.text: On a fifteen-foot square of floor with no grooves, they build it in the order they practised while Agatha wails about her shopping cart, which Carl has just put into his inventory. With her inside, there is no room for the final, centre pole. The ball hits. The structure slides with a horrifying screech, all four ceiling braces pop out, and one throws Yolanda over. The ball is wedged between the roof and the tunnel, the roof sagging. They stab up through the lattice until, as the top collapses, the boss bursts like a balloon and tuxedoed tusklings rain down on them.

beats.headline: Edited out from under it
beats.text: The recap episode shows them huddled underneath the redoubt as Donut screams that it's coming. Brandon's older brother, Chris, speaks up, only the second time Carl has heard him, and says there is more to it. Agatha was edited out of the scene. She was next to him under the speedbump, but she wasn't there when they showed it. Oh yeah, says Brandon. Weird.

beats.headline: A shield in the corner
beats.text: Krakaren's tentacles are smashing through the walls and Carl is buzzed on his own smoothie. Running for the back corner of the room with Donut, he pulls an angled, still-intact section of the redoubt from his inventory and puts it up as a shield; the clurichauns' slingshot rocks ping off the steel table, and a screaming tentacle slams it and rockets them both against the back wall. When he has sent a zombie off toward the door with a lit jug, he dives behind it again and pulls the alchemy table over the top to make a clamshell.

beats.headline: A pyramid round the cat
beats.text: Donut will not wake, and Signet says she will remain where she is. When Carl lifts her anyway, a health bar appears and starts falling, and Signet tells him a water lily must not be removed, lest it die; he puts her back. Before he goes, he pulls the last of the redoubt pieces from his inventory, wood and metal, and erects an ugly, quick and dirty pyramid around the cat's chair. It won't protect her from a determined mob, but it is better than nothing. Mongo jumps to the top of it and looks down through the jagged hole.

relations.note: fifty thrown into the front table as spikes

tagline.text: A Borough Field Guide is looted from a dead borough boss, and Donut gets one of her own. It outlines the quadrants of the map round it, and hovering over one gives the levels and types of the mobs inside, though only for a limited area.
The field guide from the bowl's borough boss shows the level and description of every mob in the area, and it covers the entire bowl.

description.text: Borough Field Guide. Ahh, look at you. The intrepid explorer. Alone. Lost. Afraid. But there is no reason to be frightened. Not today, not now. Not when the trusty field guide has added monster types to this area of the map. Now when you gaze upon the unknown, that fear is somewhat lessened. Instead of delving into the strange, mysterious dark, being devoured by an unseen horror, you will now know exactly what it is as it chews upon your tasty innards.

beats.headline: An Attenborough whisper
beats.text: The crushed tusklings lie everywhere, and Carl reaches down to loot the persistent item from the boss's corpse; Donut already has hers. The AI reads its description in a whispery David Attenborough impression: Borough Field Guide. Carl zooms his minimap out, and the quadrants round the arena are outlined now. Hovering over one to the far southeast, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5. Axebeak. Useful, but like the neighborhood map the area is limited, and one has to reach the center and kill the boss to get it.

beats.headline: Map, guide, stars
beats.text: In the middle of the enormous pile of dead mimic, a single object appears on the map. Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map, borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to both the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl already knows what this one will be. It is the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.

beats.headline: The whole bowl
beats.text: The party has taken the field guide from the borough boss corpse. Now they can see the level and description of every mob in the area, and the guide covers the entire bowl. Right now, in the dark, it shows fist-sized monsters called Night Frights emerging from the sand dunes everywhere, mobs that run at their prey, attach themselves and explode, like the rot stickers of the first floor.

entities.name: Cheat Code Potion
entities.role: A skill boost that will not keep

tagline.text: A Cheat Code Potion raises one recently-used combat or magic skill by three, chosen at random and permanent. It expires shortly after it is generated, so it has to be drunk on the spot.

description.text: Cheat Code Potion Warning: This item has a short shelf life. This item will expire shortly after it was generated. In other words, this isn't something you can hoard. Don't be a wuss. Drink it now. Causes one, recently-used combat or magic-themed skill to increase by three. Choice is random and permanent.

beats.headline: Seventeen minutes to drink it
beats.text: The silver boss box holds a hundred gold coins and a potion with a red timer flashing at the bottom of its description, already down to seventeen minutes. Cheat Code Potion: don't be a wuss, drink it now. Carl adds it to his hotlist and drinks, and it crackles in his mouth like a whole packet of Pop Rocks. His Pugilism goes up by three, to level ten. With Iron Punch, Powerful Strike and his unarmed bonus, his fists now pack as much damage as Brandon's lightning maul.

beats.headline: Already at ten
