beats.text: Among the classes on offer, Prizefighter adds three to Pugilism, which would be a huge bonus, Carl thinks, considering the Cheat Code potion has already taken the skill to ten. He would pick the class in a second if he thought he could just punch his way through the dungeon. He knows already that he can't.

beats.headline: Precious, and perishable
beats.text: Why is Pawna's Tears so valuable, Katia wants to know, when they have seen skill potions, potions that max a skill out, and Cheat Code potions that give three levels? Because it is plus five to any skill he chooses, Mordecai answers. Legendary potions that max a skill exist only for a few skills. The Cheat Code is also precious, plus three to a random skill. However, it has a short shelf life, so it has to be taken immediately.

entities.name: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph

tagline.text: The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph is a little zippered folder of twelve tools. Used nightly in a safe room, it gives Carl's bare feet extra damage, three levels of Smush, bones that will not break and a five-second warning before any trap set off by a footfall, all for thirty hours.

description.text: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. This kit contains 12 essential items for proper foot care. The magical enhancements of this item may only be imbued within a Safe or Personal Space. Warning: All of these enhancements require you to remain barefoot. Why? Because you know why. From a pumice stone to a cuticle pusher, this personal hygiene kit will keep your feet both luscious and in perfect fighting shape. Nightly care of your feet and toenails will result in the following bonuses: +15% Damage to bare-foot attacks for 30 hours. +3 to the Smush skill for 30 hours. +Unbreakable buff (feet only) for 30 hours. This buff keeps your pretty little metatarsals nice and unbroken. …

beats.headline: One last item
beats.text: Carl has one last item to examine from the haul, and he swears under his breath before he has even pulled it into his hand: a little black folder with a zipper, full of miniature tools. Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph, twelve essential items for proper foot care, working only in a safe room or personal space and only while he stays barefoot. He sighs. The very last buff, an alarm and a five-second delay before any trap set off by a footfall, is a great prize.

beats.headline: Imani shows him how
beats.text: Little sharp rocks are everywhere. Carl kicks one away, and below him his shiny toes glitter. He had tried to get Donut to show him how to use the kit, and she laughed at him. It was Imani, of all people, who sat down with him, pulling the tools out one at a time and matter-of-factly explaining how they worked. The buffs activate after about fifteen minutes of work. He doesn't need to use every tool. He just has to make a show of it.

beats.headline: Saved by a pedicure
beats.text: Carl wakes in the hallway, healed by one of Donut's healing scrolls, his one-armed jacket scorched to hell. His toes sparkle. He thinks he was saved by that damn pedicure kit. The table should have severed his feet right at the ankles. Instead it bounced off and broke his legs, and without that, he would have bled out.

beats.headline: The buffs ran out
beats.text: On the red line, a level-six baby chomps onto Carl's foot, which should do nothing because of his… and then he is crying out in excruciating pain as it gnaws on the meat of his sole. He stamps it into a burst of tomato soup, spreads his toes to check they are all there, and heals. It has been a long time since he let his pedicure buffs expire. He had forgotten what it felt like to be vulnerable down there.

beats.headline: Stuck at fourteen
beats.text: Among more achievements than he expected is one for killing a swordfish guy with his foot, worth a bronze spicy box. Carl's Smush base is now level twelve. His bonus for using the pedicure kit supposedly raises it three more, but the skill is still listed as fourteen. As always, skills go wonky when item buffs try to push them toward fifteen. And these card fights are paying seriously padded experience.

beats.headline: Negated by a costume
beats.text: Inside the stinking kangaroo costume, his boxers and kneepads somehow on the outside of it, Carl gets two warnings at once: his boxer effects have been negated by his costume, and so have his pedicure effects. He pulls a banger sphere from his inventory, praying it will appear outside the costume and not in his hand under the skin. It appears in the paw.

tagline.text: The Goo-Inator 3000 is a shaping tool from a silver mechanics box, an oversized silver lollipop with a button on the handle. It only works at a workbench, so for now it waits in Carl's inventory.
At his engineering table, the Goo-Inator lets Carl work metal like dough: flatten it into a sheet, or bend it freehand.

description.text: The Goo-Inator 3000. This is a shaping tool. May only be used at a workbench. Assists in shaping materials into something else. You might want to keep the business end away from your face.

beats.headline: A lollipop with a button
beats.text: Going through his loot after the borough boss, Carl finds a really interesting item in a silver mechanics box: a tool that looks like a silver, oversized lollipop with a button on the handle. It shapes materials into something else, only at a workbench, and the System suggests keeping the business end away from his face. He can't buy a personal space until the fourth floor, so it goes back into his inventory to wait.

beats.headline: Iron like dough
beats.text: In the empty crafting room Carl sets up three tables and stands at the engineering one, Mordecai's catch-all for fashioning items with magical tools. He lays out the Goo-Inator and the Gorgon Marital Aid and clunks the massive, unenchanted breastplate of a swordsman guard onto the table. Pointed at it, the Goo-Inator makes the plate blink and offers a menu of shapes; he could flatten it like dough. He picks Freeform and puts a slight bend in it. The metal groans but does not break. Martha Stewart, says the achievement: a bronze crafter's box, with pliers, a tape measure and a bucket of pink glitter.

tagline.text: The Second Chance tome arrives by mail: a boss box has made Donut a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, one spellbook a level. It teaches Second Chance, which raises a lower-level dead monster to fight for the party for as many minutes as the spell's level.

beats.headline: The Book of the Floor Club
beats.text: Donut leaps onto the safe room's mailbox and its front opens on its own. A tome floats out. A boss box has made her a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club: one spellbook per level, mailed to her. She reads it at once, and says ew. Carl reminds her, again, to read the description first. It's Second Chance, ten mana: she can raise a lower-level monster from the dead to fight for them for as many minutes as the spell's level. It's disgusting, she says, until Carl suggests raising a dead dingo to kill another dingo, like the Lucia Mar kid with her two dogs. This is the best spell ever.

beats.headline: Undead minion, level one
beats.text: Donut has headshot three clurichauns and has fourteen mana left, so Carl asks if she wants to try her new Second Chance spell. Her whole body glows neon purple. One of the dead clurichauns twitches, glows to match and stumbles to its feet, its scorched head listing, a one-minute timer over it: Undead Minion of Crawler Princess Donut. Donut finds it most unpleasant and has no sort of controls, but told to rip up the bodies of its friends, it does, and within seconds it is dead again, the job unfinished. For the next hour she raises one after every skirmish so Carl can practise his slingshot on it, and the spell reaches level three: the minions now last three minutes.

tagline.text: Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine is a 180-proof accelerant made by Krakaren's operation from grub slime and a secret source, and carried by her clurichaun consultants in clay jugs. Carl and Donut take twenty-five of them, and Carl wants torches.
No more Rev-Up Moonshine is being made this season, and Mordecai tells a shopkeeper that Carl and Donut are the reason. Three of the bottles they kept buy a pharmaceutical starter kit.

description.text: Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine. Type: Accelerant. Effect: Highly flammable liquid. Explosive fumes. Status: Will not activate until introduced to flame. At 180 proof, this moonshine will take the hair off your chest and then put it back on. The Rev-Up version is distilled using two types of sugars: the slime trails left behind by the passage of the Brindle Grub, and a secretive, proprietary source. Created exclusively on the dungeon's second floor by the Rev-Up company, jugs of this concoction are highly sought after by the drinking establishments that populate the third, sixth, ninth, twelfth, fifteenth, and eighteenth floors. …

beats.headline: Twenty-five clay jugs
beats.text: Donut loots the dead clurichaun consultants: each of them has a clay jug of something called toilet-grade moonshine. Over the next hour she finds a pamphlet, Rev-Up, promising the benefits of becoming a Rev-Up Moonshine Consultant, see Krakaren or one of her downline consultants. By the time they stop to think they have twenty-five jugs. The description says they are valuable and sought after on deeper floors. Donut is sure the Desperado Club will buy them all and make them rich. Carl grins and asks whether she has any extra torches.

beats.headline: A third of a glass
beats.text: With the boss's tentacles breaking through the walls, Carl pulls a glass smoothie container into his right hand and a jug of unaltered moonshine into his left, pulls the cork with his teeth and fills the glass a third of the way, to a little line on the side. A tentacle bursts in overhead and moonshine sloshes out; he pours a little more, then throws the jug toward the entrance, where it shatters. The rest of the recipe is a dead fairy.

beats.headline: Three bottles for a suitcase
beats.text: Mordecai sends Carl a private note, and two bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine appear on Quint's table. Carl has been using them quite a bit in battle, but he kept a stash to sell, and besides these two he still has twenty-three. Quint sniffs one: that Krakaren bitch said no more was being made this season. Mordecai says Carl and Donut are why it was shut down, and they have the last of it, which isn't exactly true. Make it four, says Quint. Three, says Donut, half asleep, and the potion to stop the world being wavy. Deal: a starter kit, a chest of chemicals and herbs.

beats.headline: Worth more plain
beats.text: At the Silk Road, Carl puts one of his boom jugs on Pustule's table and asks what she'd give him for it. She examines it, says nice design, rubs the bottle, whimpers, and licks it. Then she snaps back to business. His material cost is much too high: a different accelerant would burn less hot and cost ninety percent less, and the plain bottles of moonshine, sold as they are, would be worth much more. She'd sell the jug for about 7,500 gold and offer him half. He keeps it.

relations.note: three bottles

tagline.text: The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is a recipe left in a dusty box beside a bicycle-powered blender. It takes two ingredients, and Carl reckons it is how a crawler is meant to get immunity from the Taint before fighting the boss.

The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is one part moonshine and one part fairy, blended pink on a child-sized bike. It gives ten doses of temporary immunity to health-seeping debuffs and disease, with the Buzzed debuff thrown in.
What is left of the smoothie from the second floor goes into Carl's infusion experiments, and mixed with a smoke curtain it is a dud.

description.text: Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie. One part moonshine, and one part fairy, this smoothie offers 10 doses for the price of one! Each sip of this delicious concoction imbues the following effects: Temporary immunity to all health-seeping conditions and debuffs. Temporary protection against all communicable diseases. Inflicts the Buzzed debuff. …

beats.headline: Two boxes in a corner
beats.text: In the corner of the clurichauns' room, Carl pulls a dangling banner, Rev-Up Smoothies! Invigorating!, off the wall and looks over two child-sized stationary bikes. A pulley runs from each tire to a little platform: a bicycle-powered blender, apparently never used. One wooden box holds twelve glass containers with screw-on lids and a lid with blades; the second holds six glasses, no blade, and a sheet of paper, the Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie Recipe. It needs two items. No wonder they discontinued this. Gross. It's all game setup, he tells Donut, and takes everything, one of the bikes included.

beats.headline: Blend until pink
beats.text: Tentacles are breaking through the walls when Carl shouts that he needs to make a goddamned smoothie. A third of a glass of moonshine; the dead laminak shoved in headfirst, her shoulders cracking; the bladed top screwed on. He sits on the much-too-small bike with his knees at his chest, recites the recipe aloud, and pedals. The fairy spins away, green, then red, then pink, and it starts to sparkle. Running, with the Taint already on him, he takes a sip that tastes like a diseased skunk, and shoves it at Donut to drink too.

beats.headline: Infection negated
beats.text: The smoothie does not lift the Taint Carl already carries, so he still cannot heal, but a pair of icons flashes for his immunity, and both of them are Buzzed: he laughs at his own death measles joke, and Donut slurs as she fires her missiles. Then a new tentacle, covered in hundreds of tiny orifices, sprays a fine green mist through the chamber. You've been infected with the Vigorous Measles! Infection negated due to immunity!

beats.headline: A dud infusion
beats.text: Two smoke curtains are infusing at Carl's table, an idea from the cookbook he has been experimenting with. In the first he is trying a smoke curtain with a splash of the Rev-Up immunity smoothie he made on the second floor, the potion that gives temporary disease immunity and makes you drunk off your ass. He can tell right away it is a bust: the curtain is blacked out and has gained the Dud status, which is what usually happens. The second infusion, a recipe from the cookbook, works.

relations.note: immunity to the Vigorous Measles her tentacle sprays

tagline.text: The Enchanted BigBoi Boxers are white, covered in little red hearts and self-sizing, because a were-creature's underwear has to survive the transformation. They give two Constitution and let the wearer cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours.

An upgrade has made Carl's boxers probably his most valuable item, Mordecai reckons: five more Dexterity, five more Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit. It adds a hundred percent damage bonus to every attack from below the waist and allows only a single layer over the crotch, so with the boxers on, no trousers.

description.text: Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. Have you ever read an Incredible Hulk comic and thought to yourself, everything rips off of his body except his pants? No way. Well, spoiler alert. You're not wrong. Size-altering and were-creatures, such as the BigBoi are required to wear enchanted, self-sizing items lest they wish to turn the dungeon into a nudist colony when they transform. That means everything they wear requires an enchantment. Everything, including their naughty little undies. + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours.

Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. This item has been Upgraded once. All right, you already know the description of this item. Something something Incredible Hulk, blah, blah, blah. Now you want to know how this item has been upgraded. Right? So here are the original benefits of these naughty little undies: + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours. That's some good shit right there. But we can do better than that. Here's a few additional benefits. + 5 to Dexterity + 5 to Intelligence + 3 more (for a total of + 5) to Constitution + The Freeballing Benefit

beats.headline: Really? Fucking really?
beats.text: Carl opens the boss box, tells himself not to say anything out loud, and says it to the ceiling anyway. Behind him Mordecai laughs, then adds that it is actually a really good prize: a white pair of boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, plus two Constitution and a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. Don't look, Carl says. He pulls his scorched and threadbare boxers off and slips the new ones on, and the old ones fall apart in his hands.

beats.headline: Upgraded, with a catch
beats.text: A Platinum Quest Box holds five thousand gold and a Scroll of Upgrade with a twenty-minute timer: one random equipped item gets better. Carl asks whether he can strip down to a single item to steer it. Yes, says Mordecai, but he wouldn't: the upgrade is never very good when people do that. Carl activates it, and his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers glow. Five Dexterity, five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, which allows a single layer over the crotch. You motherfucker, Carl tells the ceiling. Well played. You shouldn't have said you really wanted those pants, says Mordecai, and he and Donut laugh so hard Mongo wakes up.

beats.headline: Train the spell, upgrade the shorts
beats.text: One training room here combines a regular training room, the magic workshop, the explosives studio and several others into one. Carl's ordinary spells are listed as trainable alongside the spells that come from equipment, like Protective Shell. Apparently, train one of those here and it is the equipment itself that gets upgraded: in the case of Protective Shell, his boxer shorts.

beats.headline: The squad's flag
beats.text: Every squad on this level gets a bundle of small flags to stick into the monsters, and nobody gets to design their own. The Royal Court's flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, and it is an actual miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if from a clothesline, with the Royal Court of Princess Donut embroidered top and bottom like a motorcycle-club patch and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Carl finds it tacky. Elle says her squad's flag has a bag of adult diapers on it, Donut reports, and Imani's has a butterfly, and she wants to know why they couldn't get something like that.

beats.headline: Worn over a kangaroo
beats.text: Carl shoves his arms into a stinking costume and pulls the kangaroo head over his own. There is a loud click. His boxers and kneepads are now on the outside of the costume, his jacket still on the inside, his cloak round his neck. Then two warnings: his boxer effects have been negated by the costume, and so have his pedicure effects.

beats.headline: Resized for a dachshund
beats.text: Carl has turned into a long-haired dachshund, with a high voice, a German accent, no thumbs and legs far too short to drive. As with the kangaroo costume, he is still wearing his boxers. They have resized themselves and sit awkwardly on his hips, and what dangles out of one leg of them is beyond his control. His kneepads remain, tiny on his back legs; none of his rings do.

relations.note: the Royal Court's flag is a miniature pair of them

entities.name: Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic

tagline.text: The Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic gives Donut two extra points of Constitution for thirty hours, as long as someone brushes her with it for ten minutes every night. It works much as Carl's pedicure kit does.
An upgrade out of a Scab box has the brush adding a further ten percent to Donut's Constitution, on top of its two points for a brushing.

beats.headline: Ten minutes every night
beats.text: Donut combs through her achievements and boxes and finds nothing noteworthy except one item. Her boss box holds an Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic, which works much like Carl's pedicure kit: as long as someone brushes her for ten minutes every night, she gets an extra two points of Constitution for thirty hours. It is better than nothing, Carl reckons, but even with the buff her Constitution is only four.

beats.headline: She demands more brushing
beats.text: On the screen the shots keep coming, crawlers being slaughtered, and Carl can barely taste his fried chicken. At the table, Donut sits being lovingly groomed with her new brush by the safe room's Bopca Protector. The constitution buff activated many minutes ago. She demands he keep brushing. People are asleep in all twenty of the safe room's rooms for rent.

beats.headline: Part of the schedule
beats.text: Mordecai rambles about maintaining a schedule, and has somehow found what appears to be a dry erase board to mark it on. Wake, eat, apply buffs, which means showering and brushing Donut while Carl works on his feet, then an hour in the training room on one skill. Today Mordecai wants Smush. Apparently only one skill can be trained a day, even where skills overlap.

beats.headline: Ten percent more
beats.text: In the Scab box, Donut receives an upgrade to her brush: the Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic now adds a further ten percent to her constitution, on top of the measly two points it normally gives for getting brushed each morning. The same haul brings a coupon for a free Town Upgrade and a skill potion for her Love Vampire skill.

beats.headline: Bomo, be a darling
beats.text: Donut has a program to go on, so she turns to Bomo, who is busy playing on the Gamecube: be a darling and brush me out. They say their goodbyes while Bomo brushes her. The cretin does it happily, though he is not nearly as enthusiastic about it as the Sledge had been.

entities.name: Residents' wheelchair train
entities.role: Meadow Lark's ride through the hallways

tagline.text: The residents' train is ten wooden cars on wheels from wheelchairs whose owners are gone, four riders to a car, linked by one glowing magic chain and pulled by Imani and Chris in pig harnesses. It was Imani's idea, and Brandon designed it.
Out in the scorched hallway there is no sign of the wheelchair train's cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers left behind. Only its chain, which Carl grabbed earlier, has survived.

beats.headline: A parade float
beats.text: A wall of blue dots comes down the hallway, and Carl laughs: they have built a parade float. Imani and Chris strain at the front in leather pig harnesses from the tuskling courtesans. Wheels from wheelchairs that no longer have owners are fixed to long wooden platforms, cobbled together with goblin tools, the wood from the blimp boss's warehouse. It is more like a train, ten cars of four, most riders in their own chairs locked two by two, the walker users cross-legged on the boards. More maneuverable than it looks, Brandon says, but too wide for a safe room door. He added ramps.

beats.headline: Too wide for the door
beats.text: Jack has stood up on the last car to piss on the wall. Yolanda's arrow kills him and he falls off the trailer, and as the train lurches forward Randall flies off the last car with his walker. A monster forms out of the sizzling stain: a Rage Elemental. The train rockets past Carl toward the safe room a hundred feet away, but its cars are too wide for the entrance, so Imani and Chris pull people off their chairs and toss them through the door. Gravity reverses. The last car flies up and dangles from the ceiling, still chained to the rest, and Mrs. McGibbons slams into the roof of the hallway.

beats.headline: Ash in the hallway
beats.text: Carl pushes hard on the pedals and they rush out into the hallway. Everything out there is blackened and turned to ash, and it smells like burning garbage. There is no sign of the train cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers that were left behind. The only thing that survived is the long, three-hundred-foot length of glittering magical chain, which Carl grabbed earlier.

relations.note: her idea; she pulls it
he designed it and added the ramps
pulls it in a pig harness
one chain runs through every car

tagline.text: Yog's Special Chain is a scroll out of a Gold box that makes a magic chain, any length up to something like a thousand feet, light as a feather and gone in thirty hours. Imani's runs about three hundred feet through ten cars of residents.
Imani's chain outlasts the train it pulled, and dropped from a bomb launcher with weights at either end, it snares a rage elemental by the leg.
Imani uses the few chain scrolls she still has, and the chain they make hangs a whole interdiction cart from a crane without breaking.

beats.headline: Where'd you get that chain
beats.text: The residents' wheelchair train runs on one glowing chain, about three hundred feet long, from Chris through every car and back to Imani. Carl asks where the chain came from. Imani had a scroll called Yog's Special Chain, or something like that, out of some Gold box. She could pick any length up to something crazy, like a thousand feet. It's light as a feather, but the chain only lasts thirty hours.

beats.headline: The last car dangles
beats.text: Gravity reverses. The rage elemental's spell does not reach all the way to the safe room door, so the last platform, still connected to the rest of the cars by Imani's magic chain, dangles upward, having thrown off its only remaining rider. Carl pulls himself to his feet and keeps running, upside down along the ceiling of the hallway, toward the crumpled form of Mrs. McGibbons.

beats.headline: A bola off the launcher
beats.text: Everything in the hallway is ash; the train cars and abandoned wheelchairs are gone. The only thing that survived is the long, three-hundred-foot length of glittering, magical chain, which Carl grabbed earlier. Weighted at either end, it waits in one of the two chambers built on either side of the bomb on the trailer, the levers beside Donut's chair. Drop the bola! She pulls the black lever and Imani's chain snakes away through the chamber. Far behind, the elemental stops: it has been ensnared by the chain. When it comes out of the smoke at the stairwell, a length of chain is still attached to its back leg, and its health is in the red.

beats.headline: Holding up a cart
beats.text: Imani still has a few of those chain-making scrolls, and Carl asks her to use them. Several piles of the magical chain sit coiled and ready while she asks if he is sure. Within the hour the chain lifts the back end of the interdiction cart into the air from a five-legged crane over the stairwells, and it does not break. They lock it in place, the whole cart hanging vertically like a prize fish on display, and anchor the front with more chain so it won't swing.

relations.note: dropped from a chamber beside the gunner's seat

tagline.text: Dungeon Gold Rush is a scratch-off lottery ticket with six spots. One spot can be scratched each hour, and the symbol revealed decides what happens to Donut's next attack on a mob: five thousand coins, say, or double damage, or a mob that splits in two.

description.text: Dungeon Gold Rush! Scratch off one spot, and depending on the symbol revealed, your next attack against a mob will have varying effects! Guaranteed laughs! One hour cooldown between scratches.

beats.headline: Luck goes both ways
beats.text: For hitting a mob more than seventy-five levels above them, Carl and Donut each get a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box, and each holds a lottery scratch-off ticket. Donut's is red and green, with a troll-like creature throwing gold coins in the air and six spots to scratch, and the safe room will not let her use it. On the back are about twenty symbols, most of them good, like five thousand coins or double damage, a few not, like a mob that splits in two or turns invulnerable for thirty seconds. Don't use it, Carl says, not until they have talked. Fine, says Donut.

tagline.text: Fireball or Custard is a scratch-off lottery ticket with five spots. Each scratch in battle casts a spell at the nearest red-tagged mob, an even chance of a level-15 fireball or a glob of healing strawberry custard, with thirty minutes between scratches.
Carl's first scratch comes up custard. It heals the bear he is fighting, and the healing kills the worms that have been controlling her.
Carl has scratched two of the ticket's five spots: custard first, then a fireball that half collapsed the room it hit.

description.text: Fireball or Custard? Scratch off a spot in the midst of battle, and this zany ticket casts a spell at the closest red-tagged mob! Each spot has a 50/50 chance. Will it cast a level-15 Fireball? Will it cast a glob of delicious, healing Strawberry Custard? Who knows! Either way, the results will be a hoot! Thirty minute cooldown between scratches.

beats.headline: Luck goes both ways
beats.text: Damaging the rage elemental, a mob more than seventy-five levels above them, earns Carl and Donut each a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box: luck goes both ways, like your mom. Both hold a scratch-off ticket like any sold at a gas station. Donut's is Dungeon Gold Rush. Carl's has five spots and is red on one side and pink on the other, with a little cartoon dragon in the corner holding a spoon and licking its lips. Donut loves custard, and has the room's Bopca bring her some.

beats.headline: Custard comes up first
beats.text: Carl has been saving it for a dire situation, and Heather is one: a flaming, skull-faced bear on roller skates, her skin sloughing off to show a ribcage full of worms. He scratches a spot and a little icon spins between a red fireball and a pink glob. Custard. Yummy! says a voice like the Candy Crush announcer. A beachball-sized ball of custard splatters the bear. It boils against her, her skin and fur re-form in jerky clumps, and her health eases back up. Then the skates and the hat fall away: healing her has killed the worms. What is left is an old bear, dying on her own, and Carl finishes her with two punches.

beats.headline: Then a fireball
beats.text: Krasue fill a smoking apartment and Donut is on the roof above with red dots circling her. Carl yanks the ticket, fully expecting custard again, and cries fire in the hole. Fireball. Spicy! An egg-shaped ball of fire the size of an opened umbrella rolls through the bedroom door, shattering the jamb, and detonates against the upside-down corpse of Featherfall. The building rocks, the floor buckles and the room half collapses to the level below. The red dots harassing Donut all disappear, and Carl thinks they fried Featherfall's loot.

beats.headline: Three spots left
beats.text: Shut in a train car with no doors to the outside, Carl prepares a smoke curtain and moves the ticket to his hotlist. It has three scratch-off spots left. If whatever is out there breaks in, they are screwed, and he knows he won't be saved by a glob of custard this time.

tagline.text: The Mother of All Bombs is not a bomb but a launcher Carl built on the chopper's trailer, a ski-jump ramp down which Donut rolls wheeled bombs, its babies, out behind them. Brandon says the name is wrong and calls it the Bomb Chicken, and Donut agrees with him.

beats.headline: Five hours of building
beats.text: Building the launcher takes about five hours, and Carl sprays Mother of All Bombs on its side with Agatha's paint. Brandon points out that MOAB stands for Massive Ordnance Air Blast, and that a mother of all bombs means one giant bomb: call it the Bomb Chicken or something. Too late, says Carl. While they build, he finds that in a safe room every stick of dynamite reads Inert While in Safe Room. He doesn't expect it to kill the level-93 thing outside. The babies will slow it down, though.

beats.headline: The first baby rolls
beats.text: With its sidecar the chopper won't fit through the door, so a new bike trailer carries the launcher and a tall seat for Donut behind it, facing backward like a tailgunner. The ramp is a pair of spare chopper wheel wells with half-pipe channels and wheelchair coasters at its foot. Each baby is snowboard-sized, weighted like a pinewood derby car, on free-weight wheels. Donut pulls the first, Baby Uno, onto the platform: three boom jugs, goblin oil, gunpowder and the last of Carl's hobgoblin pus. She nudges it, and it rolls away down the hall behind them, straight, without rearing up.

beats.headline: Boom babies and shredders
beats.text: Carl presses the detonator, and during its five-second delay Donut pulls the black lever to drop Imani's weighted chain through a chamber. Baby Uno blows half a second late, in the elemental's back. Then the boom babies go, one after another, flipping into the grubs and filling the hallway with blue flame, while the chain snares the monster for a moment; the few that do not light themselves she hits with a low-powered magic missile. The elemental's spell flings the back of the trailer up, but they are too far away. Around the last corner she drops shredders, gunpowder and shrapnel on long wicks, which burst the pupae and give the monster hornet creatures to stop and kill.

beats.headline: Over the edge
beats.text: The chopper's boiler is about to breach, fifteen seconds, and Carl can't remember which valve to turn, so he speeds up. In the stairwell chamber Donut pulls the red lever and the second chamber sprays champagne-coloured oil across the floor. Both of them jump. The chopper keeps going, trailer and launcher with it, spilling oil, and plummets into the stairwell hole. It crunches, followed by a relatively small explosion. At the edge Carl sets down one of the oh shit babies, two boom jars, gunpowder and a ring of dynamite, as the elemental comes out of the smoke.

relations.note: he worked out how to weight the bombs
his know-how went into the babies

tagline.text: The Gorgon Marital Aid is a spatula-shaped workbench tool that hardens and softens rigid materials, and the System says intergalactic porn stars are fond of it.
Carl has built the plungers of his first landmines with the Gorgon Marital Aid.

description.text: Gorgon Marital Aid. A favorite amongst intergalactic porn stars, this is a hardening and de-hardening tool. May only be used at a workbench. Assists in fusing joints or creating varying degrees of plasticity in otherwise rigid materials without affecting material strength.

beats.headline: Shaped like a spatula
beats.text: A mechanic's box gives Carl a tool shaped like a spatula. What the hell is this, he mutters, and pulls up its properties: a hardening and de-hardening tool for the workbench, for fusing joints or giving otherwise rigid materials varying degrees of plasticity without changing their strength. That seems pretty useful. He puts it in his inventory next to his Goo-Inator 3000.

beats.headline: Plungers for a mine
beats.text: For his first derailment Carl goes with a classic: landmines, tire-shaped sections of spike-covered contact mine, an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and one hobgoblin stick for good measure. The system labels it a Jelly Bomb and gives him no credit for inventing it. When a train presses a spike, the plunger smashes an impact-detonated hob-lobber and the whole mine shreds. The plunger idea came from the Cookbook. He built the plungers with the Gorgon Marital Aid, and they are untested, which makes setting them nerve-racking.

tagline.text: Mana Toast comes out of a plain metal toaster in a safe room, one burned triangle per crawler. It refills mana, and the System says that is all it does.
Donut keeps two slices of mana toast for an emergency, because they top off her spell points without counting as a potion.

description.text: Mana Toast. This is toast. It refills your mana. That’s it. Nothing more. Fuck you.

beats.headline: One per crawler
beats.text: An unmanned safe room was once an industrial kitchen, stripped of everything but a working walk-in freezer. On a steel counter under the screens sits a plain metal toaster in a pile of crumbs, plugged into nothing and impossible to lift. The screen reads Free Mana Toast! One per Crawler! Carl presses the handle and a burned triangle of toast jumps out onto the counter. Its description ends with fuck you. Well, that was unnecessary, he mutters, and gives his piece to Donut, who tucks both away.

beats.headline: Held in reserve
beats.text: Outside the kobold boss room, Donut has a pool of twenty-eight mana points, two pieces of mana toast and a pile of mana restoration potions. With her two-minute cooldown between potions, the potions are next to useless in a battle. So they decide to wait and see what they face first.

beats.headline: Not a potion
beats.text: Planting barrel bombs from alley to alley, Carl and Donut chain invisibility potions. Donut's potion countdown is much better than it used to be, but at a minute forty-five it still means she cannot keep her mana topped off and stay invisible. She has two slices of mana toast saved for an emergency. The toast would top off her spell points and would not count as a potion, and Carl does not want her using it unless it is absolutely necessary.

tagline.text: A Proximity Trigger is a trap part, a black box the size of a dime on a long wire, that sets the conditions for a trap to go off. Carl gets ten in a Gold Sapper's Box, and his inventory ranks them near the top for value.

description.text: Proximity Trigger. Trigger Warning! Traumatizing content! Using a Sapper's Table, the highly-valuable Proximity Trigger may be attached to any non-static trap. Allows for the establishment of activation conditions, including countdowns, mob-type triggers, etc.

beats.headline: Ten tiny black boxes
beats.text: A mob has been injured by something Carl purposely left lying around, and the System awards a trap achievement and a Gold Sapper's Box. He is not sure what earned it: the chain or the oil slick, probably not the bombs. The box holds a sapper's table and ten of a trap-building item, each a tiny black box the size of a dime with a long length of wire attached. The moment they are in his inventory they place themselves near the top of the list by value, right behind that ridiculous Fireball or Custard lottery ticket.

relations.note: attached to a trap at a Sapper's Table

tagline.text: On his show, the Maestro gives Carl a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots in his size, identical to the service boots he wore on active duty, with socks in the box. It is a troll: Carl's barefoot buffs and skills stop working in shoes, and the orc knows it.

beats.headline: A present for Carl
beats.text: The Maestro's gift for his VIPs is a literal cardboard box, for Carl alone, something the orc says Carl wants really bad. Carl opens it and has to laugh. Inside is a brand-new pair of Bates zip-up tactical boots, identical to the service boots he wore on active duty, in his size, and the Maestro adds that there are socks in the box too. These will be really comfortable in a safe room, Carl says, and puts the lid back on. His soles have fully acclimated, several of his buffs and skills only work barefoot, and the orc knows it. I love them, Carl adds. I hope they weren't too expensive.

tagline.text: An Alarm Module is a ready-to-go trap, no tinkering required. Donut's gold sapper's box gives her one, along with a Spike Module.
An Alarm Module blasts a very loud song when something sets it off, or adds an alarm to a trap someone builds. On the train its first song tells the party the babies are through the door.
At his sapper's table Carl now seals alarm traps inside hollow banger spheres so they can be thrown, and because he puts them together there, he picks the songs, from memory.

description.text: Alarm Module. Two items for the price of one! A favorite of the paranoid and the rich, you can use this module to either add an alarm element to a trap you're building, or it can be used as a ready-to-go trap for those who can't be assed to sit down and make their own. When triggered, it will play a Very Loud song. And by Very Loud, I mean Norwegian Black Metal loud. You may program the song at a Sapper's Table. If you do not or are unable to pick an alarm tone, a random, culturally-important song from the past US Billboard Hot 100 will be chosen. …

beats.headline: Two trap modules
beats.text: Back in the safe room after the battle, Donut opens her loot boxes. The only new thing is two Trap Modules from her gold sapper's box: one called a Spike Module and the other an Alarm Module. These are ready-to-go traps, no tinkering required. They can be upgraded and reconfigured, but only with a sapper's table.

beats.headline: A song in the gangway
beats.text: Rabid babies are at both doors of the car when Carl asks Donut whether she still has those two trap modules. Each is a tiny cube about the size of a pair of dice. He sets the alarm on the floor of the fore gangway and puts the spike module on the janitor car's door. When the babies break through, the announcement rattles the walls: peaking at number 2 on January 13, 2007, it's Fergalicious. Donut loves this song.

beats.headline: Physical, through the portal
beats.text: The carts make hardly any noise, which is a problem for the crawlers waiting at the far end of the line, so Carl puts an alarm trap on each of the six: thirty-minute delays on five, one minute on the last, to make sure the delay works before it goes through the portal. Donut is sure it will be Wonderwall. Peaking at Number 1 on Nov 16, 1981, it's Physical, so loud Carl takes a small amount of damage. He pushes the throttle, jumps down, and watches it shoot down the track into the portal.

beats.headline: Bouncing to the beat
beats.text: Carl made five of these at his sapper's table, each labelled with a purpose, and because he built them there he could pick the songs. This one says Bass heavy. For distraction: a hollow banger sphere with an impact-detonated alarm trap inside. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze. Peaking at Number 2 on October 10th, 1992, it's Jump Around. Muffled by the metal, it still shakes the walls, and the ball bounces with the beat, slipping out of the ooze's grasp. Donut asks if that is seriously the only bass-heavy song he could think of.

beats.headline: Swallowed by a shark
beats.text: In the water the party is sandwiched between the current and a mob, apparently a shark, lazily circling toward them. The creature crunches on a corpse and some other debris, and when it opens its mouth Carl can hear the distinctive beat of Jump Around blast out into the ocean. It has eaten the goddamned alarm trap. None of Carl's explosives with exposed fuses will work well under water, and he is not keen to be anywhere near the ones that might.

beats.headline: Donut picks the song
beats.text: Invisible, Carl chucks an alarm ball as hard as he can toward the club's front entrance. He has no idea what the song will be: Donut begged to pick a few for the distraction balls, and he let her, for the practice at his sapper's table. Topping at number two on March 23rd, 1985, it's Material Girl. As the Madonna song starts and the large demon turns toward the music, Carl bolts across the open space, and the body of a dead sai she has just tossed away slams him through the doors into the kitchens.

relations.note: its song is programmed at the table
sealed inside a hollow banger sphere to make a throwable alarm ball

tagline.text: A Spike Module is one of two ready-to-go trap modules out of Donut's gold sapper's box, no tinkering required. Changing one needs a sapper's table.

A Spike Module is a cube the size of a pair of dice that pushes fifty-centimetre spikes out of a one-metre square every two seconds, forever once something hostile triggers it. Carl has found that it will stand on a door.

beats.headline: Two trap modules
beats.text: Back in the safe room after the show, Donut opens her loot boxes from the earlier battle. The only new things are two Trap Modules from her gold sapper's box, one called a Spike Module and the other an Alarm Module. They are ready-to-go traps, no tinkering required. They can be upgraded and reconfigured, but only with a sapper's table, and that won't happen until the fourth floor.

beats.headline: Spikes on a door
beats.text: Rabid babies are at both doors of the train car, and Carl asks whether Donut still has the two trap modules. Each is a tiny cube the size of a pair of dice. The spike module pops fifty-centimetre spikes out of a one-metre square every two seconds; friendly NPCs and crawlers won't set it off, but once triggered it spikes forever. Could it go on a door? He places it against the janitor car's door, and it lets him set it vertically and moves with the door. When the alarm goes off, shrieks explode behind the far door and experience notifications roll in from mobs impaled on the door spikes.

relations.note: both came out of the same gold sapper's box

tagline.text: The Master Pen Key opens the cages of the fighters and the bait animals in the kobold fighting pits. It is attuned to kobolds, and in anyone else's hand it works once and breaks.

description.text: Master Pen Key. Opens the individual cages of both the fighters and the bait animals within the kobold fighting pits. This key is magically attuned to the kobold race. If you are not a kobold and attempt to use this key, it will only work once before breaking. Choose wisely.

beats.headline: Choose wisely, says the key
beats.text: Picking through the slagged kobolds, Carl finds that the one who pressed the button to open the cages also had a key. It opens the individual cages of the fighters and the bait animals in the kobold fighting pits; for anyone but a kobold it works once and breaks. Past a dirt arena stained red and a pile of bones as tall as the ceiling, a line of ten cages waits, and the room announces itself as a pet reward room. Its reward: you have a key, and it opens only one cage.

beats.headline: The last cage
beats.text: Donut claims the choice and gasps at the very last cage: a pink-feathered chicken dinosaur thing, a red-tagged mongoliensis. Carl thinks it looks like dinner and would rather take the brindle grub. A pet biscuit tossed at its cage bounces off a blue forcefield. Warning: the cages will permanently close in thirty seconds. Donut begs. Carl sighs, takes the key, and jams it into the lock of the mongoliensis cage. The little bastard shoots out, and he grabs it in both hands.

relations.note: his cage

tagline.text: Donut 'coincidentally' receives a spell book of Heal Critter from the boss boxes in the kobold pits, just after she and Carl have won a baby dinosaur.
Heal Critter is on Donut's spell list now, at level one.
Donut's Heal Critter is level fifteen, though like every pet spell it will not work on a special mount.

beats.headline: A coincidental spell book
beats.text: The rules are a little weird about taming dungeon pets, Mordecai says, while Mongo screams and hisses at him from his cage: remove the creature's hostility first, then come back. Then Carl and Donut open their boxes from the boss fight. Donut 'coincidentally' receives a spell book of Heal Critter; Carl gets another Potion of Determine Value and a thousand gold.

beats.headline: Mongo glows after the blast
beats.text: Heal Critter is on Donut's list now, at level one. Half the street where they were just standing explodes and throws them forward, rocks and debris raining over them, and Mongo squeals in pain. Then he glows as Donut casts Heal Critter, and she rushes to the small, blood-splattered dinosaur, clucking over him worriedly.

beats.headline: It worked, in capitals
beats.text: Up in the flying house in a storm, Donut sends Carl a message in capitals while he fights feral scorpions in a sandstorm: we did it, I cast Heal Critter, and it worked. She can't believe it. The health is still going down, though, and the stupid dog doesn't even appreciate it.

beats.headline: Not on a mount
beats.text: Weighing a vehicle against a mount, Donut points to her Twinkle Toes spell and her level-15 Heal Critter. Hedy the gremlin, on the floor fighting another gremlin, gasps that pet spells don't work on special mounts: neither Twinkle Toes nor Heal Critter will work on them.

tagline.text: The Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition is a tech-based personal shield made by the Valtay Corporation. One was in Agatha's shopping cart, and Carl only learns it from his inventory's history, after he has given the cart back.

Carl has a Perso-Shield of his own now, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, unlocked from the hunters' tech loot. Switched on, it wraps him in an inch-thick buffer against physical blows, and somewhat against corporeal spells, for about two minutes, then takes about an hour to charge.

description.text: Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition. – Tech-based Personal Shield.

beats.headline: In the History tab
beats.text: Waiting out the timer, Carl opens a new inventory tab labelled History and sorts it by value. At the top sit three items he has never seen: a Valtay tunnel communications relay, a Valtay Corp pulse pistol, and a Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition, a tech-based personal shield. The relay carries a warning that unsanctioned communication devices are illegal down here. Then a blue dot moves toward them, and when Carl sees who it is, he understands: he took Agatha's whole shopping cart into his inventory during the boss fight with the Ball of Swine and never examined it. She wheels the squeaking cart in and calls him a cart thief.

beats.headline: A Saturn on his shirt
beats.text: Back from the homeless shelter, Carl uses two of the three Cracker Jack scrolls from his trade to unlock a pair of alien shields out of the hunters' tech loot. His is a Valtay Perso-Shield, Platinum Edition, identical to the one he would have had from Paulie: a round pinback button that looks a little like Saturn, needing no equipment slot, switched on and off from his interface. It stops physical damage and somewhat stops corporeal spells like Magic Missile and Fireball. It lasts about two minutes and recharges in about an hour, and it covers Donut on his shoulder only if she is touching him when it comes on.

beats.headline: Teeth on the buffer
beats.text: A succubus picks Carl out across the hallway, I choose you, stud, shrugs off a banger sphere and slams into him with the force of a bus. As she goes for his neck with vampire fangs, he activates his new tech-based shield, and her teeth spark and shatter like broken crockery. He casts Wisp Armor to shore it up. Her hands sparkle where they grip his arms, and the shield loses power fast as she slams him against the floor. It sparks out just as a tentacle from Donut's stolen Hell Scrub drags her away.

tagline.text: A magical pet carrier is the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball: supposedly expensive, Odette says, and a way to put a bonded pet into inventory without harming it.
Mongo's carrier cost 15,000 gold: a square brown box the size of a Rubik's Cube with a fire hydrant etched on it. He sleeps and recovers inside it, and comes back out at the press of a button.
A pet carrier is how Ren hands Carl her pet, unconscious and level one now.
Carl carries Ren's pet in a pet carrier in his inventory, and as long as he stays boxed up, Mordecai says, he will be fine.

beats.headline: The dungeon's pokeball
beats.text: Donut has trained Mongo to perch quietly on her back, clinging to her fur, and he has behaved himself. Mostly. Odette has mentioned something called a magical pet carrier, apparently the dungeon's equivalent of a pokeball. They are supposedly expensive, but one would let them put a bonded pet into inventory without harming him. Carl doesn't care how much it costs. If they can afford it, it is going to be one of their first purchases.

beats.headline: Fifteen thousand gold
beats.text: They spend 15,000 gold on a magical pet carrier for Mongo. Neither Donut nor Mongo is keen, but Mordecai points out that the dinosaur feels obliged to guard them while they sleep, even in a safe room, and it is hurting his stats; and no pets are allowed in the Desperado Club. The device is a square brown box the size of a Rubik's Cube with a fire hydrant etched on the outside. Donut activates it, Mongo is zapped inside to sleep and regain his strength, and a press of the button calls him back out.

beats.headline: It doesn't work
beats.text: A door glows behind them, locked until the fight is over, and Mongo is hurt. Donut is more taken up with him than with the fight. He no longer seems to be in pain, but he is bleeding. Carl, Mongo won't stop bleeding, she cries. My pet carrier doesn't work! His health is still going down. Carl tosses a broken side table onto the stairs and tells her to try one of the bandages. They each have hundreds of them.

beats.headline: Ren's parting gift
beats.text: Ren gives Carl her best gear, and Garret: unconscious, level one now, his name gone, a tiny round ball on two stubby legs with a single tooth sticking out. She picks him up, kisses him, says she is sorry, and puts him in a pet carrier. His new weakness, she adds, is something called Reaper Gaze. She slides the carrier across, and before he can talk himself out of it Carl puts it in his inventory. A host of pet-themed achievements appear and disappear.

beats.headline: Keep him boxed up
beats.text: Carl asks Mordecai what to do with the tummy acher. Keep that thing in your inventory, Mordecai says. Carl couldn't go down the stairs with Mongo before because he didn't have a pet carrier. This one will be fine as long as he stays boxed up. Bonding can wait: with everything else on Carl's plate, a level-one pet is too much to keep alive, especially if it has an undead weakness. And Ren made a mistake saying his weaknesses out loud.

tagline.text: A Big Top Ticket is one of the things a dead clown was carrying, along with a hunk of Clown Meat and 35 gold. Carl loots all of it with a mass of red dots fifteen seconds away.

A Big Top Ticket admits one adult into Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Big Top Show, with Safe Passage through the public areas only. Signet says that means anywhere in the tent except the three rings, which is exactly where the three poles are.

description.text: Big Top Ticket. Lucky you! This ticket admits one adult into the Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Big Top Show. The holder of this ticket is guaranteed Safe Passage through the public areas only. Grimaldi reserves the right to rescind this safe passage guarantee to drunks and purveyors of violence. Guaranteed good time or your money back!

beats.headline: Off a dead clown
beats.text: A clown in a red wig and a little hat, carrying a pair of oversized butcher knives, goes down under Carl's fists, its forked tongue lolling, and he keeps pounding until its head caves in. A mass of red dots is fifteen seconds out. The clown's inventory reads Clown Meat, Big Top Ticket, 35 Gold. Carl loots it all, plus both knives, the wig and the hat. Mongo is still tearing at the clown's ankle, and when Carl picks him up he has gotten noticeably larger and squeals in rage.

beats.headline: Brandish it and go in
beats.text: Signet cannot go inside the big top. She has been banished, her minions too, and the outside of the tent is impenetrable. Some of the clowns carry big top tickets, she says: find one and brandish it. The tickets are magical, and promise safe passage within the tent as long as the holder stays out of the three rings. The three poles that have to be broken are in the rings, and so is the vine. Carl already has two tickets. He reads one again and does not expect to have a good time.

beats.headline: Held out like a shield
beats.text: Carl walks into the big top through a giant clown's mouth with the ticket held out in front of him. Round the first corner stands a round clown, shorter than he is and almost three times as wide, who hisses at him. Carl brandishes the ticket like a shield. The clown leans in and sniffs it, like a treat held up to a dog, hisses again, and steps aside. Inside, nothing so much as glances at him. Carl keeps clutching the ticket anyway. If he drops it, he fears, he is toast.

relations.note: his Traveling Circus Big Top Show

entities.name: Carl's cactus
entities.role: A gift from the Earth box

tagline.text: Carl's Silver Earth box held a small cactus in a clay pot, three inches tall and covered in yellow spikes, with a $3.99 Home Depot price tag still on it. He cannot think why they chose it for him.

Li Na has cast a dread trap on Carl's cactus and then gone into a cleaner bot that is meant to carry her out of the dungeon. Its glow, its blooms and its dust will say whether she is alive, gone or dead, and a single flower will mean the way is safe.
A single flower has bloomed on Carl's cactus. Li Na reached the Pineapple Cabaret, and it is safe to send the others after her.

beats.headline: Three ninety-nine at Home Depot
beats.text: Carl's own Silver Earth box, the incentive for choosing an Earth class, holds two random items and a Hobby potion. The first is a small cactus plant in a clay pot, short and squat, about three inches tall and covered in yellow spikes, with the price tag still on the pot: $3.99, from a Home Depot. The second is a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen westerns. Donut's gifts were deliberate, a candle and a cat tree. Carl examines the cactus, wondering why they chose it for him, sighs, and puts it into his inventory.

beats.headline: A dread for a signal
beats.text: Donut tells Carl that Li Na has cast some gooey dread thing on his cactus. Rosetta produces it, glowing blue: a dread trap, Deadly bloom, which normally blooms when someone comes near and releases a paralysing spore. Carl knows it: it came from picking an Earth class, and it was in his room until Samantha put it out for not matching the new rug. Its state will report Li Na. Glowing, she is alive in the dungeon. Blooming and spreading spores but unlit, she has left the game. Dust, she died inside. Prepotente leans in and tells them to keep it somewhere safe: what if she is trapped in the bot? Then the glow will fail over several days. One flower, still glowing, means come. Three means alive but not safe.

beats.headline: Everyone looks at the cactus
beats.text: Zhang, who has to be the one, points the pet carrier at Li Na and presses the button, and she is inside it. The white cleaner bot Suckira picks the carrier up and it is gone without so much as a beep. Nothing happens. Everyone turns to the cactus. So far there is no change. The one thing they do not want is for it to activate and then turn to dust, which would mean she is dead.

beats.headline: A single flower
beats.text: Carl has just read the reward for a finished quest and sighed that they need to get to work when Mordecai's message comes in. A single flower has just bloomed on the cactus. Donut gasps. It worked. One flower is the code for Li Na having made it to the Pineapple Cabaret, and for it being safe to bring the others the same way.

beats.headline: The only one that talks
beats.text: Imani reports 227 crawlers sent to the Pineapple Cabaret, not counting Li Na, and Mordecai reports the cactus steady, glowing with a single bloom. The druid Ronit has worked out something simpler for the rest: a small potted plant for each of them, tied to that crawler's life, wilting or turning to dust if they die and blooming if they escape. Mordecai had to build a glass terrarium for the lot because the sluggalos were eyeing them. Li Na's dread cactus is the only one with the complicated messaging system.

relations.note: casts a dread trap on it to report her status
one flower means Li Na reached it and it is safe

tagline.text: An Earth Hobby Potion is a reward the Syndicate Government requires for every crawler with a domestic class: drink it for level three in a random Earth hobby. Donut's is Scutelliphily, which nobody can explain, and Carl's is Cesta Punta, which he wonders might be a martial art.

What an Earth Hobby Potion teaches arrives all at once. Carl's Cesta Punta is jai-alai, the sport of the scoop his fans have just voted him, and Katia's has made her a gear head who has never actually fixed an engine.
Donut's Scutelliphily, Britney explains, is the love of small shields. Her hobby is patches.

description.text: Earth Hobby Potion. Per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, this particular reward is required by the Syndicate Government to be awarded to all Crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. Taking this potion is optional, however it may not be sold or transferred to other Crawlers or entities. Upon drinking this, you will immediately obtain a Level Three skill ability in a unique, Earth-based hobby. The benefit is chosen at random, however you will not receive a skill that you currently have. Gods, I hate it when the lawyers make me put their crap into the descriptions. Don't you? …

beats.headline: Required by law
beats.text: Donut's Earth box holds a scented candle labelled Sea Breeze that smells nothing like the sea, a cat tree larger and fancier than her old one, and an Earth Hobby Potion. The description cites subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act: the Syndicate Government requires one for every crawler with a domestic class. Drink it, and gain level three in a random Earth hobby. It could be Parkour. It could be Kombucha Brewing. Carl's Earth box holds one too, beside a three-inch cactus from Home Depot and a pack of eighteen paperback westerns.

beats.headline: Scutelliphily and Cesta Punta
beats.text: Donut drinks hers, glows, and makes a face. Scutelliphily. She doesn't even know what it means; she is a scutelliphile, which sounds obscene. What a waste. Carl clicks his in his hotlist and feels a warmth spread through him. Level 3 in the Cesta Punta skill, and no other explanation. Was that a martial art? He doesn't feel any different. It's likely the art of cracking nuts with your toes, Donut says, and, laughing, asks Gordo the bopca for walnuts so they can experiment.

beats.headline: Jai-alai
beats.text: Running his hand down the wicker-looking basket from his fan box, Carl's mind races, and it all comes rushing to him from that Earth Hobby Potion. Cesta Punta is not a martial art. It is a sport, more commonly known as jai-alai: a complicated, fast-paced, squash-like game in which players wear scoops on their hands and throw balls against a wall, dangerous enough to knock your head off even in a helmet. The scoop a player wears is a xistera, and that is what the fans have voted him.

beats.headline: A gear head
beats.text: Katia tells Carl what she can do. She has no useful spells. She is immune to wind spell damage. She is also good at fixing engines, though she was never a mechanic and has never actually fixed one: she got her Earth Hobby Potion, and she is a gear head. Before all this she was an art teacher, which Carl, looking at her poorly sculpted face, finds hard to credit. She smiles sheepishly.

beats.headline: Engines on demand
beats.text: Putting the vehicle's track mechanism together with Carl, Katia credits the hobby potion. She was sitting there wondering how they were going to build it, and suddenly it was there, like that Matrix movie. Carl's cesta punta translates well into action, he says, but it is mostly muscle. Donut's is still a mystery. Scutelliphily. He has asked a hundred people, and nobody knows what the hell it is.

beats.headline: Small shields
beats.text: Carl thinks he has finally worked out Donut's hobby. He pats his bomb patch: what type of thread is on this thing? Something to do with embroidery or patches, he says, and Donut gasps that he's right. Britney supplies the rest. Scutellus is Latin for small shield, phileein the Greek for the love of, so it means the love of small shields. Donut loves little patches. If anyone had asked, Britney says, she could have told them earlier.

tagline.text: Mongo's collar is black and magical, out of Donut's gold pet box, and it puts his orange dot on the map wherever he is. He does not care for it.

beats.headline: Out of a gold pet box
beats.text: In the gold pet box, Donut receives a black, magical collar for Mongo that places his orange dot on the map wherever he is. Mongo screams and tries to rip it off. After a few admonishments from Donut he relents and stops scratching at it.

beats.headline: A boa on the collar
beats.text: Katia and Donut come back from the Desperado Club, where they spent the whole two hours of the storm, Katia with a feather boa round her neck. Mongo is loose too, and he has a boa of his own, dangling from his collar. He keeps snapping at it, and feathers fly everywhere. Donut and Katia went into the Penis Parade together.

entities.name: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak

tagline.text: The Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak is a simple wooden anklet off a dead crawler, with three little beads that click like seed pods. Its description calls anklets garish, so Carl gives it to Donut for the constitution, and she wears it on a back leg where nobody will see it.
To the city elves, the anklet on Donut's back leg is the forbidden oak, and they take its bearer for the Oak Fell, Apito's version of the antichrist.

description.text: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak. Imbues wearer with +1 Dexterity, +1 Constitution, and gives +3 to the skill Double Tap. It's also an anklet. One would think anklets enhance the beauty of feet like toe rings do, but they are excessive, jangly distractions that make you look too garish.

beats.headline: Pried off a dead crawler
beats.text: Three dead crawlers have been left out as a trap where the lemurs caught them: three women of one family, all level 8. Their gear was stripped in a hurry, but the tree-like one still wears an anklet, which takes a few minutes to pry off her ankle, and another still has two rings. The anklet is wood, with three little beads that click like seed pods. Plus one Dexterity, plus one Constitution, plus three to the skill Double Tap, and a description that calls anklets garish. Wood, says Donut: what is this, the 70s? Carl says she needs the constitution. She puts it on her back leg so nobody will see it, and it shrinks into her fur.

beats.headline: The beads rattle
beats.text: Nine city elves are spoiling for a fight, and Carl wants them to make the first move in front of the town guards. On his word Donut lifts her back leg and shakes it, and the anklet's three little beads rattle. The elves come apart. They growl and hiss like a pack of wild animals, the Light Healer claws her own face bloody, the fire mage wets himself and the summoner sucks his thumb. Donut grumbles that she always said wood jewelry was ugly. Salvatore names her the bearer of the forbidden oak, eats an acorn, and begins to glow.

beats.headline: Kept out of sight
beats.text: A single crawler stands in the crowd watching the municipal building fall, and Carl whispers to Donut not to let him see the fallen oak bracelet on her back leg. It is Daniel Bautista, the man who killed the Divider in the swimming pool, and Carl takes him for family of the three dead women they found days ago. Donut picked up the anklet off them. If the man knew, would he want it back? Too bad for him if he did. Carl decides it is best not to broach the subject at all.

relations.note: her city elves take its bearer for the Oak Fell

tagline.text: Nica's strength rings are two rings, each +2 to strength, that Carl takes off a dead crawler named Nica. They bring his strength back to an acceptable level.

beats.headline: Off a dead crawler's fingers
beats.text: Of the three dead women left out as a trap, the human named Nica still has two rings on her fingers, both +2 to strength. Donut can't wear them, so Carl rubs the blood off and puts them on himself, which makes four rings and brings his strength back to an acceptable level. He takes no joy in looting the corpses of fellow crawlers. All the same, he can see the allure of being a player killer. This game gives a lot of loot.

beats.headline: Best not mentioned
beats.text: In the crowd outside the fallen municipal building, Carl recognises a crawler he takes for family of Grace, Nica and Lea, the three dead women they came across several days earlier. Someone with them had looted most of their gear. Donut picked up the anklet, and Carl took the two generic strength rings. If the man knew they had them, would he want them back? That would be too bad for him. Carl figures it is best not to broach the subject at all.

tagline.text: Mordecai mixed a double healing potion that he insisted would cure a parasitic infestation. Carl drinks it in Grimaldi's big top with a mouthful of worms, and throws up a never-ending stream of them, dead and dying.
The double healing potion also works on a brain parasite, Mordecai says, if it is drunk before the parasite reaches the brain.

beats.headline: Worms on a cone
beats.text: Apollon the ogre hands Carl a rotten cone heaped with wriggling worms. Compliments of Grimaldi. Carl casts Wisp Armor, opens his mouth, and the worms glide down his throat: he has been infested with a parasite, and the voices tell him he is one of them now. He pleads with Grimaldi to listen to Signet. With less than a minute on his timer he readies the double healing potion Mordecai mixed the night before, which Mordecai insisted would cure a parasitic infestation. As the worms surge back into his mouth he slams it, and falls to his knees vomiting a never-ending stream of dead and dying worms.

beats.headline: Out through the neck
beats.text: Phased, Carl reaches into Chris's lava-rock head and grasps the palm-sized worm lodged in his brain. It doesn't die. It bites his palm, burrows into his arm and is gone. Mordecai said the double-healing potion would work only if Carl drank it before she reached his brain, and she will get there fast. He waits out two seconds of potion cooldown and slams it. Last time he vomited the parasites out. This time she bursts out of his neck like a sniper's round, thrashing, her health in the red with Poisoned pulsing over her.

tagline.text: Carl's Lucky Bastard box, for surviving Signet's attack, holds a single comp chip worth 100,000 gold at the Desperado Club casino. It cannot be sold, traded or cashed in for gold, only played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune.
Carl played the chip on the Wheel of Fortune, where a comp chip leaves only two bad spots, and it won him a Scroll of Upgrade.

description.text: 100,000 Gold Coin Casino Chip. This is a comp chip, and it may not be sold or transferred. You may not redeem this chip directly for gold. This chip must be played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune game at the Desperado Club Casino. Good luck.

beats.headline: Not a lottery ticket
beats.text: Carl expected another lottery ticket from his Lucky Bastard box, the one he got for surviving Signet's attack, and instead gets a single casino chip. Mordecai snatches it before it can vanish into Carl's inventory; he has never even seen one. It is black, with pink and purple splotches staggered round the edge and a familiar dagger logo in the centre, and it feels as if it weighs fifteen pounds. So you're rich, Mordecai says. Maybe. It can only be played at the High Roller's Roulette Table or the Wheel of Fortune. Bea always loved roulette.

beats.headline: One spin, then another
beats.text: Carl wants to cash the chip in. It is the Wheel of Fortune or waiting until the sixth floor for the High Rollers Roulette Table, and he never liked roulette anyway. The croupier, Tito, explains that a comp chip is the maximum bet and leaves only two red spots on the wheel: Nothing! and Get stabbed in the stomach by the croupier. Carl does the odds and plunks it down. The wheel stops on Spin Again, beside the 500,000-gold sliver. Behind him a roulette player drops through the floor into the Nothing. The needle hangs by Nothing! and settles on green: a Scroll of Upgrade.

entities.name: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk
aka: Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk

tagline.text: The Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk are a pair of metal caps like loose vampire teeth, out of Donut's Platinum Quest Box. They add half again to a bite, with a chance to poison or paralyze, and Donut decides at once that Mongo is getting them.
Mongo wears the fang caps now, and every time he snaps his teeth, little tendrils of electricity burst from his mouth.

description.text: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk. This is a Fleeting item! Fun fact. There is not a single dentist from your world left in the dungeon. A few made it to the first floor, but every single one of those fuckers is now tits up. There're a few hygienists left, but I wouldn't want to rely on those chuckleheads. What I'm getting at is that you need to install these yourself. Make sure they're facing the right direction. You can always take them off, but this is a fleeting item. That means they disappear once they're off. So don't fuck it up. …

beats.headline: Out of a quest box
beats.text: Donut's Platinum Quest Box holds 5,000 gold, a skill potion and a pair of fang caps. They don't suit her fighting style, Mordecai says: sell them, or give them to Mongo. Most gear can't be swapped with a pet, but these can, and his type can wear up to six pairs. The caps look like loose vampire teeth. Fifty percent more bite damage, a 25 percent chance of level-five poison, 10 percent of paralysis, and they vanish once they come off. Carl, you'll have to put them on him, says Donut. Carl eyes the sleeping dinosaur, who chomps at the air.

beats.headline: Snapped in like Legos
beats.text: Getting the two chompers onto Mongo is easier than the description made it sound. The golden fangs resize themselves and snap into his mouth like Legos in about five seconds, while he whimpers like a dog getting his nails clipped. Now little tendrils of electricity burst from his mouth whenever he snaps his teeth. At first it scares him so much he pees himself, which sets Mordecai off. Once he learns the electric bites don't hurt him, he chomps at the air constantly, grunting with excitement at the sparks.

beats.headline: They bite ghosts
beats.text: The alley on the way to the magistrate's roof is full of Shadow Leaks, smoke-like, ghost-class mobs with a stinging cold attack. Carl's magical gauntlet damages them as easily as if they were flesh, and Mongo's magical teeth caps can hurt them too. The ghosts give off an unusually high amount of experience and are easy to kill. Mongo hits level 13 and gets noticeably larger, rising to the height of Carl's chest.

beats.headline: In a muted zone
beats.text: Donut finds the area muted and cannot cast. Mordecai explains: in a muted zone, spells from the menu and scrolls won't cast, but magical items, potions and spells already cast still work. Mongo has those magical teeth caps. Go bite that elf's head off, Carl tells him, but be quick, and Donut says sic 'em. The dinosaur weaves in, turns his head sideways like he is eating a taco, and chomps down. The dark elf's head caves in under the bite, and the purple swirls of magic blink off.

beats.headline: A second pair
beats.text: Donut's next platinum quest box holds what the last one did: a pair of fang caps and a skill potion. The first set gave Mongo a damage buff and the chance to poison or paralyze, though neither seems to happen often, because the mobs are usually dead by the time he is chomping down on them. The two new caps add 15 percent movement speed and 15 percent strength to the level-29 dinosaur. Once again Donut makes Carl put them in, and he has to fish a piece of robot Donut out of Mongo's mouth first.

tagline.text: Hobgoblin dynamite comes in white sticks instead of goblin red, with a larger yield and far more stability. Carl's first whole box of it came with three globs of hobgoblin pus, remote-controlled detonators.
A stick of hobgoblin dynamite is practically a mini nuke: thrown half a block, it knocks Carl off his feet and brings down a building's front. It is utterly impractical in a regular fight.
Hobgoblin dynamite is much more stable than the goblin kind and should survive several impacts, so Carl builds it into his bigger bombs.
Carl cuts hobgoblin sticks down at need, carefully slicing one into twenty pieces.

beats.headline: White instead of red
beats.text: Sifting through his rewards, Carl finds more goblin dynamite and smoke bombs, and, in the bronze boss box from his fight with Heather, a whole box of hobgoblin dynamite along with three globs of Hobgoblin Pus, the remote-controlled explosive detonators. He has never seen hobgoblin dynamite before. The sticks are white instead of red, with a larger yield, and they are much more stable.

beats.headline: Highway robbery
beats.text: Pustule's tables at the Silk Road hold boxes of goblin and hobgoblin dynamite, smoke bombs, detonators and pancake-like claymores at 5,000 gold each. A case of goblin dynamite is twenty-five sticks for 500 gold. The hobgoblin sticks are twenty for 2,000, which Carl calls highway robbery. Her fused hob-lobbers, she says, work like hobgoblin dynamite: impact resistant, extra stable, light the fuse and toss.

beats.headline: Practically mini nukes
beats.text: From a rooftop near the saferoom, Carl does not want to waste his hob-lobbers on a handful of shambling berserkers, so he tries a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, which he has never used. He hurls it with his upgraded strength at a shambler half a block away. The explosion knocks him off his feet, the front of a distant building caves in and fills the street with debris, and the shambler and the one behind it are obliterated. The power is great, he decides, but the sticks are utterly impractical in regular fights.

beats.headline: Two robots, three sticks
beats.text: For the two robots, Carl uses three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator. He sets the charges without incident, moves all the way back to the platform and sets them off. The automatons never turned on or fought back, and they come back as scrap, their bottom halves mostly intact and hunks of metal everywhere: the hobgoblin dynamite is especially good at tearing stuff up. Once the metal cools he collects all he can, cogs, wheels and two damaged dwarven batteries.

beats.headline: A stick in every mine
beats.text: Carl's new mines look like tire-shaped cross sections of the spiked naval contact mines of the early twentieth century, the plunger lifted from the cookbook and changed just enough. Each is an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers, with a single, hopefully stable stick of hobgoblin dynamite added for extra measure. When a train depresses a spike, an impact-detonated hob-lobber shatters and the whole mine shreds. The system calls it a Jelly Bomb, and gives him no credit for inventing it.

beats.headline: A train full of explosives
beats.text: Elle tells Carl by chat that some crazy asshole is throwing a train full of explosives their way. He laughs and ties the last piece of hobgoblin dynamite onto the pile. It is much more stable than the goblin stuff and should, in theory, survive multiple impacts, and the bundle rides up high so it won't go off until triggered: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high for the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a giant stage-three monster, or the back of the other train.

beats.headline: A block per barrel
