description.text: Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar. "AnD SO The lioN fEll iN lOVe WiTh The LaMB." I'm actually quite fond of the Twilight novels. Plus, I would never stoop so low as to disparage the work of an over-imaginative and obviously undersexed artist who managed to become a brazilianaire from barely-disguised erotica targeted at adolescent girls. However, I would like to take this opportunity to point out that your culture's obsession with fictional, underaged heroes was absolutely misguided. …

beats.headline: Purple, like garlic
beats.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty gives a patch; Donut's gold box from the Apothecary gives a sparkling bracelet, and she equips it at once. The obsidian Fireball bracelet moves to her right foreleg, this one goes on the left, and with the fallen oak anklet and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the back legs, all four legs are full. She loves it, though the description sounds like the AI is having a stroke. Its purple gems are shaped like bulbs of garlic. It protects against vampirism and lycanthropy, with plus 25 percent magical damage against sapient undead. Carl's patch gives the exact same benefits. Mordecai grunts: the two sponsors really are working together.

beats.headline: A vampire, by coincidence
beats.text: Miriam Dom is trapped and asking for help as the sun sets. Mordecai suggests letting her die and collecting her gear in the morning. Two different sponsors who know more than they do just spent a huge amount of money to protect them from vampirism, he says, and by coincidence a vampire shows up asking for help. She saved my life, Carl says, grabbing the sewing kit. If it's a trap to turn them into vampires, they will be protected.

relations.note: the same three benefits, from the Plenty

tagline.text: A gold box from the Plenty holds a patch for Carl's jacket: a gray goat head on black, denim-like cloth, the symbol of the Midnight Epicure, a children's bogeyman grown into a ward against all night evils. It protects against vampirism and lycanthropy and adds a quarter more magical damage against sapient undead.
The goat on Carl's patch is the Midnight Epicure, the god Prepotente worships: a tale made to scare non-caprid children that grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Medium. Ah, yes. The Midnight Epicure. The Caprid Who Devours the Sky. This scary-ass fable is used to terrify children across the universe. […] Over the cycles, the rather disturbing symbol of the Midnight Epicure, which is really just a racist caricature of an adult Caprid, developed into a ward against all night evils. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: Protection against Vampirism. Protection against Lycanthropy. +25% Magical damage against all sapient undead. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: The Plenty's goat
beats.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty hisses, spins and opens like a flower on a patch for his jacket, the same size as his white bomb patch: black, denim-like material with a gray goat head screen-printed on it. Donut mutters about screen printing. Read the description, says Mordecai, and sew it on right away. Carl has seen the satanic goat before, on the back of Prepotente's hand, and sketched it into the cookbook, assuming it was a deity's mark. The description calls it a fable. Its benefits are exactly those of the silver bracelet Donut has just pulled from her own box.

beats.headline: Sewn on, not straight
beats.text: Mordecai suggests letting Miriam Dom die and collecting her gear in the morning: two sponsors who know more than Carl have just spent a fortune protecting him from vampirism, and a vampire is asking for help the moment the sun sets. She saved my life, says Carl, grabbing the sewing kit; if it is a trap, they will be protected. He sews the patch on beside the bomb patch, his wide stitches covering Katia's careful threading, and Donut gasps that it is not straight. It is good enough. An achievement, a few levels in sewing, and the patch glows as it is officially affixed.

beats.headline: Protected by the jacket
beats.text: Carl stabs the loose heart of the boss in the rain, and the monster explodes, showering gore over all of them and spilling the rest of itself from the ruined trees. When Mongo leans down to bite at the remains, Carl tells him not to dare. Vampirism is contagious, and Carl knows that if his jacket did not protect him he would likely be infected: he would die, then wake up overcome with hunger. Half the dinosaurs in the forest are infected already.

beats.headline: She can see the glow
beats.text: Carl is still cautious with Miriam Dom, and she understands why. The two of them are in no danger from her, she tells him. She can see the glow on them: Carl and Donut are both protected from vampirism, and she could not feed on them even if she wanted to.

beats.headline: The goat is a god
beats.text: Carl asks Prepotente about his god; all he knows of it is what the patch on his jacket says, the one that protects him from vampires and werewolves. The Midnight Epicure, says Prepotente, protects all prey animals by destroying all existence after unleashing all the consumed back into the galaxy: they who were eaten become the devourers. It began as a xenophobic tale to scare non-caprid children and grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind. His sponsors gave him the ability to worship it in a benefactor box.

relations.note: the same three benefits

tagline.text: Mordecai's holy water grenades: potion balls of a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant, dipped in the blood water of Carl's Emberus shrine. Against vampires, he says, they act like napalm.

beats.headline: Napalm to vampires
beats.text: As Carl heads out to Miriam Dom, Mordecai calls wait, hops sideways into the crafting room and comes back with two potion balls in his small arms. He dips them in the red water of the Emberus shrine at the back of the room and hands them over. The system labels them Holy Goopers. Blessed water mixed with a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant, Mordecai explains: Emberus is a light-based god, and the shrine's blood water with a healing potion and the coagulant acts like napalm to vampires. Hit them with this, then have Donut max out her Torch spell. So they're holy water grenades, Carl says. Cool. Exactly.

beats.headline: Against Sierra's talons
beats.text: Sierra has Carl in her twin talons, one round his legs and one round his chest, trying to pull him apart like a hot mozzarella stick. A magic missile hits her wing. Carl casts Heal and pulls the Holy Gooper into his free hand, smashing the sticky holy water against the talon on his chest. The foot sizzles, and she only crushes harder. He pulls his second and last as the new sun comes up and Donut emerges from the canopy. The throw misses when the boss rears back from the light, but her head bursts into flames anyway, and she tosses him straight up into the sky.

beats.headline: Clearing the way
beats.text: Before the cemetery, Carl moves a few of Mordecai's holy gooper grenades to the ready position, though he has only six of them, along with healing potion smoke curtains he has not yet tested. The mobs swarm. The saferoom is that way, Donut cries, pointing through a mass of creatures, and Carl tosses a holy gooper and clears the way, then another curtain to keep the path open. None of her psionic attacks work on these things, she shouts.

relations.note: dipped in his shrine's water

tagline.text: Miriam Dom left over forty scrolls of something called Size Up in the pile of everything she owned, and Carl takes two where Prepotente cannot see.
Prepotente knows Carl took Size Up scrolls from his mother's pile, and he asks for five fine healing potions as payment.
Donut drinks a Size Up potion before the race and reads off Osvaldo's dexterity with all his buffs, his abilities and the levels of his skills.

beats.headline: Two of forty
beats.text: Miriam Dom is a pile of dust, and beside it stands a stack of everything she owned, dumped from her inventory because she feared turning to dust would make her body unlootable. She was right. She told Carl he could take a few items for helping her, and he promised it would all go to Prepotente. He intends to keep that promise. Mostly. Among the potions and plants are over forty scrolls of something called Size Up. He walks out of Prepotente's sight and takes two. As the second goes into his inventory, his interface flickers, and the number 50 slams into place.

beats.headline: Payment for the scrolls
beats.text: Prepotente needs at least five more fine healing potions for the recipe his benefactor box just sent him. Carl has about fifty and says he has a few. Give them to me, says the goat: consider it payment for the Size Up scrolls you stole from my mother. Carl pauses, then asks to hear what is on the paper first, and once he has, hands over five potions without further complaint.

beats.headline: A look at Osvaldo
beats.text: While they wait, Donut downs a Size Up potion and watches the back of Osvaldo's head. Then she reports. His dexterity is really high, 285 with all his buffs. He has a Deflector ability, and his Jump skill is level fifteen. Carl asks about Puddle Jump or Phase: he has Puddle Jump, but only at level eight, which means a ten-second countdown.

beats.headline: Protected from examination
beats.text: In the Desperado Club's casino the croupier is level 120 and an Enforcer, his examination full of redactions, a much higher level than Carl expected. Carl tells Donut to take a Size Up and asks anyone else with examination skills to let him know what they see. Donut reports back that he is protected from the examination.

tagline.text: A legendary benefactor box gives Prepotente a vintage-style spray applicator and a recipe for a herbicide. The mix of fine healing, blessed water and weedkiller only works when his new magical canister turns it into a very fine mist.

beats.headline: A pump and a tin can
beats.text: Prepotente spends his wand's tiny three-minute safe space opening his loot boxes, which Carl thinks is a waste. Ten seconds before it closes, his legendary benefactor box gives up two items. One looks like a handheld bicycle pump with a tin can welded under the nozzle; Donut says it is like one of Bea's perfume bottles, and Carl recognises a sprayer for putting herbicide on a garden. The other is a piece of paper. Prepotente wants five fine healing potions from Carl, payment for the Size Up scrolls Carl stole from his mother, and Carl makes him tell what is on the paper first: fine healing, blessed water and a weedkiller, applied as a very fine mist through the new canister.

beats.headline: Mordecai builds on it
beats.text: A System message: another Odious Creeper has fallen, credit to Crawler Prepotente, forty remain. That is his third, says Carl. On the counter, Mordecai has four moonshine jugs of his own weedkiller, built on what Prepotente said and what he received: a weedkiller designed to take out an odious bloom, with several anti-undead boosts added, like the holy grenade he once made for Carl.

entities.name: Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition

tagline.text: Uncle Morty's is Mordecai's weedkiller for the Odious Creepers, an existing weedkiller for an odious bloom with anti-undead boosts added: four moonshine jugs of it, each enough for two or three creepers. It is very flammable, and if it burns before the monster absorbs it, it does not work.
Poured into the little cup on the elven rock chucker's sling, Uncle Morty's goes out with a three-hundred-pound rock and brings a creeper down in seconds.

beats.headline: Four jugs on the counter
beats.text: Katia asks whether Mordecai made the stuff. Four moonshine jugs of bubbling yellow liquid sit on the counter, one almost as big as he is, labelled Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition. He took a weedkiller designed to take out an odious bloom and added anti-undead boosts. Each jug has enough for two or three, maybe four. Louis's Tent the House ability spreads a potion over a wide area, but he must use it at maximum distance: the stuff is very flammable, and if it catches fire before it is absorbed, it will not work. Carl takes two jugs, Louis the other two.

beats.headline: Into the sling cup
beats.text: Carl's delivery system was over-engineered. The venomous elven rock chucker taken from the Dream hunters has a Poison Cloud enhancement, and a potion poured into the little cup on the side of the sling changes the poison. A mile short of the creeper, in the mud and rain, Donut climbs a tree to watch. Carl adds the poison, hits the lever, and a rock flies. You hit it perfectly, says Donut; the green stuff is getting all messed up by the rain. Mordecai said that would help. A few seconds after that, the notice comes: a creeper has fallen, credit to Crawler Princess Donut. Thirty remain.

relations.note: built on what Prepotente received

tagline.text: The smallest of the four nipple rings Carl pulled out of the hunter Iota, about the size of a nickel, worth plus ten and another five percent to constitution. Donut wears it in the top right, for a price.

beats.headline: One does not pierce cats
beats.text: It's not going to happen, Donut says: does she look like some sort of sex pervert? It gives plus ten and an additional five percent to her constitution, Carl says, and it is the smallest of the four; it will hide in her fur and probably shrink once attached. She will have to attach it manually the first time, and one does not pierce the nipples of cats; that is how one gets a visit from the ASPCA. Why doesn't he wear it himself? He is, Carl says, a bigger one. Of the four rings off Iota, two are for selling, the third gives Quarter Fall, and the fourth is this constitution ring, about the size of a nickel.

beats.headline: Bought with a sponsor prize
beats.text: A sponsor's note has just told Carl to give his new Pawna's Cries potion to Donut and keep it secret. If she puts the nipple ring on, he says, she gets his sponsor prize. She licks her lips. Mordecai looks about to speak, and Carl gives him a slight no. Donut agrees, if he goes first and they don't tell Katia. He shoves the needle through his left nipple. I don't think I can respect you anymore, Donut says, and an achievement arrives, Sex Pervert, whose reward is that whores don't get rewards. He searches her belly for a nipple. Not that one: up higher, on the other side. The top right. Okay, Carl says, he is going to count to three.

beats.headline: Was the bribe a trick
beats.text: Don't let that nipple ring fool you, Donut tells Bautista: Carl doesn't get very many girls. Then Elle and Imani report benefactor boxes from the Apothecary, also for Donut, and Donut starts to think the nipple ring bribe was a trick, and that Carl was directed to give her that potion all along.

beats.headline: One, two, stab
beats.text: Donut is still on about it, days after. Once trust is broken it can never be replaced, she tells Carl: if someone says they are going to count to three, one expects them to actually count to three, not to stab willy-nilly into one's body without warning. She didn't get to prepare herself.

tagline.text: Pawna's Cries adds three to any spell or skill and has a limited shelf life, so it must be taken before the end of the floor. It comes with a note telling Carl to give it to Donut in secret, and he hands it over as her price for wearing a nipple ring.
Donut drank Pawna's Cries before the Masquerade and took her Laundry Day spell from nine to twelve.

description.text: Pawna's Cries. This potion has a limited shelf life. This potion adds plus three to any spell or skill of your choosing.

beats.headline: Save the toraline
beats.text: Carl's benefactor box holds a familiar, valuable potion: Pawna's Cries, plus three to any spell or skill, limited shelf life, which means it must be taken before the end of the floor. His Pawna's Tears does the same at plus five, with no limit. This one comes with a note, which is unusual: Save the toraline. Notes are expensive, says Mordecai, and the rules force you to be cryptic. Then Carl's Escape Plan skill buzzes and more words appear. Circe sponsored Diwata. Give potion Donut. Need 15, but make it a secret. Prepotente, Imani and Samantha at the same time, or the other Pawna potion. Will replace.

beats.headline: The price of a nipple ring
beats.text: Donut will not wear the smallest of Iota's nipple rings, plus ten constitution and five percent more, so Carl takes out his new potion. Put it on, he says, and she gets his sponsor prize. You never give up your prizes, says Donut. She is almost at twelve in Magic Missile, Carl tells her, so in a few days she can use it to top that off. Mordecai looks as if he is about to say something, and Carl gives him a very slight no.

beats.headline: One more for Donut
beats.text: Mordecai stands over a table of five items from Apothecary sponsorship boxes, each given to a different crawler with a note saying it should go to Donut, and he has never seen anything like it. Carl's Pawna's Cries, from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, was meant for her too, and so was the I Take It All Back potion given to Prepotente. Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a box not meant for Donut.

beats.headline: Nine to twelve
beats.text: Laundry Day, the armour-removing spell Carl has had Donut training every day for weeks, has to reach fifteen. She got it to nine on her own. Just before the party, Carl finally made her take the Pawna's Cries potion, which she secretly used to raise the spell three levels, to twelve. The note said to boost the rest with Prepotente, Imani and Samantha, but no spell or buff could be coaxed out of Samantha, and she is gone anyway. So Donut drinks Carl's more powerful Pawna's Tears, which his sponsor claims he will replace, and before the god she casts Laundry Day.

relations.note: the stronger potion Carl already holds

tagline.text: The third of the four nipple rings Carl pulled from the hunter Iota imbues its wearer with Quarter Fall, a falling speed a quarter of normal. Carl puts it through his own left nipple.
When the Sledge counts down the last five seconds, Carl does not trust his nipple ring's fall ability and drinks a Feather Fall potion as well.

beats.headline: Through the left nipple
beats.text: Of Iota's four nipple rings, two hold any real value. The biggest gives plus five to Drink Mixing, for bartenders; the next shows an item's average selling value; both are for selling. Carl groans at the third, because he will pretty much have to wear it: a glowing gold ring the size of a half dollar that imbues Quarter Fall, a fall at a quarter of the normal speed. Not a pleasant landing, but a survivable one, and better than the half-splat potions. Donut will wear the smallest ring only if he does his first, so he shoves the needle through his left nipple. New Achievement! Sex Pervert!

beats.headline: A fall ability, not trusted
beats.text: The Recital quest completes, and the Sledge sends his last message: five seconds, good-bye. All around them is blood and carnage and death. Carl meets Donut's eyes and shouts for potions. He has his nipple ring's fall ability, but he does not trust it, so he drinks a Feather Fall potion as well. Then the world goes vroom, and everything freezes.

relations.note: taken from the same hunter

entities.name: Satchel Bomb
entities.role: A bag that levels a town

tagline.text: Satchel bombs are little bags with leather handles that Carl can toss and set off with the power of three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite, enough to level a small town. An Odious Creeper's boss box gives him a bunch.
Carl has been making his own satchel bombs in his bomber's studio, safe for regular crawlers to handle, and now they go on the market.

beats.headline: Good, but not unique
beats.text: Carl's regular loot boxes are uninteresting, including the boss box from the one Odious Creeper they killed. It gives him a bunch of satchel bombs: basically little bags with leather handles that he can toss and detonate with the power of three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite, which is enough to level a small town. It is a good prize, but it is not anything unique.

beats.headline: Stock for the market
beats.text: Carl messages Elle, Katia, Donut, Li Na and Mordecai: spread the word, everyone has to stop fighting each other. Whoever has lost keys should clear the stairwell chambers of debris, isolate them fast, blow up what is around them and tunnel underneath with Build Trench scrolls, room enough for a whole party. Mordecai is to go into Carl's bomber's studio, take the pile of satchel bombs and put them on the market to help people with the demolition. Carl has been making them for the next floor, so they are safe for regular crawlers to handle.

entities.name: I Take it All Back Potion

tagline.text: A black, bubbling potion that removes any effect of Scolopendra's Transmutation spell, given to Prepotente in a benefactor box and handed on to Donut with a tag: use it when the time is right, and do not give it to Tina.
Burst over Kiwi in the middle of the castle battle, the potion turns the raptor pack leader back into an ursine, and Tina knows her mother.

description.text: I Take it All Back - Potion This will remove any effects of Scolopendra's Transmutation spell.

beats.headline: A package for Donut
beats.text: Prepotente screams in Elle's face, announces that he is here to deliver a package, and puts a black, bubbling potion on the table in front of Donut. He received it in a benefactor box and cannot fathom why his sponsor would give him something intended for her. Then he leaves, and Bianca screeches outside. It is the second benefactor item given to somebody else for Donut. A tag hangs off the top like a label on a Christmas present: Give this to Princess Donut. Use when the time is right. Do NOT give to Tina. Carl tells Donut not to use it until he says so, and not to tell Signet, who would want it for Grimaldi.

beats.headline: Bubbles on Kiwi
beats.text: Imogen snaps Carl's arm, Sir Ferdinand slams into her head and she backhands him away, and Carl heals himself. Kiwi, Donut calls from the stage, come here, lower your head. She grasps one of the paper bubbles on the back of Kiwi's neck with two paws and squeezes, and the potion ball hidden inside bursts just as Big Tina reappears on stage. The effect is instantaneous. Kiwi staggers and stands, no longer a dinosaur but an ursine, naked but for the remaining paper bubbles. The other raptors roar as one and their dots turn red. Tina roars, then roars again, and the third time it sounds almost like words. The fourth: Mom? Mommy?

relations.note: Scolopendra's Transmutation spell

tagline.text: Bautista has a line of about a hundred stuffed slate butterflies from his sponsor's sample box. They are harmless: summoned, one flies to the nearest light and sucks the energy out of it.
Britney's jacket is made of stuffed slate butterflies, and one pull on a tag sends one up to drain the warning light in the Masquerade's ballroom.
The lightning found the cloud of butterflies from Britney's jacket and blew it apart over everyone's heads.

description.text: Stuffed Slate Butterfly Figure. (With tags.) The slate butterfly is one of the more common figures in Jaxbrin's newest lineup. The tragic story of the butterflies who accidentally killed all their fairy friends is a beloved fairytale. It's also based loosely on a true story, which is no surprise considering how parents just love to romanticize mass-casualty events.

beats.headline: A hundred harmless moths
beats.text: Bautista has a line of about a hundred gray and brown fuzzy moth or butterfly beanies. They came from his sponsor, but not in a benefactor box: he was pulled out of the dungeon to film a commercial and stole the sample box at the end of the session. Been there, says Carl. Bautista has tried them just once. They're harmless, he says. They don't attack. They just fly to the closest light source and suck the energy out of it. You can have one. You can have five.

beats.headline: The warning light
beats.text: Britney's whole jacket is made of the stuffed butterflies; she wanted them on her boots, but Carl liked having a ton at the ready. Mordecai says their ability is not considered magic, which is why they beat Carl's idea of smuggling in his slingshot. While Vrah threatens Carl, Britney pretends to drop something, the guard looks down, and she pulls a tag. A hand-sized butterfly flies straight up to the warning light, wraps it in its wings and drains it dark. Then it is a stuffed animal again, bounces off the tip of the elf's spear and lands in her hand.

beats.headline: It does not flash
beats.text: Up on stage Elle and Imani finish, and every crawler in the ballroom is unmuted, no longer peace-bonded and able to reach their inventory again. All around the room, crawlers look about. The warning light that would have let the guards and Imogen know about the change does not flash, and Carl's people spread out telling everyone to keep their mouths shut.

beats.headline: A cloud of stuffing
beats.text: Imogen's health is almost gone and the lightning is coming. Your jacket, Carl shouts at Britney, and tosses a hobgoblin disco ball against the queen's head, meaning the butterflies to seek it out and overwhelm her. Instead the lightning comes out as a single bolt, drawn to the spreading clump of butterflies, and the summoned creatures explode barely ten feet overhead. Donut, Mongo, Britney and Carl go flying in different directions. Flaming bits of stuffing fall everywhere like embers.

tagline.text: Cracker Jack is a rare scroll that frees gear locked to its original owner, the usual guard on benefactor box items. Nobody Carl knows has one.
Carl has three Cracker Jack scrolls from his trade with Orren, enough to free three of the locked items taken off hunters.

beats.headline: Gear that will not change hands
beats.text: Most of what the hunters carry is restricted to the hunter. Florin took out two Goriffs, blue aliens with antennae like twin elephant trunks, and has their pulse rifles and electric armour, but he cannot equip them. Donut's sunglasses carry the same restriction, as Louis learned when he tried them on. Mordecai says it is a common addition to benefactor box items, to keep players from murdering the recipients for their gear. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack can free an item, but nobody they know has one. They collect everything anyway.

beats.headline: Three, for a bin
beats.text: Orren means to take a plastic bin of loot back from Carl, for its communicator and Valtay upgrade pills, while Quasar argues caselaw. Carl does not care. He offers to trade for the bin, and Orren warns that the AI's value on it may disappoint; Carl just wants to finish the floor. For the homeless man's dirty clothes and a few Valtay items he receives a single wand recharge scroll, three scrolls called Cracker Jack, and leave to keep the four cretins for the ninth floor. Orren will not give back the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: Two shields unlocked
beats.text: Carl spends two of the three Cracker Jack scrolls on a pair of alien shields from the pile of tech looted from hunters, unusable until unlocked. His is a Valtay Perso-Shield, Platinum Edition, a pinback button like the planet Saturn, identical to the one he would have had from Paulie. Donut's is the Bull Rush, a longhorn pin from Hereford War Machines. Neither has been tested in a real fight yet.

beats.headline: Not for the guns
beats.text: Most of the guns they have looted are user locked, and unlocking one would waste a precious Cracker Jack scroll. The bigger guns carry no such restriction, so those sit in the fortified bunkers along the line, made of a composite concrete different from the castle's and almost impenetrable, while the earthworks teams work underfoot.

tagline.text: Spider Stalkers are rat-sized robot spiders built from one of the recipes Carl took from Dr. Ratchet's manual. Each can be programmed with a target and armed to explode.
Carl carries fifteen spider automatons. Ten are armed with regular explosives, and the rest he can arm with a holy grenade or a healing potion against the undead.
The spider automatons carry the anchor halves of Carl's teleport traps on their flat tops, so he can teleport to wherever one of them is.

beats.headline: Twenty out of the bag
beats.text: Carl finally finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers, which are really just robot rot stickers, a pretty common mob. Their main driveshaft is rare and expensive, and he secures a case on his way out of the Desperado Club. On the raid, Donut is to do the honors. He pours twenty rat-sized automaton spiders from a bag; they roll out like spilled tennis balls, sprout legs and line up. Each exploding one is programmed with a target, Hunter Not Already Targeted, so any kill goes to Donut. Two more he sets on Samantha: explode five seconds after target acquired.

beats.headline: Seekers into the rain
beats.text: You, and you, and you, Donut says, tapping each seeker spider on the head, and they scuttle off into the rain. Samantha rolls off toward the town exit, and on Carl's word Donut taps the last two, and they chase her: the anti-air gun has an anti-seeking enchantment, and the indestructible head is the workaround. Explosions rip through the night as the seekers find targets, and the gun goes up in a red geyser. When it is over, a few spiders walk in circles, unable to find a target. They will run out of power in a few minutes, and Carl will have to collect them and recharge them at his table.

beats.headline: Guts out on the counter
beats.text: Little Bonnie the gnome sits on the counter, humming to herself as she pries the guts out of a disarmed spider automaton. Carl's eyes catch her as he weighs taking the stairs and avoiding what comes next. We need her and the rest of them, he thinks, if we want to survive the ninth floor.

beats.headline: Fifteen, ten already armed
beats.text: Before going in against the undead, Carl readies several of his spider automatons and moves a few of Mordecai's holy gooper grenades to the ready position. He has fifteen spiders, but ten of them are already armed with regular explosives, which makes them useless if the mobs are non-corporeal. The others he can arm with a holy grenade, or just a straight healing potion.

beats.headline: A mouse trap for an elephant
beats.text: With Minge tearing the club apart, Carl dives behind a kitchen station and pulls spider robots from his automaton menu, saved for an emergency: one utility spider and three anti-undead ones begun in the ghommid village. He puts a demon snare in the first one's trap slot and ups its yield. All three automatons reach the demon and activate. The snare, fixed to the spider's top, only attaches the spider to her bulk, and it detonates, splashing her with blood water from Emberus's shrine, while the other two set off holy-water smoke curtains. At level 225 she will not be badly hurt, but it will hurt like hell.

beats.headline: Seekers in the Prism
beats.text: Inside the Prism's headquarters, Carl drops hunter seeker automatons on the floor, and they scatter off into the small castle. Empress D'Nadia sends her three guards out of the throne room the moment they approach. The one Saccathian hides behind the other off-worlder, a gnoll, as the explosive spider automatons close in, and both off-worlders are splattered over the wall before the party arrives. The samurai rhino casts a powerful shield, but the concussions knock him out for ten minutes.

relations.note: she activates them, so the kills are hers
two spiders chase her to the anti-air gun
she takes a disarmed one apart

tagline.text: A new tiara for Donut, one of five gifts from the Apothecary laid out on a table before the Butcher's Masquerade. Unlike the hammer and the stick, its purpose is clear.
Once on Donut's head, the tiara doubles her charisma for thirty hours and then dissolves: her base of 138 becomes a god-like 276, before the saferoom buffs.
The tiara doubled Donut's charisma through the masquerade, and it is lost in the battle that ends it.

beats.headline: No hidden seven
beats.text: Of the five Apothecary items on the table, all meant for Donut, Carl understands three: a recharge wand scroll, a sheet of music and a new tiara. It is the stick and the hammer that puzzle him, and each carries a hidden seven. He checks the others. The scroll has no symbol that he can find, and neither does the tiara or the sheet music. That makes sense, he thinks. Their purpose is clear.

beats.headline: Good with the dinosaurs
beats.text: The caravan is escorting the party to the castle, and new guards in black jackets keep coming. Carl tells Donut to keep Tina under control: they have waited long enough, so put the new tiara on. She already has, Donut replies, and it has helped a lot with the dinosaurs, but the guards are still agitated, probably because of the lady in the last cart.

beats.headline: Ugly, and temporary
beats.text: At the castle, Donut complains that her charm upgrade is not working on the high elves. It is working fine, Carl tells her: these elves think the party is beneath them, and someone has left them with a negative opinion, so the fact they are talking at all is a sign. He is only bummed it is not permanent. This tiara is ugly anyway, Donut says. But don't tell the Apothecary lady she said so.

beats.headline: Two hundred and seventy-six
beats.text: Donut's unenhanced charisma sits at 138, and the benefactor-box tiara on her head doubles it, to a god-like 276 before the saferoom buffs. Once placed, it only lasts thirty hours before it dissolves. According to Mistress Tiatha, an NPC fawns over a crawler when the crawler's charisma beats the NPC's constitution and charisma together, by a hundred points for a province boss, which is what Ferdinand is. His total is 175. Donut is 101 over, and with her buffs and the Seize the Day Toothpaste, her effective charm is well over 300.

beats.headline: All eyes on her
beats.text: The spotlight narrows on Donut alone on stage, her tiara glittering. She does not take out her sheet music, because she does not need it. She sings a song her mother used to sing to her, All Eyes on Me, with Britney on guitar backstage. It is a charm spell that focuses everyone's attention on a subject of the caster's choosing, and with Donut's insane charisma it catches the whole room, the queen and Carl included. Only Signet seems unaffected.

beats.headline: Elves in love
beats.text: Atop Mongo and matted with gore, Donut is giddy. She was wrong about her charisma not working: her love vampire skill works really well when it is this high. Behind her, elves wade through the fray with little heart icons over them. It does not work on the bugs. We need to get her charisma that high permanently, Carl thinks.

beats.headline: Gone in the battle
beats.text: After the fight, sticky with blood, Donut asks Carl why it does not hurt as much as it should, and she circles once and settles into the crook of his arm, the way they used to so long ago. Running his hand across her bloody, matted head, Carl realizes her temporary, charisma-gaining crown is gone, lost in the battle. She has taken off her sunglasses, too.

tagline.text: A ball peen hammer small enough to fit in Carl's hand, sent by the Apothecary through Imani with a note that it is for Donut. Its description says it is magical and does nothing magical, and a seven is pressed into its wooden handle.
In Prepotente's hand, the hammer gives the Stick of Cascadia's Screams one very tiny tap in the glass wall of the seventh floor's starting chamber, and the whole level shatters.

description.text: Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward. This is a small hammer. It's enchanted. That means it's magical. It just doesn't do anything magical.

beats.headline: Borant appealed, and lost
beats.text: Five hours before the Butcher's Masquerade, five Apothecary sponsorship boxes sit on one table, given to five different crawlers, all with notes saying they belong to Donut. Imani's held a ball peen hammer that fits in Carl's hand, and she was told Borant had filed a dangerous appeal to keep it from arriving, an appeal immediately denied. The box was only silver. Why give it to Donut, Carl asks, when she cannot even use it: is she supposed to hold it in her mouth? Mordecai has seen it before. Some items are enchanted with no properties, which lets them be used against things like ghosts. After finding a seven on the stick, Carl looks at the hammer again, and along its wooden handle is another.

beats.headline: One very tiny tap
beats.text: Five minutes on the timer in the seventh floor's starting chamber. Prepotente asks Donut for the hammer and the magical stick, lays them on the ground by the back wall and goes to a knee; he still does not understand why they were given to her and not him. When the countdown has dropped to zero and the stick is halfway into the glass, he picks up the hammer and whispers that he is a good, smart boy. He gives the stick a very tiny tap. A lightning pattern of fissures spreads across the wall. Then every wall of the level shatters into fine dust.

tagline.text: A ten-inch metal rod that looks like aluminium, sent by the Apothecary through Dmitri Popov for Donut. It is not a wand, its description says, but used correctly it can do something truly magical, and a seven is pressed into one end.

Pushed halfway into the glass wall of the seventh floor's starting chamber and tapped with the hammer, the stick cracks the wall, and the whole level shatters while Cascadia screams over the announcement system.

description.text: Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams. This is a stick. It's enchanted. It's not a wand, but when used correctly, it can do something truly magical.

beats.headline: Not a wand
beats.text: Dmitri Popov was ridiculously excited to finally meet Donut and hand his gift over, and unlike Imani he got no notice of an appeal. It is a metal rod about a quarter of an inch thick and ten inches long, apparently aluminium, though its description does not say, and from that description it seems connected to the hammer. Who's Cascadia? Carl asks. Mordecai shrugs: this kind of thing is usually named after past crawlers, bosses or places, and of the few Cascadias he can think of, only one is connected to the crawl. Then Carl's finger catches a slight imperfection at the end of the rod. It feels like a symbol. He thinks it is the number seven.

beats.headline: Prepotente has been collecting clues
beats.text: At the masquerade Carl asks Prepotente when he last slept, and the goat insists on joining his party. Carl says no: talk to Katia, or start a party of his own and join the guild. It would only be for the rest of this floor, Prepotente says, so that they travel together to the start of the next. He has been collecting the clues, and Katia has told him about Donut's magical hammer and stick. Then a voice booms from the stage, Prepotente screams right in Carl's ear, and Carl bookmarks the whole thing until they are through the party.

beats.headline: Through the glass like magic
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente explains himself. The level is built like a Prince Rupert's drop on a massive scale, and it is called the Great Race, which is also the name of a fairytale about a boy in a maze whose tunnels seal behind him. He asks Donut for the hammer and the magical stick and holds a thermometer to the glass; the whole tale, he says, is in the description of his mother's boots. He splashes a potion on the wall. When the countdown hits zero and Cascadia rushes through the rules, he pushes the stick into the wet spot, and it slides through like magic. Godsdamnit, Prepotente, Cascadia says. Don't do it. The stick stops halfway.

beats.headline: The whole level breaks
beats.text: One tiny tap of the hammer, and a lightning pattern of fissures runs over the glass. Interesting, Prepotente says, his voice gone distant: he thought it would be instantaneous. Then the wall shatters, and not just that wall. The entire level explodes into fine dust, every crawler is sucked into the portals at the same time, and Carl and Donut flip head over toes into the stairwell. The last thing Carl hears is Cascadia screaming over the announcement system. He broke the whole level, Donut says in the marble chamber. All their sponsors came together to make sure he pulled it off, Carl answers.

relations.note: Dmitri brought it

tagline.text: Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a benefactor box not meant for Donut. It held a small knit beanie that raises all her stats by three percent and gives her a spell, I Need My Personal Space, which knocks everyone around her back with a powerful blow, her own party included.
In the fight in the pit where the castle stood, Katia takes the beanie off her own head and puts it on Carl's, so that he can clear a way through the nymphs and get Donut close to the god.

beats.headline: The one box not for Donut
beats.text: Mordecai has never seen anything like it. Five items sit on the table, all from Apothecary sponsorship boxes, all given to different crawlers, all with notes saying they should go to Donut, and that is not counting Carl's Pawna's Cries or Prepotente's I Take It All Back, both meant for her too. Of everyone the Apothecary sponsors, only Katia got a box not meant for Donut: a small knit beanie, three percent to all her stats down the line, and a spell called I Need My Personal Space. It violently knocks everybody back, party members included. She puts it on, and it sinks into her mass and disappears.

beats.headline: Off her head, onto his
beats.text: Katia has to go back and help against Imogen, and Carl has already spent his Protective Shell. A fifteen-foot mountain of bugs, some still alive, stands between him and the deity hiding in the corner. Katia pulls the beanie off her head and puts it on his, where it equips itself with a little beep: use the spell to clear through the nymphs, get Donut close enough. At the top of the hill a group of bugs lunges at him. He casts I Need My Personal Space, and it pushes them all in different directions, like a miniature Protective Shell. Mongo and Donut jump in, and they land before the god.

entities.name: Wand Recharge scroll
entities.role: A scroll that brings a wand back

tagline.text: A recharge wand scroll is one of five Apothecary gifts that arrive in sponsorship boxes given to other crawlers, each with a note saying it is meant for Donut. Carl understands what this one is for.
On the Masquerade stage, Donut casts the recharge scroll on the dead wand in Big Tina's hand, and the wand glows back to life.
Carl gets another wand recharge scroll from Orren, in a trade that also brings him three Cracker Jack scrolls.
Carl keeps his rare Wand Recharge scroll in his inventory, in case the shrink wand ever runs out of charges.

beats.headline: Five boxes meant for Donut
beats.text: Five hours before the Butcher's Masquerade, Carl and Mordecai stand over a table of five items, all from the Apothecary in sponsorship boxes given to different crawlers, all with notes saying they should be given to Donut. Mordecai has never seen anything like it. One is a recharge wand scroll. That one Carl understands, he says, and the tiara and the sheet music too. What he cannot work out is the stick, or the ball peen hammer he picks up next.

beats.headline: Readable from the stage
beats.text: Carl's planning notes for the castle set out how the stage works. When Donut stands on the stage in ballroom A, she can physically handle the items moved to the stage of the attendant ballroom a few stories below: a wand there can be picked up and cast while it stays three floors down. She will be able to read the wand-recharge scroll and her sheet music if she needs them. The one thing she cannot do is drink something that is not with her, so the charm potion has to be smuggled in.

beats.headline: Big Tina's wand glows
beats.text: Donut's song has charmed the room, and Britney has started a faster, baroque piece with the spotlight on Big Tina at the centre of the stage, her pink boa round her neck and her inert wand in her hand. As everyone watches, the wand glows: Donut has just cast the recharge scroll on it. The dinosaur looks at it with wonder and waves it, and sparkles dance through the air. It casts a charm as well, a performer's trick called The Recital, which makes everyone happy to be there and wanting to watch the stage.

beats.headline: A second one, from Orren
beats.text: Carl's inventory is back on, and he has made the exchange with Orren without even looking into the bin. For the homeless man's dirty clothes and a few Valtay items he receives a single wand recharge scroll, three scrolls called Cracker Jack, and Orren's agreement to let them keep the four cretins for the ninth floor. Carl tries to get the Gate of the Feral Gods back as well. Orren refuses and will not budge.

relations.note: on the wand she carries
the second scroll, in a trade

tagline.text: A sheet of bard music in Chaco's prize case at the Butcher's Masquerade, priced at ten hunter hands. Chaco offers it when Mordecai asks for something like his own escape spell, though it is not quite as good, and Carl buys it for Donut.
Skedaddle is Donut's second way out of a fight after Puddle Jumper. With both, the party can jump twice, as long as she sings it in key.

beats.headline: Ten hands at Chaco's counter
beats.text: Over chat, Mordecai wants to know whether the prize counter has any sheet music like Chaco's own escape spell. Chaco looks up in surprise: Carl has a bard in his party? Can she hold pitch? He points at a sheet at ten hands, a song of Skedaddle, not quite as good as Wings of the Pyxie, which she could not sing for a while anyway. Sheet music sits somewhere between a scroll and a magic book. With it in front of her, the system helps a bard perform; sung badly the page tears a little, too many tears and it is ruined, and sung perfectly the song joins her repertoire. Carl adds it to his order.

beats.headline: Handy, in case of swarm
beats.text: Sister Ines wants to march straight into a fenced cemetery, and when Paz asks what if they get locked in, Donut points out that of course they will be: that is the whole purpose of the giant gate and fence. Once the nun agrees to circle the outside first, Carl tells Donut to keep the Skedaddle sheet music handy, and Puddle Jumper too. She already has, she says, but neither will let her leave if they are locked in. The place is big, Carl answers. Inside, they can use both to get away from a swarm, and with Skedaddle they can jump twice, as long as she sings it in key. What is that supposed to mean, Donut asks, when he called her masquerade performance flawless?

beats.headline: Not into Sheol fire
beats.text: Imani and Tran are trapped in a pocket below, Elle and the others are digging desperately through the rubble, and demons are coming up from both sides. Carl needs Donut to get rid of her deck, and asks whether she still has Puddle Jump available, to get everybody out. She still has Skedaddle as well, but Carl leaves that one alone: the escape spell would likely dump them all into a pile of Sheol fire.

aka.name: Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas

tagline.text: One of two Future Floor Boons in Chaco's prize case, thirty hunter hands apiece and one to a customer: a book of lore for the eighth floor, whose random starting location and full title reveal themselves on purchase. Carl buys it.

Its full title is Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas: a thin hardback under the Bahamas flag, full of the monsters there and their stats. Carl tells only Prepotente the title, and Donut picks somewhere else.
Donut chose Cuba, but the Bahamas book still earns its place on the eighth floor. Its index runs from Common to Unique, and Shi Maria is in it, among the uniques.

description.text: Eighth Floor Book of Lore – (Random starting location. Full title will reveal itself upon purchase)

beats.headline: Thirty hands, one each
beats.text: At thirty hands, Chaco's prize case has only two items, both Future Floor Boons, with a sign under them: limited to one each. One is a little checkered flag, Seventh Floor Pole Position, already sold out. Prepotente bought it, Chaco says; he was the first customer. The other is an Eighth Floor Book of Lore, its starting location random and its full title to be revealed upon purchase. Carl takes it, along with the shrink wand, the Skedaddle sheet music, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions.

beats.headline: Book of Lore – Something
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente wants the full title of the eighth-floor boon. Carl makes him explain what he is doing first, and the goat asks again: please, tell me its name. Carl pulls out a thin hardback, Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas, with the aquamarine and gold stripes and black triangle of the Bahamas flag on its cover and nothing else. Inside are descriptions and stats of monsters, and it falls open on an owl creature called the Chickcharney. The Bahamas? Donut says. That's where Miss Beatrice went for her vacation.

beats.headline: Twenty seconds at the globe
beats.text: Squad Leader Donut must spin a holographic globe and choose the eighth floor's starting location, and Carl has told nobody but Prepotente what his lore book covers. If the pole position boon is anything to go by, he tells her, the Bahamas book was designed to be really helpful, though he kind of wants the western United States, which they know. Donut wants Ibiza. With twenty seconds left Carl says go with the Bahamas: they have the lore book. Donut agrees, insists they are absolutely not going into the water this time, spins to the Caribbean and clicks. Goddamnit, Donut, Carl cries. That wasn't the Bahamas.

beats.headline: Somewhere close, obviously
beats.text: Throwing themselves right into the Bahamas was a bad idea, Donut explains in the empty hall, so as party leader she picked somewhere close. They gave Carl a book about the place Miss Beatrice was: it was quite obviously a trap. Its usefulness is painfully obvious, and Carl understands her logic, but she was wrong. Bea and her friends flew there on the twenty-sixth, after phase one would have moved them on, so they would never have seen their ghosts there; with a second location for phase two, the show has plenty of time to engineer a scene with her. Then Donut reports that Prepotente is in the Bahamas.

beats.headline: The index at the back
beats.text: Sister Ines's people lost a flag trying to tag one of the local mobs, and Carl pulls the Bahamas book out and flips to the index for the first time. Prepotente seemed to think there would be some overlap. There are a lot of ridiculous monsters listed, mixed in with some that sound terrifying, sorted as Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, Legendary, Mythic and Unique. There are lots of birds and bats and fish. He sees no monk seal listed. He puts it away to examine more closely another time.

beats.headline: Among the unique monsters
beats.text: Samantha's messages describe a spider lady she calls Shi Maria, who says she is looking for her husband and has fangs with a very lovely shimmer. Carl pulls out the Bahamas book, turns to the index and finds Shi Maria listed in a sub-index as one of a monster's alternate names, in the very last section, under unique monsters. He turns it to show Donut and Mordecai. Donut peers at the image of the screaming spider woman: that lady really needs moisturizer.

beats.headline: Just him and Bianca
beats.text: Donut has news from Prepotente: he wants Carl to read him a few chapters of that Bahamas book. He is all by himself there, and she thinks he is really lonely. He is not a member of any guild or the Desperado Club, and he is not allowed into Club Vanquisher anymore, so it is just him and Bianca, who is really nice but does not talk. They are moving toward Samantha, Carl answers, but it will be a few days before they get there; he will talk to Pony after.

beats.headline: An hour read to Pony
beats.text: On Donut's insistence, Carl spends a good hour reading directly from his Bahamas book and transcribing it into his notepad, copying it to the cookbook and to Prepotente in chat at the same time. The goat does not even thank him. He only answers when Carl asks whether the messages are arriving, and then only to point out a few typos in his translation.

beats.headline: La Ciguapa, asleep
beats.text: Mongo chomps to death a hairy woman with backward feet, asleep under a pile of foliage, before she fully wakes. She is La Ciguapa, and there is an entry on her in the Bahamas book: she lures opponents with charm and is hard to kill, except by familiars and pets. She is Legendary, so another is unlikely, which makes her a wasted opportunity for the deck. The good news is that she drops two cards.

relations.note: Carl reads it to him in chat

tagline.text: A shrink wand with ten charges, like the one Zhang used to have, is in the Masquerade's prize case, and Carl buys it with his hunter hands.
The shrink wand cannot be used on living flesh, so Carl uses it on a steel collar locked round a neck.
Carl's shrink wand has seven charges left after Zhang borrows it to bring down a church.

beats.headline: Bought with hunter hands
beats.text: Chaco the Bard runs the prize counter, and Carl has sixty-six hunter hands to spend. Among the twenty-hand items are spellbooks, wands and oddities: a drop shield, and a shrink wand like the one Zhang used to have, ten charges. Mordecai calls the wand a good choice too. Carl takes the shrink wand, the eighth-floor lore book, the sheet music for A Song of Skedaddle, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions. Everything bought arrives as a prize box, which can only be opened in a saferoom.

beats.headline: A collar, then a zap
beats.text: Carl has been saving the wand for armoured vehicles on the next floor, but the hydra's heads heal by breaking into pieces, and Carl is pretty sure the fire head is Bea's mom. The shrink wand cannot be used against living flesh. So he drives a snap collar, a frisbee of orcish steel, into her neck until it clicks shut, aims the wand at the collar with his left hand, and fires as a fireball forms in her mouth. The collar shrinks, the head flies away still screaming, and an achievement appears and goes.

beats.headline: Lent for a demolition
beats.text: Chris feels bad: the church across the way is pretty, and bringing it down will break the key. Carl tells him the real church is already gone, the key would only let one of them through, and the saferoom entrance can be protected if they do it right. Chris goes back to the church, where he, Zhang and several crawlers and strippers are to start a controlled demolition and build a channel underneath for the escape. Carl lends Zhang the shrink wand, since he has a lot of experience with that spell.

beats.headline: Two zaps, seven charges
beats.text: The Sheol fire finally starts to ease, and everywhere it touched there is nothing left. Chris and the others have been hard at work the whole time, making certain there is nothing directly above. Zhang messages that he only had to use two zaps on the wand, which leaves it with seven charges, and Carl also has a rare Wand Recharge scroll in his inventory if he ever runs out. Zhang returns the shrink wand as he and Chris go back to the saferoom.

entities.name: All Eyes on Me sheet music
entities.role: Donut's song for the talent show

tagline.text: Among the Apothecary's gifts for Donut was sheet music. On the Masquerade stage she sings All Eyes on Me, the song her mother used to sing to her, without taking her sheet music out, and the whole room falls under its charm.
All Eyes on Me normally takes a song, but Donut's charisma is now so high that she can cast it with spoken words.

beats.headline: She does not need it
beats.text: Donut stands alone on the stage in her little fake headset microphone, the charm potion already taken, and a spotlight narrows on her. My name is Princess Donut, she says. She does not take out the sheet music. She does not need it. She is singing a song her mother used to sing to her, and it is called All Eyes on Me. Backstage Britney strums the Popovs' guitar, a string missing, a sad minor strum, and Donut sings: good girl, good girl, you're a good girl, my princess.

beats.headline: All eyes on the stage
beats.text: She repeats the lyrics a few times, the same song a drunken Bea used to sing to her, moving slowly to the right of the stage, and her voice soars. The spell does exactly what its title says. Everyone in the room, hunters, crawlers and the queen among them, falls under a minor charm that fixes their attention on a subject of the caster's choice. Britney lets the last chord hang and starts a faster piece, and the spotlight re-forms on Big Tina. Everyone is affected, Carl included. Only Signet seems untouched.

beats.headline: Spoken, not sung
beats.text: Both Tigrans start screaming, and Nico tries to cover the oblivious pig's ears; it would not have mattered. Donut is casting All Eyes on Me, a spell that under normal circumstances requires a song. Her charisma is now so high that she can cast it with spoken words, and after just a few seconds of her talking, her listeners cannot keep their eyes off her. She uses it to tell Penelope and the tigers that they could all use some relationship advice.

relations.note: the song Bea used to sing to her

entities.name: Princess Lunette
entities.role: Signet's mother, as a body in Carl's inventory

tagline.text: Princess Lunette is an incomplete flesh golem: Signet's mother, or the memory of her given flesh, with the memory itself gone. Signet wants Carl to take the body, help Samantha and find a pulpmancer.
The body was a tattoo of a fish before Signet's final spell. Carl carries it in his inventory, waiting for a caster who can put Samantha into it.
Princess Lunette's heart and lungs are in Louis now. The body that was supposed to house Samantha went to save him instead.

beats.headline: Take the golem
beats.text: Signet is gone, and not all of her tattoos were warriors. Beside the crying boy Clint and Miss Nadine lies a naiad with her eyes closed as if sleeping: Signet's mother, or the memory of her given flesh. Princess Lunette. Incomplete Flesh Golem. Samantha pokes her with a burned head and calls her cousin. Nadine, breathless, says Signet wants Carl to take it; she took the memory with her and left just the body. Help Samantha. Find a pulpmancer. It weighs nothing and has no dot on the map. Carl pulls it into his inventory, and Samantha shoots off down a hole in the floor.

beats.headline: A body on the asphalt
beats.text: Samantha insists the spider in the trees can cast the spell that will put her into the golem. Carl pulls the body from his inventory, rigid as a board: a full-sized, pure naiad in a flowing dress of seaweed, smelling of brackish water, weightless, her silky white hair so long it reaches the pavement. Before Signet's final spell it was a tattoo of a fish. He lays it on the wet asphalt, and Samantha floats up, shaking with excitement. Shi Maria clicks and gestures at the body. She needs supplies first.

beats.headline: Good heart, good lungs
beats.text: Epitome Tagg is in Louis's heart and lungs, and when the soldiers take the Dream castle within the hour, Tagg will die and take Louis with him. Samantha knows how to save Louis. The flesh golem body in Carl's inventory, Princess Lunette, has a good heart and lungs; swap them out fast enough and he lives. Mordecai calls it a great idea. Edgar remembers that the body was his tattoo first, before Signet turned it into an incomplete flesh golem. Baroness Victory warns that it will not work outside the dungeon, and Louis will need an expensive deal to survive.

beats.headline: Heart and lungs out
beats.text: Carl dumps the body on a cot beside Louis. It is a slight, beautiful naiad, and it has gills, so Mordecai takes the kua-tin rebreather Carl looted from Loita. Imani and Rosetta open the golem up, and with Elle they hold its dripping heart and lungs up in a net. When Louis's heart stops, Bucket Boy yanks the old organs out, Imani places the new ones, Juice Box casts, and Mordecai sews the rebreather into the bronchial. The chest snaps shut. Louis coughs water from new gills and opens his eyes.

relations.note: the body meant to house her
his tattoo before it was Signet's spell

tagline.text: The Dart of Ophiotaurus is a priceless artifact Odette's crawlers spent half of the tenth floor hunting. Worship a god and use it on someone else, never yourself, and the god is summoned through them; the god's immunity does not start until five units after it forms.

beats.headline: A god through Uzzi
beats.text: Odette's crawlers spent half the tenth floor hunting the dart, only to learn the puzzle needed a storm god. They have summoned two, Dodola has sent the other away, the timer is running, and Mordecai has a plan that will kill him. Odette has another: worship Dodola, then use the dart. It cannot be used on oneself, and Hold Steady is keeping the puzzle primed, so it has to be Uzzi. Chaco worships Dodola. Uzzi looks down at the dart in his hand, caws a war cry and spreads his wings. Chaco throws it into his breast. Uzzi's chest rips open as Dodola forms inside Chaco's containment with the puzzle, which shatters into the key. Her own lightning ends her. Did they use the dart on his brother, Mordecai asks.

tagline.text: Every squad leader on the eighth floor gets twenty flags bearing a logo the system designed. Plant one in a living thing below five percent health and it becomes a T'Ghee totem; a lost flag is not replaced.
A flag only works in the hand. It has to be touching whoever shoves it in, so a flag tied to a crossbow bolt is simply lost.
A flag does not check what it goes into. It has turned a dying city boss into a card, and a dying crawler too.

beats.headline: Twenty flags, one logo
beats.text: The floor's announcement ends with a gift: each squad leader receives a set of twenty flags carrying the squad's logo, created by the system itself. Plant one in the body of a living entity below five percent health and it becomes something called a T'Ghee totem in the squad leader's inventory. Carl's breath catches; he knows the word from the Cookbook. Noncorporeal monsters count too, and a flagged monster becomes a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point. Lose the flags before the squad is full and they are not replaced.

beats.headline: Heart boxers on a stick
beats.text: The flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, the kind given to children to wave at a parade, and it is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways as if from a clothesline. A motorcycle-club patch is embroidered top and bottom: The Royal Court of Princess Donut. An embroidered bomb patch sits over the crotch. It is tacky. Elle's squad got a bag of adult diapers and Imani's a butterfly, Donut reports, and why could they not get something like that? Its pole is a glowing metal spike about a foot long, enchanted to stick into any creature, ghosts too, below five percent health.

beats.headline: A flag in his mouth
beats.text: Sister Ines's squad lost a flag tying it to a crossbow bolt: it has to be physically touching whoever shoves it in. So she hands Carl one of hers, Team Sister Ines on a blue field around a black-and-white embroidered blob that may be a ball and chain wearing a nun's habit, almost as dumb as his own. Carl carries it in his mouth into the fight with the monk seal, gets an arm caught, takes the flag out and stabs it into the side of the seal's head. Pling. The seal is a card, and it belongs to Team Sister Ines.

beats.headline: A flag in a god
beats.text: Carl comes to a decision. He pulls a flag and jumps at the dying Asojano just as his health starts to blink. The grass skirts are gone, and what is left is a pale, albino man, wide-eyed and afraid, half his face covered in festering boils. Carl shoves the flag into the top of his head, and Asojano puffs away into a card. A warning arrives: Carl has been infected with SlugPox. His momentum slams him into the wall.

beats.headline: Into Paz's neck
beats.text: Paz has asked to be let go, and he says goodbye. Sister Ines will not have it: he is not leaving her, everyone leaves her. She suddenly has a flag in her hand and jabs it into his neck, so fast that it does not occur to Carl to try to stop her. Whoom. Paz is a card.

relations.note: the Royal Court's flag is heart boxers

entities.name: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden
aka: Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden

tagline.text: The Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden is a glowing red ring from Princess Donut's Beguiler's box. It makes her impervious to natural fire and lava, strengthens her fire spells, and lets her cast a berserking spell called Bitch, What? once every thirty hours.

description.text: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden. This may only be equipped on a quadruped. This may only be equipped on a female. Warning: Unless you're planning on getting a lot of weird and unnecessary surgery, you ain't equipping this. All nipple rings must be manually affixed the first time they are equipped. Oh boy. Let me tell you about Superior fire demons. These bitches are crazy. Worse than the minor demons. I know, I know. That sounds chauvinistic and rude. You can't get away with saying shit like that anymore. Here's the thing. These bitches are godsdamned crazy. Full stop. …

beats.headline: From the Beguiler's box
beats.text: Carl laughs when Donut's Beguiler's box opens on a single shining nipple ring that glows red. This is not funny, Carl, she says. When she pulls it out, she calls it the most sexist description she has ever read. It may only be equipped on a female quadruped, and superior fire demons, the AI explains, are so crazy they must be chaperoned by hellspawn familiars, who use rings like this one. Worn, it allows the removal of cursed items, makes her impervious to natural fire and lava and resistant to fire spells, keeps her from losing health inside Sheol, and adds Intelligence per cent to every fire attack.

beats.headline: Bitch, What?
beats.text: Carl wants it on her right away. Mordecai agrees, but wants to talk about the spell first. Bitch, What? is a berserking spell, once every thirty hours: for twenty seconds Donut catches fire, is invulnerable to blunt damage, gets really angry and kills every goddamn thing in the room. Mordecai has seen it; the rage elemental lived in that state, and it is really called Fire Berserker. She is to cast it only when she is by herself. Her three fire spells, Fireball, Magic Missile and Wall of Fire, will all be much more intense. It is good, he says, but still not as good as her spellbook; and when Donut complains that she got no celestial box, he tells her the ring is practically a celestial.

beats.headline: Wall of Fire, bigger
beats.text: As the ghommids come out of the fog, Anton's crossbow makes little monkey noises each time he fires and Sister Ines lobs her white balls one after another. Donut casts Wall of Fire, and it crackles bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring. A pair of clockwork Mongos appear and tear through the mobs, and Carl tosses two infused smoke curtains.

beats.headline: Better than Carl's
beats.text: The Iowa area is about to crash to the ground, with maybe an hour to loot it. The cards and a lumpy leather bag hover in the middle of the burned trailer, still too hot to reach. Donut actually has better fire protection than Carl, thanks to her nipple ring, but they are both exhausted and do not want to risk it. They wait for the fire in the yard to calm.

entities.name: Tome of Legionnaires of the Damned

tagline.text: The Tome of Legionnaires of the Damned is a summoning spellbook from Princess Donut's De-Sleeving box, chained shut and wriggling. Its spell fills recently unequipped armour and weapons with wailing spirits that fight for the caster, and Donut learned it the moment she had it; the tome screamed as it went.
Legionnaires of the Damned is the second half of Donut's Phantasm move: Laundry Day blasts the armour off Bomo, and the spell fills every scrap of it with a screaming ghost.

description.text: Tome of Legionnaires of the Damned. Type: Summoning Spell. Cost: 25 mana Duration: (spell level*2 + intelligence level) seconds. Cooldown: One minute. May only have one active instance of this spell at a time. Target: May only be cast on recently-unequipped armor or weapons. Total targets allowed varies based on multiple factors. Effect: There are a lot of angry souls out there. Like, a lot. It's said if one has the ability to actually see all the wailing souls that filter through the edges of our world, one would go quite insane. …

beats.headline: Chained shut, and quivering
beats.text: Donut's De-Sleeving box holds 100,000 gold and a kind of spellbook Carl has never seen: thick as a dictionary, with a bumpy leather cover, chained shut with a lock, bouncing about on its own and giving off purple smoke. It reminds him of the spellbook in the Evil Dead movies, and Mordecai gasps. When Donut gives it an uncertain slap with her paw and asks why it is quivering, Mordecai says that happens sometimes with the more powerful tomes, especially summoning ones. In Carl's hands it is squishy and warm, and it wriggles like a puppy.

beats.headline: A little scream
beats.text: The spell reanimates weapons and armour with undead spirits plucked from the river of falling souls, and most of the gear disintegrates when it ends. Mordecai sees the combination at once: with Laundry Day at level fifteen, Donut can strip a group of mobs of their armour and turn it on them, full of wailing spirits. Carl slides the tome back to her. She glows as she applies it, and it lets out a little scream as it disappears in a puff of purple smoke.

beats.headline: The Phantasm move
beats.text: Donut casts Laundry Day on Bomo, and the armour Carl made for him at his armourer's table, dozens of metal pieces and trash-tier daggers sewn one by one onto a fabric undershirt, explodes off him like a fragmenting grenade. Then she casts part two, her new spell. A purple rent opens above the temple, dozens of wispy white ghosts pour down screaming into the scattered armour on the floor, and every piece starts to shake. It is working.

entities.name: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler

tagline.text: The Nipple Ring of the Defiler is a silver ring with an eyeball hanging from it, wearable only by a crawler a god has marked for death, which Carl is. It reads the religion of everyone nearby, lets him break shrines without divine fallout, adds a quarter to his damage against clerics and casts Black Nimbus once an hour.
Black Nimbus strips a worshipper of their god's blessing for a while. It takes away the god's protection, not the god's wrath.

description.text: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler This may only be equipped on a crawler who has been Marked for Death by a god. Hey, that’s you! All nipple rings must be manually affixed the first time they are equipped. Wearing this ring imbues the following effects: Instantly know the religious affiliation of all nearby mobs and crawlers. Allows the destruction of church shrines without further ill effects from deities. +25% damage against all clerics. The ability to cast Black Nimbus once an hour.

beats.headline: The apostate's box
beats.text: The platinum apostate box, earned for not getting killed by Diwata, holds a ring. A nipple ring. Donut is triumphant: now that his nipples are full, there are other places he is not pierced yet. It is silver, with an eyeball hanging from it, and only a crawler marked for death by a god may wear it. Li Na could already do everything it does. Its spell, Black Nimbus, pulls a target out of their deity's blessing and keeps them out of church. Lots of divinity-themed items, says Mordecai, and that is never good.

beats.headline: Black Nimbus on Anton
beats.text: Ogun has come for his two worshippers, Paz and Anton, and has eyes only for them. Carl's new ring came with Black Nimbus, which removes the benefits of worshipping a god, and maybe it would save them from a smite, but it reaches only one. He steps forward and casts it on Anton, then reads a Heal scroll on each man. A black crown forms over Anton's head, and the shunned mark disappears. The god turns, more curious than angry. A good attempt, he says: it has removed the man from his protection and his mercy, not from his wrath. He steps back onto Anton's head and crushes him.

tagline.text: The Prison Tattoo Kit is the same stick-and-poke gear Edgar the tortoise used on Tsarina Signet. Tattoos can carry all sorts of magical buffs and upgrades, and everything depends on the artist.
Katia has used the kit to tap a Desperado Club pass onto Samantha's neck, and the ink is already starting to fade.
Shi Maria has used the kit through Carl's own hands: its stick took Li Jun's eye, then tattooed an eye into Carl's chest.
With the right ink, the kit can put a skill into a crawler's skin. Katia is using it to tattoo a skill from Li Na's blood onto Carl's right arm.

description.text: Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit. So, you’re doing time. Hey, I’m not one to judge. You wonder, how did I get here? How did I mess my life up so much? You figure, now is the day I’m going to turn everything around. Now is the day I’m going to make certain I get on the right path. I’m gonna get out of here and get a job and make my family proud. Let me commemorate this important occasion by letting SkullFuck from the next cell come over and etch a poorly-drawn dragon on the side of my face. This kit allows an artist to create a tattoo of their choosing upon the skin of a willing or unwilling target. …

beats.headline: Stick and poke
beats.text: The Gold Quest Box for the Vengeance of the Daughter opens, and Carl recognises what comes out at once. Donut asks, with disgust, whether it is what she thinks. It is: a stick and poke tattoo kit, the same items Edgar the tortoise used to put magical tattoos on Tsarina Signet. A long, sharp needle, some ink, a few stick things, and something that looks like sandpaper. He has no idea how any of it works, and the description, about doing time, is no help. What is he supposed to do with this?

beats.headline: A pass on her neck
beats.text: At the Desperado's door, Clarabelle glares at Samantha: she has seen her on the recap plenty of times and never noticed the pass on her neck. Samantha hisses, snaps her teeth, and announces that she is going to kill Clarabelle's mother. Carl clamps her jaw shut with his arm and tells Clarabelle they just finished a quest where she killed someone, and they put the tattoo on her neck. It is disgusting, says Samantha, who hates tattoos more than she hates sushi. A gold coin, and Clarabelle waves them through.

beats.headline: The ink is fading
beats.text: Carl picks Samantha up in both hands and looks her in the eyes. She is covered in sand and gore, heavier than usual, with a slight vibration to her. The Desperado Club logo is still on her neck, where Katia tapped it with the poke and stick tattoo kit, but the ink is starting to fade. This is important, he tells her, so pay attention.

beats.headline: Through Carl's hands
beats.text: Combined with Shi Maria, Carl is a torso on a spider's body, and she is in control. She pulls the stick and poke kit from his inventory into his hands. When Li Jun slides down Li Na's chain to help, she has warned him: Carl jabs the stick into Li Jun's eye, licks the eye off and eats it. If he will not take her card to the next floor, she tells him, she will attach herself to something he cannot discard so easily. She dips the stick into the beaker and rapidly pokes a small tattoo into his bare chest, just above the sternum: an eye, which blinks, closes and disappears against his skin.

beats.headline: The right sleeve
beats.text: Katia sets a vial of ready-mixed ink on the table, and Carl puts the poke and stick kit beside it. Li Na is not mad at him, Katia says, only at herself for not protecting her brother. Her blood was freely given, so she lost five levels only for a while and can still use the skill; the tattoo itself is permanent. Carl has several tattoos on his left arm and none on his right, so the right sleeve it is. A level-13 skill needs a big one and almost all the ink. Rosetta says a properly themed tattoo lasts longer.

relations.note: the same tools he used on Signet

entities.name: Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield

tagline.text: The Right Back Atcha Personal Shield is a short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles that throws out an overeager small buckler. It catches physical attacks on Carl's dexterity and magic bolts on his intelligence, and sends three in four of them back at the attacker, sometimes doubled.

description.text: Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield. You ever meet one of those dudes who is always super quick to take offense to everything? You gotta walk on eggshells around him. Has some job where he wears a shirt and tie even though he looks like he just woke up in an alley somewhere. He’s always saying, “What the hell is that supposed to mean?” He hits on anything with a pulse. He wants people to call him T-Bone or Bulldog or something. He dies of a heart attack in his mid-forties. You get my drift. Well, this little auto buckler is the armor version of that. …

beats.headline: Swapped for the Peach Pit
beats.text: Among the box prizes is a forearm bracer, black, short and covered with little buckles. Carl already has two: the one that forms his Grull gauntlet, and the one on his left arm that forms a buckler meant to disarm opponents 1.5 percent of the time, which he has never got to work. This one auto-deploys a small buckler that catches physical attacks and magic bolts, with a 75 percent chance to reflect them and a 25 percent chance to double the reflection. Mordecai says it is much better, and it matches the other bracer. Off comes the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit, onto the pile for the Faction Wars team.

tagline.text: The peace symbol patch is a small upgrade patch from Carl's gold pacifist's box. It makes neutral mobs less likely to aggro and adds ten per cent to his Dexterity and to his skill at the bongos, and it is sewn to the bottom of his jacket, beside the bomb symbol.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This patch depicts a peace symbol. Ahh, isn't that cute? Buzz off, dirty hippie. Go be smelly somewhere else. The Grateful Dead sucked. And so does Phish. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: Neutral mobs are less likely to fall into aggro. +10% to Dexterity. +10% skill in playing the bongos. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.
