beats.headline: Ink that does not fade
beats.text: After Donut's dog tattoo, Milk tells Carl there are more magic systems than he can imagine, dozens with ink and calligraphy and maps alone, and that inks and letters that shine the brightest burn out the fastest. She had a book once and wrote her recipes in it, then switched to a different ink to share them more widely, and only recently learned that all she wrote after the change faded and disappeared. She hands him a wineskin: Stayfast Ink, 825 ml. Then a fountain pen, the adept's, the most basic of a calligrapher's implements. He has another book, she adds, the Book of Voodoo, and anything he writes in it reaches everyone who has it.

relations.note: Carl takes Milk's story of her book to be about the Cookbook

tagline.text: A Mini Tactical Nuke rides on the back half of the biggest Reaver sentry dogs. When Elle froze one solid, Carl hauled the burning block of ice into his inventory before it could go off.
Carl still has his, attached to its dog, and keeps quiet about it; Samantha has one of her own hidden up her neck hole.

beats.headline: Into the inventory, frozen
beats.text: Robot sentry dogs pour out of the holes in the Reaver castle's great wall: Reaver Industries Security Sentry Dog, the Ditch Digger, optional anti-personnel explosive. One of the larger ones, the size of a lion, carries a massive glowing bomb notification on its back half, and before Carl can examine it, an Elle spell turns it into a ball of ice. He rushes forward and lifts the block. It burns, but it goes into his inventory before the dog can explode. The bomb says Mini Tactical Nuke. Fall back, he shouts.

beats.headline: The castle goes up
beats.text: Carl tells Juice Box to drop the No Disassembles Louis carries and get clear, then runs with the others, shouts for everyone to hit the deck, dives atop Donut and triggers them remotely. The pulse should fry every robot dog at once, but the bombs themselves would still... The Reaver castle explodes from the inside out, flinging them all. Carl's bones break and his hearing goes again, and he decides the bombs are much smaller than he feared: probably only one of the mini nukes went off, maybe two. Everyone seems okay but Jamal, whose legs the initial No Disassemble has wrecked.

beats.headline: Up her neck hole
beats.text: Samantha thinks her child died in the acid, and she is quite certain it is Tish's fault, so once this is done she is going to plant the nuke she stole from Buster, the robot dog she bonded with, up at the college. You have a nuke up your neck hole, Carl asks. He has one too, still attached to one of the dogs, but he is not about to tell her he has one of the dangerous robots. Nobody is nuking anyone, he says. Tell us the plan to save Louis.

beats.headline: Still in stock
beats.text: Carl dropped every bomb he carried when he fled out of Larracos, and he needs to restock. All he has left are the big bombs, such as Carl's Doomsday Scenario and the tactical nuke still attached to a robot dog. That reminds him that Samantha also has a nuke hidden up her neck hole, and it has to come out as soon as possible.

relations.note: carried by the sentry dogs guarding the Reaver castle
one of her own, taken from her robot dog

entities.name: A Banquet Fit for a Princess

tagline.text: A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Donut's own book from the crawlers leaving the dungeon: pictures and kind words about her, and on each page a skill or spell its painter gave up. Eating a page lends her the spell for a short while.
Every page in it that offered lightning magic has been removed, and Donut carries a dozen lightning spells into Club Scolopendra.

beats.headline: A present in Larracos
beats.text: In the rings around them, thousands of crawlers who mean to take a deal on the next floor, and former crawlers going home, look down as Milk announces a present. Carl's Book of Voodoo splits in two. Donut shouts that she has a book called A Banquet Fit for a Princess, filled with pictures and nice things about her, and spells. Milk taught the leavers to take out a skill or spell and paint it onto a page, three each: one for Carl, one for Donut, one for anyone. They lose it for good. Eaten, a page gives it back for a very short time, depending on the quality of the drawing, and each should carry a personal note of thanks.

beats.headline: Luca Di's pasta
beats.text: An entry from Donut's Banquet: Luca Di, a human Pastamancer, final level sixty-two, who gave her his train hat on the fourth floor. His mother had dementia, and they were in the dungeon soon after he wheeled her out of her home. On the third floor she took a Benevento, an elf-like witch, and with her mind repaired they could finally talk. She fell during the bubble level. He tells Donut it is okay to forgive herself for War Crime, and that she saved him and his mother's memory. The drawing is a bent tube of pasta. The spell: Temporary Macaroni, cast at level 14.

beats.headline: A tunnel of cannelloni
beats.text: Skulls pelt and explode against the shield of the car behind. Carl shouts for macaroni, and the truck's windshield shatters. Donut, who has just taken the spell from her Banquet Fit for a Princess, casts Temporary Macaroni, and a tube of pasta fifteen feet tall and twenty wide appears ahead like the mouth of a highway tunnel. The spell casts at level 14, enhanced to 15, and at that level she can choose its size, shape and direction: uncooked, dried cannelloni, at least a foot thick, ten mana a cast. She chains it into a tunnel, and Gluteus slides the truck inside.

beats.headline: Mees Koning's magnet
beats.text: Another entry: Mees Koning 2, a half-orc Boring Ol' Mage, final level sixty-three. He froze around people and stuttered, the race choices only made him uglier, and when a Whoopsie Daisy spell backfired he took two player-killer skulls and was alone. Before the battle at the southern border in Faction Wars, Donut stopped at his stinger unit, said she liked his fangs, and told him about Imani and that we all have scars. He was inside the ball when she cast her Atrocity. The drawing is a curved piece of metal with little electric bolts. The spell: Big-Ass Magnet, cast at level 14.

beats.headline: Every lightning page
beats.text: The hints about Scolopendra scattered through the dungeon's descriptions all have one thing in common, and Carl has seen it: lightning. So every page in Carl's Book of Boom, Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess and the original Book of Voodoo that offered lightning magic has been removed, and the party is strapped head to toe in lightning spells. Donut has eaten a dozen. Even so, killing the centipede is only the backup plan.

relations.note: she taught the departing crawlers to paint their spells onto pages
arrives with Carl's book

entities.name: Carl's Book of Boom
entities.role: The second volume of the Book of Voodoo

tagline.text: When the Book of Voodoo floods with entries it splits in two, and the second volume is Carl's Book of Boom: pages painted by crawlers leaving the dungeon, each a note of thanks with a skill or spell he can eat to use for a short while.
Every page in it that offered lightning magic has been removed, and Carl has consumed ten different spells for the fight against Scolopendra.

beats.headline: The second volume
beats.text: Milk's voice carries over Larracos: the crawlers in the rings have a present. Carl's Book of Voodoo is updated with a metric fuckton of entries and segmented into two volumes. The second is Carl's Book of Boom. It behaves like the first, about five hundred pages where the Book of Voodoo should by now have almost thirty thousand, and it zeroes in on the entry he is meant to find. He opens it at random. Crawler 1,982,122, Asi Hamami, a level 59 fox warrior, thanks him and has not lost hope. Below, a crude red lock and key. Eating the page gives a level 10 Lockpick skill for five minutes.

beats.headline: Mehmet's page
beats.text: An entry in the Book of Boom: Mehmet Or, a human Sipahi, final level sixty-two. He owned a bowling alley in Istanbul, left to him by his father. He asks Carl to forgive him for taking a deal; he has too much to lose. His daughters, Azra and Yaz, did not step into the light with him, and he believes they are alive where the children are kept. If Carl cannot save those who took deals, please find them and tell them their father loves them. His party's mage loved this spell. The drawing is an amateur bowling alley. The spell: Gutter Bumper, cast at level 9.

beats.headline: Bumpers away
beats.text: Rolling toward the raft, Carl has already eaten Mehmet's page. He casts Gutter Bumper, clicks on the river ahead, is warned that it will not cover the whole river, and deploys. Donut casts Ice Slick, and the river freezes along the bumpers in a winding line, half again as far as the cone would reach. It is not the explosive magic Carl is always hunting for, but here it is perfect. He never met Mehmet. He has heard of him: a support player who saved countless lives in Faction Wars.

beats.headline: Does your dad own a bowling alley?
beats.text: Lucia Mar's manner changes in an instant, shoulders hunched and afraid, and she grabs Carl by the shirt. A shining lady has told her that Carl knows her father, that he gave Carl a spell. Her name is Azra, and Yaz is here too, crying, while the goddess tells them Carl used their father's spell to win his races. Carl remembers the note in the Book of Boom he ate for the Bumper spell. Does your dad own a bowling alley? Yes, that's him. He is safe, Carl tells her, and he loves her.

beats.headline: Strapped in lightning
beats.text: Every hint about Scolopendra in the dungeon's descriptions has had one thing in common, and Carl has seen it: lightning. So every page in Carl's Book of Boom, Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess and the original Book of Voodoo that offered lightning magic has been removed, and they are strapped head to toe in lightning spells. Carl has consumed ten different spells; Donut has a dozen, and Elle too. And this is only a contingency, stacked on other contingencies.

relations.note: its second volume
she taught the departing crawlers to paint their spells onto pages

tagline.text: Made human again by Eileithyia, Katia is missing her right arm to the shoulder, her left leg, her right leg up to the knee and an ear. She built cybernetic parts for herself in anticipation, Bautista finished them, and she waves goodbye with her cybernetic right arm.

beats.headline: Clicked into place
beats.text: Eileithyia tells Katia she will first be made human again, and Katia shrinks, her blonde hair turning black. Her entire right arm is gone to the shoulder, her left leg is gone, her right leg up to the knee, and an ear. Just a few things she has lost along the way, she says. Bautista quickly brings the cybernetic parts: she made them herself in anticipation of this and left them in the crafting room, and he finished them. They all click and fasten them into place while the goddess lays her hand on Katia's stomach. The word Ineligible appears over her head. Bye, guys, Katia says, raises her cybernetic right arm, waves, and is gone in a puff of smoke.

relations.note: he finished them

tagline.text: The Scorpion's Bite is a non-magical quadruped weapon mount from the Apothecary's gold benefactor box, a bandolier that lets Donut carry ranged weapons on her back and fire and load them from her inventory. Katia's crossbow, bigger than Donut herself, forms on it.
Loaded with Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus, the mount puts a bolt into one of Emberus's eyes, and a Danforth bolt into the other.

description.text: Quadruped weapon mount. “The scorpion’s bite.” Non-magical bandolier accessory. Allows for the mounting of multiple ranged weapons. May fire and load via inventory action.

beats.headline: A gift with an implication
beats.text: In Eileithyia's tent, Donut stalks a circle round Huanxin, whose shields she has just clawed away, while the goddess cannot move until Katia makes her choice. A strange device appears on Donut's back, from the gold benefactor box she received from the Apothecary: a simple gift, Carl thinks, but the implication is clear. A non-magical quadruped weapon mount, the scorpion's bite. Katia's crossbow forms on it with an ominous click, bigger than Donut and not loaded, and she holds the weight just fine. It is not as strong as it could be, she says, because she has no women in her party.

beats.headline: A bolt for the driver
beats.text: On the starting line, Donut's target is Rapture, the womantaur driver. Her weapon mount forms on her back with Katia's crossbow, and a glowing Danforth bolt locks into place on its own; they have only ten and hope to get this one back. The plan: when the light turns green, Carl breaks the window, Donut roots the driver in place with the bolt, and Chiyome's giant bear smashes the car aside, so that it moves out from under her.

beats.headline: Into the god's eye
beats.text: Emberus, sobbing, enraged and growing, rears back with a flaming ball in his hand. Donut zaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with the Scorpion's Bite on her back and the crossbow cocked and ready. Loaded into it is Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus. Donut aims, and she fires true: the bolt buries itself in Emberus's smoldering eye socket. A second shot enters the other eye, one of her ten Danforth bolts, designed to hold the god in place.

tagline.text: The wheel gives the Royal Court a Big Shot Chicken food truck, about twenty feet long, with a faux-1920s hood, chrome fenders, a brand-new aluminium kitchen in the back and no passenger seat. A giant plastic tommy gun on its roof partly blocks the windshield.
After every race the garage regenerates the food truck to the form it started in. Its first upgrade is a set of retractable spider legs, Hedy's pick, which can climb walls when they are switched on.

The food truck races on spider legs and resizable all-terrain tires, with a gyro that keeps it from flipping, a full Bubble Buddy shield, a heat sink, booster rockets, and Roller Limbo, which lets it race upside down.
Off the tenth floor, the truck's racing rules no longer apply: its consumables are no longer magically refreshed, and all damage has to be repaired by hand.
The food truck is the last float in the Royal Court's procession, with Dwight's looted magic missile launcher on its roof and a crew of sluggalos at the wheel and the deep fryer.
Smashed, stinking of fire and somehow still running, the food truck pulls up beside Carl with about ten sluggalos left inside.

beats.headline: The wheel picks a food truck
beats.text: The wheel clicks past a bookmobile, the Popemobile, a forklift and a missile launcher and settles on the square shape of a box truck. What crunches into place on squeaking shocks is a food truck, about twenty feet long, with a chicken in a fedora and red tie painted on the side: Big Shot Chicken, the 1920s-gangster chain whose safe room Carl and Donut sat in on the second floor. It has a faux-1920s hood, chrome fenders, round fluted headlamps, a brand-new aluminium kitchen, no passenger seat, and a plastic tommy gun on the roof. Carl turns the key. The engine starts.

beats.headline: Make way for the big shot
beats.text: Mongo is left in the truck as security and finds the horn, which is not a honk but a recording of a gangster's voice saying make way for the big shot, a chicken squawk, and a tommy gun's rat-a-tat. It is funny the first time. By the twentieth, Carl wants to rip it out. Then Mongo leans on it while Dwight's tumbleweed mount stands at the cave mouth, and the plant bursts forward, over the trailer and the van and away. There is no trailer hitch, so the flatbed carrying Team Free Love's van is chained to the welded step under the back door. Radoslav rides in the open back watching the trailer, and Jasha stays in the van.

beats.headline: Spider legs, on Hedy's advice
beats.text: In the garage, Hedy taps the trailer and does not approve of the help. Carl wants the kitchen gear out of the back and the gun off the roof, because it blocks his view. At the end of every race, Hedy explains, the truck is regenerated to its form at the start. Her tablet offers a mobility upgrade first: retractable spider legs, a hover upgrade, or all-terrain tires with vertical climb. Spider legs are her pick. Carl swipes through over a thousand options, weapons included, and hands the tablet back. Pick the spider legs. Sexy and smart, says the gremlin.

beats.headline: Over the line in the air
beats.text: Gluteus Maxx passes out at the wheel before the finish of heat three. Carl grabs the wheel, Donut rips free of her seat to stamp on the accelerator, and Carl lies on his back across the hood, steering over his shoulders, feet aimed at a kaiju skull. Then Dwight's cannon rips through the side of the truck. It flips and spins like a badly tossed football, clips the GTO and the vine, and all three go over the finish line in the air. The truck lands on its back and spins off. Tater tots, fries and chicken patties are everywhere. First place: the Royal Court.

beats.headline: Two Golden upgrades
beats.text: After the fourth heat there are two Golden upgrades to pick, and the next track needs vertical climb, inverted racing and gaps of more than a hundred metres. Hedy suggests one Golden and three regulars, and they take her advice: the Bubble Buddy shield brought up to its golden version, which floats and holds off molten steel for a while; a heat sink in case they lose containment; and the regular version of Team Sparkles' booster rockets, which with the bubble should carry them over long jumps. The Golden one is Roller Limbo, a trans-dimensional upgrade for racing upside down and slipping under any gap of ten centimetres.

beats.headline: Upside down over molten steel
beats.text: In the fifth heat the spider legs carry the truck up a flat wall and onto the ceiling, lowering its wheels onto a track, and Roller Limbo holds it there over a river of molten metal. In the back, everyone stands on the overturned counter: Donut, Grigori, Dong, Corky and Porky, blood sloshing as spells hold them together, and Grigori calls out instructions for pressing a head back together. Gorilla-like beasts of molten metal hurl globs at the racers. The heat sink gauge tops out twice, and a hole opens in the hood over the whirring engine.

beats.headline: The last float
beats.text: At the arena's huge door Carl sends Tipid out of the cab to the RV, and Bigs and a crew of blood-soaked sluggalos pile in to drive. The side server window opens, the deep fryer hisses on, and the Sluggalo Chick-Chick Express is open for business. A fryer will splash or catch fire, Carl warns; Bigs tells him to do his thing. With his face on the jumbotron, Carl pulls the last rope, the display collapses, and the massive magic missile launcher looted from Dwight stands on the roof. This is our revolution, he tells the galaxy. Floor it. The truck lurches forward and sideswipes the door, and only the gyro keeps it from flipping.

beats.headline: Spinning, burning, firing
beats.text: When Donut's Puddle Jumper brings her and Carl back out to the arena entrance, the food truck is spinning in circles, flames pouring from the side window by the deep fryer, missiles launching one after another at the Krakaren boss while sluggalos crawl over it. The Krakaren boss is in the stands with only two tentacles left. Moments on, the truck is miraculously still upright, still on fire, still spinning. Most of the sluggalos who were riding outside are gone, and the missile launcher is wrecked.

relations.note: the garage mechanic who picks and fits its upgrades
its navigation
driver in heat three
its driver in the parade
Donut's seat, voted in by the audience
the navigation box on its dashboard

tagline.text: Dwight is a sparkling unicorn, more magical than most, and the System advises that whoever kills him should grab his horn as quickly as possible, because certain parties value such horns.
Dwight's horn is a weapon as well as a treasure: in the Lollipop he stabs the karaoke DJ in the face with it.
Dwight's magical horn is in Donut's inventory, taken from his head before the notification of his death has even arrived.

beats.headline: Grab the horn
beats.text: Team Sparkles stops in the road, and Carl examines the bigger of the two: Dwight, a level-87 sparkling unicorn enchanter. A sparkling unicorn, the System says, is pretty much a unicorn, but it sparkles because even more magic permeates it. Their horns are quite valuable to certain parties, so if Carl kills him, he should grab the horn as quickly as possible. Most unicorns are known for their gentle manner. But not Dwight.

beats.headline: Stabbed into the DJ
beats.text: At the Lollipop the gremlin DJ has been on the floor yelling at Dwight, who still has not moved. The DJ goes back to his booth and calls up Princess Donut and Carl to sing Take On Me, slaps a microphone into Carl's palm, and the screens say Get Ready to Sing. Carl reads his scroll. The synth pop starts, the crowd cheers, the gauges appear. And that is when Dwight the unicorn stabs the DJ in the face with his horn.

beats.headline: Into Donut's inventory
beats.text: At the green light of the last heat, it goes for Dwight exactly as planned. He bursts off the line dragging his missile cart and fires his cannon into Bruna, whose shield is already up. The hole punch, the vine-killing potion balls and the GPS-frying potion all do their jobs, and Donut goes out the passenger window as smoke, onto the roof of the truck. Dwight's head comes off in a single swipe of her claw. Before the notification even arrives, his magical horn has been removed from his head and placed in her inventory.

tagline.text: Oozy Form is a special-edition spell book that ran out of the mailbox on little legs, spewing slime. Carl has read it, and he can turn into a slime and slip through cracks until the spell runs out.
Carl used Oozy Form for the first time in the cul-de-sac, to slide up to Jasha and Radoslav's beers and swap one for a bomb.
In Oozy Form, Carl has carried Penelope through the inside of Scolopendra, the pig made part of him by the backpack on his chest.

beats.headline: A book with legs
beats.text: Donut has opened the little door of the mailbox when a spell book scurries out, trailing slime, rushes across the room like an escaped rat and bangs against the kitchen cabinets. Mordecai shouts to catch it: they can break if they injure themselves. The cleaner bot swoops on it and drops it in Carl's arms, where it wriggles on its little legs and spews slime down his shirt. Oozy Form. With an O, like slimy: you turn into a slime. Mordecai calls it great, a special edition that trains faster, but warns him to be somewhere safe when it runs out; only at level 15 can he stay in it indefinitely. Donut is never going to use it.

beats.headline: Applied in both hands
beats.text: Donut gives the ooze a suspicious sniff. Her Smoke Form, from her new class, is better, a Phase-style spell, so Carl should take this one. Mordecai agrees: Carl's Gloom Wraith Phase is an attack and forces him in a direction, so it is no use for travel, and with this both of them can slip through and around obstacles. The spell book squeals and squirts more goo, and the cleaner bot complains. Sorry, says Carl, and grasps it in both hands and applies it, learning Oozy Form.

beats.headline: A beer in the cul-de-sac
beats.text: Forgive me, friends, Carl whispers, and clicks Detonate. Team Free Love is eliminated, both racers dead. The bomb went in at the cul-de-sac. Samantha rolled in to distract the two bugbears while Carl used his Oozy Form spell for the first time, slid up and replaced one of their peach-flavoured beers with the can they had given him, drilled out and fitted with a hidden explosive he built in his bomber's studio. Their magical cooler teleports back into their van after every race.

beats.headline: Through the centipede's organs
beats.text: Inside Scolopendra they land in a massive chamber with a slippery, stinking floor, and on the map the outer wall of the club is perhaps fifty metres away. Carl casts Oozy Form. Splatch. He has done this only once before. He loses his eyes and his ears, his vision is suddenly all around him, and he can see perfectly in the dark. Thanks to the magic of the carrier, Penelope is part of him too. He slimes toward the building wall over and around giant pulsing organs, forty seconds before the next attack.

relations.note: out of the mailbox; her own Smoke Form is better, so she tells him to take it
a passenger buckled into the backpack goes with him

tagline.text: An Emergency Gremlin scroll is a heavy green summoning scroll that clanks like metal. It calls up a gremlin who can fix a vehicle that breaks down mid-race, or a biological mount.
A summoned emergency gremlin arrives in overalls with a toolbox, a little different every time, and explodes when its summoning runs out.

beats.headline: Twenty of them
beats.text: Donut's boxes are mostly crappy clothes and healing scrolls until a green scroll clanks heavily onto the table, as if it were made of metal. Emergency Gremlin? The next several boxes hold nothing else, and suddenly she has about twenty. Why does she need so many emergency gremlins? It is a summoning scroll, Mordecai says, like Bautista's toys. They can fix your vehicle if it breaks down mid-race, and this kind can fix biological mounts too. Donut hisses as more appear.

beats.headline: Babies for the pouch
beats.text: Prison Pocket wants babies. Carl reads an Emergency Gremlin scroll as Donut reads hers, and he repeats it three more times, and eight bewildered gremlins in overalls stand in the road with their toolboxes, one in goggles, one with one eye, one with a hook for a hand. What're we fixing, boss? The kangaroo dips two in his pouch, and eats more to heal. Carl tries not to feel bad: Imani says they explode when the summoning ends anyway. Afterwards one survivor drops his toolbox on Carl's stomach, tells him to go fuck himself, and times out.

beats.headline: Word gets round the garage
beats.text: Back in the garage the generated gremlins chitter angrily at Carl, and one flips him off. Donut explains to Hedy that they used some Emergency Gremlin scrolls to distract the boss: a few got dipped in the pouch, a few got eaten, and she wonders how the others even know. To Carl's surprise, Hedy laughs. Serves the little freaks right. They'll still fix the truck true. Probably.

beats.headline: Keeping Bruna alive
beats.text: The roof blows, Osvaldo is gone, and he has left a grenade to kill Bruna, his slaughter gnu. The party fires three potion balls at her to save her life: a liquid drop shield, an explosion blanket and a smoke curtain. Donut lands on the gnu and casts her own shield, sprouts trees all round her, and then a half dozen emergency gremlins sprout along the gnu's back. She has already been poisoned, but one of the gremlins is in his toolbox pulling out medicine. They can help biological mounts as well as mechanical ones.

tagline.text: The Assassin's Veil is a beaded Egyptian headdress for a female cat, worn in the court of the goddess Sekhmet. It adds ten percent to dexterity and warns its wearer when someone nearby readies a spell or a skill, and the enemies of Sekhmet turn hostile at the sight of it.

description.text: Enchanted hat item. The Assassin's Veil. This is a unique item. Warning: This item may only be worn by a female. Warning: This item may only be worn by a feline-class species. Worn by those in the court of the goddess Sekhmet, this beaded headdress warns off strangers who might think to do harm to the bearer. Wearing this item imbues the following benefits: Plus 10% to dexterity. The Precognition Benefit. Warns wearer if someone nearby is preparing an offensive or binding spell or readying a skill. Warning: Enemies of Sekhmet will be automatically hostile to you if you wear this in their presence.

beats.headline: A veil that covers nothing
beats.text: The mailbox has given Donut another hat, and one each for Mongo and Rend. Hers appears on her head in place of her tiara: an Egyptian-style beaded headdress, red, yellow and orange beads cascading down either side of her face to match her fur, the beads clacking as she shakes her head at a little mirror. It calls itself a veil, though it does not cover her face. She means to drain its magic into her tiara. Mordecai warns that the conditions would transfer too, and that Sekhmet is surely under Odette's thumb by now, so Odette's enemies would all be hostile to her. Let him research it first.

entities.name: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion

tagline.text: The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion is a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail from a celestial box, the matching piece to Donut's champion cloak.

The crupper has the cloak's abilities, and worn together as a set they buff Donut's constitution a further twenty percent, take Find Weakened to level 10 and let her raise Puddle Jumper to 16. A third piece of the set would earn her a fourth.

description.text: Enchanted crupper. The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. This is a unique item. This item is part of a matched set with the Cloak of the Benevolent Champion. There are two more pieces to this set. Find the third, and the fourth will be awarded in a box. Considering what you did to get this one, it's gotta be something really good. This item was originally awarded in a celestial slap-chop box during the 9th floor. Let's talk about what a hero is. You, Donut, received this prize because you performed one of the most brutal kills in the history of this game. …

beats.headline: A golden blanket, a swan
beats.text: Donut's War Crime spell earned her two celestial boxes. The slap-chop box is a quivering golden blanket that flutters through the room like a magic carpet, dances about, folds into an origami swan and opens on a plain silver crupper, like the one she already wears but made of fine chain mail instead of larger scales. Holy fucking shit, says Mordecai, before it disappears. He has not seen its abilities yet, but it matches her champion cloak. It is called the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion.

beats.headline: A matched set, and a rant
beats.text: Off comes the Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, worn since the first floor for a +2 dexterity that is laughable now, and on goes the new one: lighter, more elegant, with an opalescent glow. An achievement for a matched set says a third piece earns a fourth. Then Donut reads the description and goes stiff. It is about Sanderson Pinkstaff, a gnoll quartermaster she killed in her attack, and his children, and whether a hero can be a hero to all. It makes her raise one spell to level 16 now. She picks Puddle Jumper.

tagline.text: The Danforth is an enchanted crossbow bolt that does no damage and anchors the part of a body it hits in place, for two seconds per level of the shooter's Crossbow skill. Donut has about ten of them.
Donut puts a Danforth bolt into Emberus's second eye, after Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus takes the first, and the god cannot move.

description.text: Enchanted crossbow bolt. The Danforth. This bolt does no physical damage. However, anyone hit with it will be anchored in place for (two seconds × your Crossbow skill level). More specifically, the area of their body that is hit with the bolt will be anchored in place. If they happen to be moving at the time, the physics involved might get a little . . . messy.

beats.headline: Sparkly, from a hot-dog bag
beats.text: Donut's legendary Lorena Bobbitt box comes as a giant 7-11 hot dog bag. The wrapper drips imaginary blood as it peels back on a quiver of glittering crossbow bolts, about ten of them. They're so sparkly, says Donut. Carl snatches one before they disappear and reads it: whatever part of a body it hits is anchored in place, and if the target is moving, the physics get messy. Hell yeah, says Carl, and asks her Crossbow skill. She tells him he is ruining it.

beats.headline: The shot not taken
beats.text: The plan for the start of the second heat has a Danforth bolt in it. Donut's Scorpion's Bite mount forms on her back with Katia's crossbow, and the glowing bolt locks into place on its own with an ominous click. They hope to get it back; there are only ten. At the green light she will root Rapture, the Lady Dominators' driver, in place, and Chiyome's giant bear will smash the car out from under her. Donut has the shot. At the green light she tenses to fire, and pauses: a long tank-like tube has popped out of Team Sparkles' bush, aimed at the muscle car in front of them. It fires, and the car goes straight up into the air.

beats.headline: Holding a god
beats.text: Emberus, enraged and growing, is rearing back with a flaming ball in his hand when Donut zaps into the room by one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps, the crossbow cocked on her back. Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus goes into one smouldering eye socket. A second bolt goes into the other: one of her ten Danforth bolts, to hold the god in place. His yellow invulnerability glow winks off. He is vulnerable for fifteen seconds, and he cannot move.

tagline.text: The Nemes of Pestilence is a striped pharaoh's headdress that came with Donut's new class, for Mongo. When he is within three meters of her and her health falls below ten percent, he turns invulnerable and twice as strong for sixty seconds, once a day, and his bites carry a 75 percent chance of Cruel Sepsis.
Donut's new Gurkha class has brought wild clothes for every pet, but Mongo keeps the nemes on for the parade's fight, with kukri claw caps on his feet besides.

description.text: Enchanted hat. The Nemes of Pestilence. This item may only be equipped by a pet. Equipping this item to an eligible pet will imbue the following properties: Eternal Protector of Rage. Pet will become temporarily invulnerable and will gain 2× strength if it is within three meters of its owner and their health is below 10%. Invulnerability will last 60 seconds and can only trigger once per day. Bringer of Death. Bites from this pet have a 75% chance to inflict the Cruel Sepsis debuff.

beats.headline: A hat for Mongo
beats.text: Donut's new class came with accessories for every pet in the party, and the mailbox has delivered hats for Mongo and Rend. Carl asks whether those can be drained too. Donut will not have Mongo's new hat's powers stolen, and Mordecai says they cannot anyway: both are labelled pet accessories. Then the two are on the table. Mongo's is a fabric hat with shiny blue and gold stripes and two wide bands hanging down either side like large, floppy ears: the sort of thing a pharaoh wore, by way of a cheap costume shop. A nemes. Carl examines it. Eternal Protector of Rage, Bringer of Death. It will look absolutely ridiculous on Mongo's head, but that protector benefit is worth it.

beats.headline: Dong does the honours
beats.text: In the garage, while Hedy explains the gremlins who do the bulk of the repairs after a race, Dong Quixote helps Mongo into the hat. Isn't it great, says Donut. The dinosaur looks absolutely ridiculous. Rend starts grunting and bouncing up and down as Donut produces his headband.

beats.headline: Kept on for the parade
beats.text: The float procession takes shape in the garage, and Mongo, Rend, Simoom, Gonk and Bianca are its marching band. Donut's new Gurkha class has brought some pretty wild clothes for all the mercenaries and pets, but for this fight the crew keeps the nemes on Mongo and the headband on Rend. Mongo gets special kukri claw caps for his feet as well, which greatly increase his slicing.

relations.note: a pet accessory that came with her class
Donut's own headdress from the same class, examined in the same chapter

tagline.text: The Wrap of Sekhmet's Compassion is a red headband, Rambo-style, that came with Donut's new class, for Rend. When he is within three meters of Carl and Carl's health is below ten percent, Rend turns invulnerable for sixty seconds, once a day, and gains the Heal Party Member skill, and his fatal bites have a 75 percent chance of casting a level 10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse.
Rend has come back from his sixth death bigger, and the headband from Donut's class has stayed with him, slipped down to half cover his eyes.

description.text: Enchanted headband. The Wrap of Sekhmet's Compassion. This item may only be equipped by a pet. Eternal Protector of Health. Pet will become temporarily invulnerable and will gain the Heal Party Member skill if it is within three meters of its owner and its owner's health is below 10%. Invulnerability will last 60 seconds and can only trigger once per day. Bringer of Resurrection. Fatal bites from this pet have a 75% chance to cast a level 10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse.

beats.headline: A headband for Rend
beats.text: The second pet accessory from Donut's class is more a headband than a hat: a red piece of fabric, Rambo-style, until a closer look shows the rich red covered with an intricate pattern Carl cannot quite make out. It does almost what Mongo's nemes does. Eternal Protector of Health: sixty seconds of invulnerability and the Heal Party Member skill, once a day, when the pet is within three meters of an owner under ten percent health. Bringer of Resurrection: a 75 percent chance that a fatal bite casts a level 10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse. Holy hell, says Carl. Bigs asks why she got no hat, and Carl tells her she is not a pet: she is technically a mercenary.

beats.headline: Bouncing for it
beats.text: Back in the garage, Rend sits in a circle with Splash Zone, Dong and Mongo, watching Hedy balance a wrench and giggling in his deep baritone, raw French fries falling from his mouth. Donut produces Mongo's Egyptian hat, and Dong helps the dinosaur wear it. Rend starts grunting and bouncing up and down as Donut produces the headband.

beats.headline: Left on guard duty
beats.text: The garage door opens on a different world, and Donut tells Mongo and Rend to stay behind with Splashy and Dong and guard Hedy. Mongo screams in protest, waving his wings, and Rend, wearing his new headband, complains loudly too. Dong salutes as the door closes.

beats.headline: Half over his eyes
beats.text: Rend giggles as he rises from the dead. It is his sixth death, so he keeps his memories and identity and comes back 25 percent stronger, with a new random weakness: potatoes. Carl shouts at the ceiling that random, his ass. Mongo dances around the awake Rend. The Tummy Acher is bigger now, and the headband from Donut's class has stayed on him, sitting slightly lower and half covering his eyes. He gives a deep giggle and turns to the garage door as if nothing has happened.

beats.headline: Kept on for the parade
beats.text: Rend marches in the float procession's marching band with Mongo, Simoom, Gonk and Bianca. Donut's new Gurkha class has brought some pretty wild clothes for all the mercenaries and pets, but for this fight the crew keeps the headband on Rend and the nemes on Mongo, and the mounts get black-and-gold blankets that raise their constitution by 20 percent.

relations.note: a pet accessory that came with her class

tagline.text: Donut's right front claws glow a brilliant blue since her godslayer box, and four red claw caps from the shop, bought by Rosetta, mute the glow to purple. She can take them off and put them back on through her inventory.

beats.headline: Red, to mute the blue
beats.text: The godslayer box's prize is a celestial boon on Donut's right front paw. Extended, its four front claws glow brilliantly blue, like obnoxiously bright LED lights, and what about Carl's shoulder, she asks, when they come out on their own? Claw caps, says Rosetta from the shop interface: made for exactly this, in different colours, removable at will. You might as well cut her paw off, says Donut; go with purple. These stupid claw caps better mute the glow. Rosetta buys red ones, a little translucent, and puts four on the table. They go into Donut's inventory and appear on her claws, and the blue light is muted and purple. This will have to do.

beats.headline: Off for the Astral Paw
beats.text: Cannibals scream and shake spears from an arch of bent, tied-down tree over the way ahead, and the cannibals dropping onto the truck are overheating its shield. Vaguely racist, Donut mutters. Her claw caps disappear and blue light fills the cab. She swipes into open air, and her Astral Paw sweeps the cannibals off the bridge like pieces off a chessboard; whatever held the arch down snaps and the tree flips up like a catapult. She waves a few more times, clearing the trees. Then she growls with annoyance, her claw caps reappear, and the giant paw dissipates.

relations.note: she bought them at the shop interface
the caps come off for the spell

tagline.text: Ice Slick is a special-edition spell book, freezing cold to the touch, for a spell that lays an inch-thick sheet of ice over a wide area. It starts at level 5 and trains faster, and Donut calls it an Elle spell.
Donut's Ice Slick normally casts in a cone, but laid along Carl's Gutter Bumper it follows a whole river and runs half as far again.

beats.headline: An Elle spell
beats.text: Carl asks about the other spell book, hoping to take Donut's mind off her blue claws, and she brightens. It's an Elle spell! The spell book thumps onto the table, and when Carl picks it up it is freezing cold. Ice Slick covers the ground in ice an inch thick over a wide area, how wide depending on intelligence and the spell's level. Carl has seen it used a few times now. This copy is a special edition, so it starts at level 5 and trains faster. This is great, he says.

beats.headline: A frozen river
beats.text: The raft waits on the River of Sloth, which is full of inner-tube gingers. Carl, who has eaten Mehmet's page from his Book of Boom, lays Gutter Bumper along the river. Donut leans forward and casts Ice Slick, and in seconds the whole river freezes, cracking, splitting and exploding, the ice following the bumpers half as far again as it would reach in its usual cone. Hundreds of gingers are stuck in place. The truck drives over the dock and onto the ice, dragging every spare non-magical weapon from Carl's inventory behind it on chains.

beats.headline: The dance floor
beats.text: In the mostly-music middle of Take On Me, with a brawl filling the Lollipop, Donut casts Ice Slick on the dance floor. A group of fighting NPCs goes spinning and crashes against the bar, into Prepotente, who is bent over the unattended counter rummaging behind it, and he flips with a yelp and disappears with a clatter.

entities.name: Quadruped baby backpack
entities.role: A chest carrier for a pet

tagline.text: A Gold Adventurer Box has given Carl a pink baby backpack, worn on the chest, that only carries quadrupeds. With a passenger buckled in, his Phase or Oozy spell takes them too, and Donut refuses to get in it.
Mordecai has modified the backpack to fit a giant pig, and Carl wears Penelope strapped against his chest.

beats.headline: Like the Hangover movie
beats.text: One more item of note comes out of a Gold Adventurer Box: a pink backpack thing. Donut sniffs it and says it looks like one of those BabyBjörn baby backpacks from the Hangover movie, and asks whether Carl and his new wife have already had a honeymoon. That is exactly what it is, says Carl, except it only carries quadrupeds. It is for carrying her on his chest, and if he wears it with her buckled in, his Phase or Oozy spell will phase her too. Donut is absolutely not getting in. Does she look like a milk-soaked toddler? Carl laughs. It might come in handy someday.

beats.headline: The backpack is done
beats.text: With seventy-five minutes on the countdown on every screen, and crumbs and wrappers all over the room, Carl lays a patch, a gun, a sewing kit and a holster out on the table and asks out loud whether Mordecai got the chance to make the carrier thing. Mordecai answers in chat. The backpack is done, and it is sitting on Carl's crafting table. Carl thanks him and starts sewing a patch onto his jacket.

beats.headline: A pig on his chest
beats.text: Carl pulls open the back of the truck. A sluggalo is on fire, and Penelope is eating a fully cooked chicken sandwich, already wearing the front part of the harness. He only has to slip his arms through. He steps out wearing the enormous, struggling pig against his chest: the special backpack from the start of the tenth floor, meant for Donut so he could take a quadruped through his movement spells, modified by Mordecai to fit the giant pig, whose legs wave in the air. She squeals. Even at his strength it is a struggle.

beats.headline: Unhooked in front of a god
beats.text: In Oozy Form, thanks to the magic of the carrier, Penelope becomes part of Carl as he slimes through Scolopendra's insides, and he does not want to think about how that works. Inside the club, with the floor rumbling and Emberus in front of them, he activates Sticky Feet, tells Penny not to move and promises her more splooge, unhooks the backpack and gently sets her on the floor, then steps aside so she is out of the line of fire.

relations.note: modified it to fit a pig

entities.name: Enriched Pet Biscuit
entities.role: A pet biscuit with a known result

tagline.text: An Enriched Pet Biscuit is a highly refined pet biscuit with a known result instead of a gamble. Prepotente has three from a celestial box: the Paramour, Nothing Special, and Nothing Special Party Companion.
The Nothing Special Party Companion biscuit has made Penelope the pig a sapient crawler who cannot talk out loud, in a party with Carl because he fed it to her.
Donut, combining in a hurry from Carl's inventory, put the wrong pet biscuit into the bomb for Scolopendra, and the boss comes out of her goo a level-one crawler in Carl's party instead of a pet.

description.text: Enriched Pet Biscuit. “The Paramour.” This is a unique item. Okay, so we all know by now what enhanced pet biscuits do. While extremely valuable, enhanced pet biscuits are items that leave the result up to chance, and when you feed your pet one, there’s a very real risk you’ll be saying goodbye to your furry friend forever. Or they’ll be saying goodbye to you. … This is an Enriched Pet Biscuit. This leaves nothing to chance. These are highly refined pet biscuits with a known result. This biscuit imparts the “Paramour” benefit. …

beats.headline: Three from a celestial box
beats.text: Prepotente puts a glowing little treat on the table. He got it in a celestial box, one of three, and they are not the run-of-the-mill enhanced biscuit: one is Nothing Special Party Companion, one is Nothing Special, and this one. Carl picks it up. Enriched Pet Biscuit, "The Paramour": a known result, an upright transformation, a reset to level one, crawler status for a dungeon-born pet, and a permanent, incurable charm that makes the eater fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them. Nothing Special makes a creature a dungeon pet in juvenile form. The Party Companion one keeps its existing form and gives no ability to talk.

beats.headline: Absolutely not
beats.text: Prepotente wants advice. Her name is Ragazzaccia, and she was his girlfriend before the dungeon. Absolutely not, says Donut: he will not be turning anyone into a sex slave. With the other two biscuits, he protests, she would stay a regular goat, and it is not called that: it is called Paramour. Donut points out that she would be a level-one crawler, not allowed in a pet carrier or his safe room, and would get hurt. Nobody will like him if he uses that biscuit on anything. Don't use it. Ever. Right, Carl? Carl is still caught up on the biscuit that stops a pet from talking, and wonders aloud whether it is too late to give that one to Donut.

beats.headline: Penelope 3
beats.text: In the back of the truck Penny the pig is eating a chicken sandwich, already in the front of the harness. Carl examines her: Crawler #12,953,454, "Penelope 3," level 10, Yorkshire Pig, no class. They fed her the Nothing Special Party Companion biscuit, which made her a sapient party member without the ability to talk out loud, not that it stops her using chat. Because Carl fed it to her she is in a party with him. He has blown up whole settlements, thousands of NPCs dead by his hand, yet dragging a pig into sapience feels like a line he never knew was there, especially since he means to use her as bait.

beats.headline: Search and combine
beats.text: Every inventory has swapped hands and Donut is holding Carl's. Racing at the centipede, he yells for her to combine the ball in his hotlist's slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve. Her hotlist only has ten slots. Search and combine, he shouts, fast. She finds it and drops the ball into his xistera, and he flings the banger sphere with the biscuit inside straight into Scolopendra's yawning mouth. The biggest, baddest entity in the dungeon splatters onto the arena floor, a gelatinous puddle the size of a small elephant.

beats.headline: The wrong biscuit
beats.text: By the biscuit's description, the boss should come out of the goo a regular pet at level one, to live in a pet carrier in Carl's inventory: if he dies, she dies, a true fail-safe. Then Donut tells him not to get mad. With the inventory moving so fast, she made a mistake. The gelatin drains away to a human-sized centipede, and a new member joins the party: Sexy Scolopendra, level 1, a crawler, with a humanlike face, giant lips, no arms and a red bow on one feeler. She is not a pet. Donut gave him the wrong pet biscuit. Hi, Carl, she says, and boops his nose.

relations.note: combined it into the bomb from Carl's inventory

tagline.text: The Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin is a dead joey's hide worn as a costume, with clawed gloves, padded palms and big kangaroo feet. It protects from seeping acid and gives a level-10 Jump, and it is a twelve-hour timed item that will not come off.
In the crash at the end of heat three the kangaroo skin flays off Carl as he slides down the road, and its feet catch fire, but the shredded suit is still on him.
Carl's shredded kangaroo suit has two hours left on its timer, and he still has to move in little hops.

description.text: Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin. This item fills a costume slot. This can be worn as an outer garment. You might want to protect your face, though. I'd fuck me. I'd fuck me so hard, mate. Equipping this costume imbues the following effects: Protection from Seeping Acid. A level 10 Jump skill. +5 to the Lotion Application skill. Warning: This is a 12-hour timed item.

beats.headline: Peeled off the engineer
beats.text: Genesis was supposed to bring Carl a dead joey. She hooks the engineer in Prison Pocket's pouch through the face with her grappling hook instead and drops the body at his feet, so Carl has to pull the kangaroo skin off Niels's corpse. It is stuck fast and burns his hands. It has built-in gloves with long clawed nails and palms padded like a dog's paw. He shoves his arms in and pulls the head over his own, and it clicks. His boxers and kneepads are now outside it, and his boxer and pedicure effects are negated. He turns to run at the boss and falls flat on his face.

beats.headline: Hopping into the pouch
beats.text: So Carl hops. He leaps higher and farther than he expects and lands on the outside of Prison Pocket's pouch, and the boss stuffs him in face-first. The costume's claws drag him down through warm jelly, burning, past bones, more joey corpses and a toolbox, to the bottom, where he releases his two satchels. Then he presses his kangaroo feet against the inside, hops as he phases out, and detonates in midair. When he starts to pull the costume off, the System reminds him it is a timed item.

beats.headline: Paws that can feel
beats.text: A generated gremlin leaves the truck, wrench in hand, and Carl is about to hop back from a kneecapping. Instead it hands him a note and runs off. The paper is weirdly warm. Carl unfolds it awkwardly with the costume's kangaroo paws and realises with a start that he can feel its wetness: he has sensation through the paws. It is bizarre enough that he stops to stare at their pads for several seconds.

beats.headline: Too short for the pedals
beats.text: The kangaroo suit makes it hard for Carl to reach the pedals properly, so Gluteus Maxx, the best of the strippers at Mario Kart, drives heat three, and Carl crouches between him and Donut, which is awkward in the suit too. At least it is clean-ish again after the showers. At the line Gluteus admits he has taken two of Samantha's outworlder uppers. Carl asks Donut to get her Laundry Day spell ready and get the suit off him so he can drive. No, says Donut: Mordecai said it could really hurt him, even kill him. Then the ground rumbles.

beats.headline: Feet first at the skull
beats.text: At the end of heat three Carl lies across the hood, his foot buff run out, and activates Daughter's Kiss, meaning to ram the kaiju skull with his giant feet. Dwight's cannon flips the truck, his feet hit the skull and it explodes, and he lets go of the wheel. He hits the ground and slides, and screams as his kangaroo skin flays off. Afterwards his kangaroo feet are literally on fire, and when he tries to walk on them, he falls over.

tagline.text: Hobgoblin big boom satchels are explosive satchels Carl keeps ready in his inventory. Two of them, released at the bottom of a demon kangaroo's pouch and set off from outside, blow a level-170 gatekeeper apart.

beats.headline: Two satchels in the pouch
beats.text: Prison Pocket, a level-170 gatekeeper, blocks the road, and Carl's plan goes through his pouch. Carl, dressed as a joey, prepares two hobgoblin big boom satchels in his inventory and hops. Stuffed into the pouch face-first, he claws his way to the bottom and releases both satchels, which start to degrade quickly. He presses his feet against the inside, hops as he activates Gloom Wraith Phase, and hits the detonator in midair. He lands rolling on the asphalt while ice and kangaroo bits rain down round him.

tagline.text: Denial of Service missiles are Rosetta's idea: a load for Carl's eight-pack launcher, a different recipe from his potion balls but just as insidious, for a race in which every team has a shield and a direct attack will likely do nothing.
A Denial of Service missile does not explode. Its impact sets off a chemical reaction that spreads a thick membrane of green slime over a wide area, blinding a vehicle under its own shield.

beats.headline: Marked and programmed
beats.text: Heat three, with Gluteus Maxx at the wheel and a dragon-faced Draconian on One Fine Pig's APV manning a heavy machine gun. Carl marks the Draconian with two denial-of-service missiles and the gun with two more, to fire as soon as they are free; he wants that team slowed, not killed. The other four in his eight-pack launcher he programs too. By now every team will have shields, and direct attacks will likely do nothing. This is a Rosetta idea, a different recipe from the potion balls but just as insidious.

beats.headline: Goo, not boom
beats.text: Team Sparkles is rolling far ahead on some sort of rocket. Carl aims the launcher straight up and fires out the back of the speeding truck, and the eight missiles spiral off, four toward One Fine Pig and four toward Sparkles. They are not designed to explode. Three slam into Sparkles' bush, which veers off spinning in panicked circles, its round shield covered in a thick membrane of green slime so they cannot see. Drop the shield and the sludge falls into the vines, which Mordecai insists will slow them to a crawl.

beats.headline: Too early over the pigs
beats.text: A message from Chiyome, somewhere behind: the missiles meant for the Fine Pigs detonated too early, and the goo went all over the place, Onikuma included. Her team cannot see, the road is too steep for their Oni, who keeps stumbling, and the Jugglers are somewhere back with them. Carl tells her to move to the right side; they will toss the tunnels if a third wave comes.

beats.headline: Goo on the loop
beats.text: In Satan's Water Park, Florin has Denial of Service missiles too, and has said he will hit Team Sparkles just as they start the loop-de-loop: too slow, and they drop out and start again. Now they are on his tail and about to bump him, so he fires. When Satan headbutts the whole loop over and both vehicles come tumbling down near the food truck, the Sparkles vine is on fire and covered with goo.

relations.note: her idea

tagline.text: The Smart Companion Royal Pet Throne is the passenger seat the audience voted Donut: an ordinary bucket seat until she sits on it, when it grows a fluffy bed, monitors her vitals, feeds her snacks and agrees with everything she says. Donut has named it Dorota and given it a Polish accent.
Dr. Metcalf, whom the chair's very existence has annoyed from the start, has cut Dorota off mid-sentence and put her into diagnostics mode, out of commission for a few hours.

beats.headline: The princess throne
beats.text: The audience voted Donut a new seat, and Hedy saw to its installation. On the passenger side it looks like a regular bucket seat until Donut sits in it, when a small, fluffy, rectangular bed appears. It is a real product out in the universe, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition: it adjusts like a gyro to keep her safe in an accident, monitors her vitals, offers her relief when she is stressed, feeds her snacks on demand and compliments her fur. It came with a creepy man's voice; Donut insisted on a woman with a Polish accent, and named it Dorota. Its existence pisses off Dr. Metcalf.

beats.headline: Arms out of the seat
beats.text: Near the end of the tunnel Donut starts to recast her shield, and the large skull of some orc-like creature crashes through the front and wraps itself around her face like a facehugger. Before anyone can react, multiple arms appear from the car seat and violently rip it off her. The skull and the creature inside are torn to shreds. Thank you, Dorota, Donut sputters. Then, with Gluteus unconscious at the wheel, Donut struggles to get out of the car seat and it holds her tight, so she rips free with her claws, shredding the belt, and slams her paws on the accelerator.

beats.headline: Over its weight capacity
beats.text: Carl is in the seat with Donut on his shoulder, and Dorota does not see why both of them must sit on it at the same time: they exceed its recommended weight capacity. Its breathtaking princess should sit there alone, it whines. Without her it has no purpose, no reason even to exist, and with the nude human added it is unable to function. Carl says he is not naked. Donut asks Dorota to please stop complaining.

beats.headline: Cut off mid-sentence
beats.text: The audience's upgrade for Dr. Metcalf is cosmetic, a hologram. I don't like the way she's looking at me, says Dorota, tightening the straps around Donut. The hologram becomes a giant floating head, and Dorota promises to protect her princess from the obviously senile... and the voice cuts off. The straps loosen. Dorota is broken, cries Donut. Dr. Metcalf, small again, says she has just initiated Dorota's diagnostics mode: the chair might be defective, and will be out of commission for a few hours.

beats.headline: Still gagged, still useful
beats.text: Moments before the heat, Carl has been turned into a long-haired dachshund, and Donut, ready to go, needs the window down. It is manual, she may not break the glass until the heat starts, and Jamal is too snug to reach. Then Donut's chair, still muted, unhooks herself, an arm appears, grasps the handle and quickly rolls it down. Thank you, Dorota.

relations.note: put into diagnostics mode, and kept gagged

tagline.text: Eris's five-sided coin looks like a plain poker-chip-sized coin with her laughing face on one side and a swirl on the other, until she reveals four fates on it. Carl snatches it out of the air, and it dissolves into a swirl tattoo on his palm that spins on its own.
Eris has told Carl not to forget about the coin: they have until the end of the twelfth floor to figure out how the fifth side lands.

description.text: I don't even know what the hell this is. This bitch is coloring outside the lines.

beats.headline: Four sides on a coin
beats.text: Eris spits into her hand and a coin appears, about the size of a poker chip, her laughing face on one side and a swirl on the other. Then she reveals its sides. Donut's face and RIP. Carl de-feeted, with a pair of bloody severed feet. A pile of bodies: Most of my friends are dead. Carl hanging upside down by one foot from a tree branch, smiling, player-killer skulls round the edge: I become what they accuse me of. One of the four has to happen before the Ascendent is chosen. She hands it to Uzi Jesus to flip, and Carl grabs it in midair.

beats.headline: The fifth side
beats.text: The coin burns in Carl's right fist and he does not let go. You picked the fifth side, Eris says, clapping: chaos wins again. The coin dissolves, and on his palm is a swirl pattern tattoo that spins on its own, like a slow-motion Signet tattoo. When he examines it, the System does not know what it is either. The fifth choice, Eris explains, is one of the other four, or two of them, or three, or all of them, or none of them. Chaos. Random. She kisses him on the lips: they will see what he gets.

beats.headline: Shown to the chat
beats.text: Carl writes down everything he saw and heard, starting with the four sides of the coin. Grabbing it unlocked the fifth choice and made everything random, and he wonders whether that made things much worse. Then, back with the others, he holds up his hand to show the swirl and explains it all in chat. The chat explodes. Hanging out with him, Elle writes, is as dangerous as hanging out with Samantha.

beats.headline: Until the end of the twelfth
beats.text: With Scolopendra a puddle, Eris, huge, tells Carl she does not need his worship: he is chaos incarnate. Does he know how doors work? Every exit is an entrance. And don't forget about the coin, she says. They have until the end of the twelfth floor to figure out how the fifth side lands. Then she is gone in a puff of smoke, and the world unfreezes.

relations.note: now a tattoo on his palm

tagline.text: A disintegration trap is a hidden trap module. Carl pulled one off the secret door that Akuma was hiding behind at the back of a diner.
Disintegration traps fire in silence and take a single target. Carl has laid two beside the Tigrans' truck, set to go off only under a Tigran.
Both of Carl's disintegration traps have fired, and team One Fine Pig is out of the race. No notification has come about Penelope.

beats.headline: Behind the yak poster
beats.text: Behind the jukebox at Chicken and Waffles and Upgrades is the room of top-shelf upgrades, and the upgrade imp, Hickster, lies dead on the counter with his eyes burned out, killed by Akuma. A note in black crayon on a kiddie menu calls Carl a moron for not coming alone. Behind a poster of a hairy yak in body armour is a secret door, and attached to the door is a hidden disintegration trap. Carl hops the counter, rips the poster off, deactivates and loots the trap module, scans for more, and opens the door on Akuma.

beats.headline: Keyed to Tigrans
beats.text: While Donut talks the twin Tigrans of One Fine Pig into staring at her, with relationship advice for their pig, Carl takes about five seconds to lay a hidden trap on each side of their truck, as close to its shield as he dares. Both are disintegration traps, like the one he looted from the war mage's door. They activate silently and target a single individual, and to be safe he programs both to go off only when stepped on by a Tigran. Even if one is carrying Penelope, she should be safe.

beats.headline: A pair of notifications
beats.text: At the pit stop, before Carl can announce the crew's new track, the notifications come in a pair. Your trap has activated: he has dissolved a Tigran. Another trap has activated, and he has dissolved another. Team One Fine Pig is eliminated on the expiration of both racers, and five teams remain. Carl holds his breath, waiting for a notification about Penelope the pig. There is none.

tagline.text: From this race on, the team that wins a heat is given a key. It opens a single garage of a defeated team, with whatever supplies, items or even vehicle or mount are left inside.
Carl's first garage key opened the house of One Fine Pig, and Penelope the pig was inside.
A garage key can be looted. Donut took Dwight's last two and came back with a bear and a dog for the parade.

beats.headline: A key for the winner
beats.text: Zev's harried voice announces the containment bubbles and the rule change that comes with them: a destroyed vehicle or a killed mount no longer loses the race outright, though last place still does. And from now on, the team that wins is given a key. That key opens a single garage of a defeated team, where there may be supplies to upgrade a vehicle or mount, other items, and in some cases an entire vehicle or mount, which can be added to the team's garage and swapped in at pit stops.

beats.headline: Two Golden upgrades and a key
beats.text: Carl's team has won the heat. Hedy, reading the room and unusually subdued, has two Golden upgrades to offer and a key, which means they can go into any of the old houses in the cul-de-sac; if they mean to trade vehicles, she says, do that before picking. Carl already knows: the house of One Fine Pig, whose armoured vehicle he rates below his own truck. Imani reports that Louis has just used his key to add a gecko to his garage, and found an engineer in a hidden room.

beats.headline: The garage of One Fine Pig
beats.text: The abandoned houses stand in the order their teams lost, so One Fine Pig's is the closest. Osvaldo asks whether Carl is using his key; Osvaldo lost the chance at his own heat's garages when he moved. Carl puts his hand on the garage door and it yawns open. Next to the parked APV with the cracked windshield stands Penelope the pig, licking up the remains of a gremlin. Hi, Penny, says Carl, going to a knee. She snorts happily and follows them out.

beats.headline: Dwight's last two
beats.text: Donut bounds away before Carl can stop her, rushes to a garage door, swipes and goes in. The keys, he realises: Dwight had two left, and she has looted them from him. She goes into the garage of the razor foxes and then into the garage of the Jugglers, and it takes maybe two minutes. She comes back grumbling, having moved Onikuma the bear and Old Shuck the dog to their own garage, and she is not going to talk about it. They will need them for the parade.

relations.note: Donut says he has two, and does not think he used them
the garage it opened held her

tagline.text: Splooge is the crew's name for the secretions the bat dudes sell at the pit stop. Half a potion bottle's worth protects the drinker from most environments for about half an hour; it smells like poop and, Louis says, tastes like Miami swamp ass.
Splooge has carried Carl through toxic air, kept a starfish alive, and calmed a panicking pig, who now craves it.
Splooge does not let anyone breathe where there is no air at all. It is a type of potion, but it is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply to it.

beats.headline: Not really splooge
beats.text: At the pit stop Louis brings Carl the bucket he bought for him. It is not really splooge, he says; that is just what they are calling it. It says it is secretions, which he does not think means poop, though it smells like it. The bat dudes sell it. Prepotente will not stop talking about it: a single sip, about half a potion bottle's worth, seems to give half an hour of protection against most environments, though it has to be drunk manually. Because it tastes like Miami swamp ass, says Louis. Donut keeps a good distance from the buckets.

beats.headline: A full cup, nine minutes
beats.text: In apartment 130 Prepotente sits in the toxic air against the leg of his mother's piano, Jurgen is stopped on Sweety in the hallway, and the race has ten minutes left. Carl pulls a full cup of splooge from his inventory, swallows and drinks it down, gagging; it tastes worse than he expected. You've been Splooged: protected from environmental hazards, and for a whole hour, which is awfully bold with nine minutes left in the race. He pulls himself out through the ceiling, jogs into the living room and spots Prepotente cross-legged on the floor. Leaving the truck, he cannot breathe for a moment and his eyes burn, and then it settles in his chest.

beats.headline: Dropped on a starfish
beats.text: The wheel's first attack was a Transformation, and Imani checks in at once: Elle has been turned into a goblin, Jacobus is a starfish, and she had to drop splooge on him to keep him alive. Florin's lot are unchanged, Chris is a werewolf in human form, and Prepotente's Apito memorial crystal kept him and Jurgen from changing at all. Carl is a long-haired dachshund with a German accent.

beats.headline: A beaker for the pig
beats.text: Carl steps out of the truck with Penelope, enormous and panicking, strapped to his chest, her legs in the air. He takes a beaker of splooge and pours it down the spluttering pig's throat, and she calms. Okay, that's a delight, she writes in chat, more please; it says it's called splooge, and she craves it. Carl drinks some more himself, choking it down, then puts his father's gun to the pig's head and calls for Taranis.

tagline.text: Gelded Choirboy is a scroll that lets Carl physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot, at the cost of sounding squeaky. Mordecai insists the name is not literal, and Carl reads it alongside a few singing potions Mordecai has compounded together to get round the cooldowns.
On the Choirboy scroll and Mordecai's potions, Carl sings Take On Me through a bar brawl and hits the high note, and he is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.

beats.headline: Squeaky on purpose
beats.text: The guild only opens to someone who sings a song with the needle in the green. Mordecai has compounded a few special potions together, a new trick to get round potion cooldowns, so Carl and Donut stay in sync; Carl takes the lead on a two-singer song. The scroll, Gelded Choirboy, is so he can physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot. Mordecai insists the name is not literal. It will make him squeaky, so he will read it at the last second. The singing potion lasts a long while, so he drinks it now: Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd, Dio'd. Onstage he reads the scroll. You've been Choired! He sounds as if he has sucked helium. Then Dwight stabs the DJ.

beats.headline: The high note
beats.text: Carl sings Take On Me through a full bar brawl. Bottles break against him, Dong clears the stage with his sock, and on the extra-high note the gauge by Carl's head chimes and showers digital sparkles. Half the crowd stops fighting. Both gauges sit all the way in the green, his with little flames out of the top. He catches Donut's toppling microphone stand between his toes and keeps singing, off the stage as the curtains burn. Fireworks on the long last note. A paralysed kappa falls on Donut during her final line. Carl is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.

relations.note: he compounded the singing potions read alongside it

tagline.text: An XL pet carrier cannot hold a crawler, but it can suck one in who allows it, for about ten seconds before it breaks. Mordecai's has a device fixed to the outside, and it is how the crew means to get Li Na out.

beats.headline: Ten seconds inside
beats.text: Prepotente examines a pet carrier and hands it to Mordecai, who holds it up for Li Na: an XL pet carrier, with some sort of device installed on the outside. Carriers cannot hold crawlers, he explains, but they can still suck one in if the crawler allows it; within about ten seconds the carrier breaks and expels them with a Bonked debuff. A carrier with a crawler in it will not go into a personal inventory, but the cleaner bot's weight-based utility inventory works. XL carriers are expensive. Zhang points it at Li Na, she nods, and she disappears inside. It starts buzzing, and the white cleaner bot picks it up.

relations.note: sucked into the bot's weight-based storage before it can break

tagline.text: Big-Ass Magnet is a spell on a page of Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess, drawn by Mees Koning, a half-orc mage she was once kind to for about a minute. It casts at level 14.

Cast on an object, Big-Ass Magnet activates at once and grows stronger for about fifteen seconds. Donut casts it on Dong's lance, and it pulls every screw within two hundred metres toward him and Corcunda as they charge Grull.

description.text: Drawing: A well-shaded, curved piece of metal with little electric bolts coming off it. Associated Spell: Big-Ass Magnet. Casts at level 14.

beats.headline: A page from Mees Koning
beats.text: An entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess comes from Mees Koning 2, half-orc, Boring Ol' Mage, final level 63. He always felt invisible; a backfired spell left him with two player-killer skulls and nobody at all. Before the battle at the southern border in Faction Wars, Donut stopped, said she liked his fangs, waited out his stutter and told him we all have scars. He was inside the ball when she cast her Atrocity. He used to draw anime characters, and his drawing is a well-shaded curved piece of metal with little electric bolts coming off it: Big-Ass Magnet.

beats.headline: The backup plan
beats.text: In the fifth heat, Prepotente's plan is for Bianca, his hellspawn familiar, to grab Corky out of the back seat of the Lady Dominators' car, once its shield is down. If that does not work, there is a backup plan, which Carl came up with about ten minutes earlier and which is a little more iffy. It involves the Big-Ass Magnet spell Donut has just eaten from her Feast book.

beats.headline: Every screw in the factory
beats.text: Corcunda, one man again, will go out to meet Grull, and Dong climbs onto his back with his lance pointed out the open back of the truck. Wait, says Donut: it has to be cast on an object, it activates at once and grows for about fifteen seconds, so be far away. It is the spell meant for Genesis and Rapture's car. She casts it on the lance as they jump. Every screw within two hundred metres rockets toward the charging pair, through the slag elementals, which stagger and melt into puddles of molten steel. The lance meets the god of war, and Grull vanishes back to the twelfth floor.

relations.note: cast on his lance

tagline.text: The hidden beer-can bomb is a peach-flavoured Busch Light from Team Free Love's own magical cooler, drilled out in Carl's bomber's studio and refilled with an explosive that only a level-12 Find Traps skill would notice. Carl sets it off himself.

beats.headline: Forgive me, friends
beats.text: Osvaldo says he is about to cross the finish line, and Carl cannot know what place the Royal Court is in. He looks at Donut, and she nods. He finds the detonator under Primed in his explosives menu, whispers forgive me, friends, and clicks Detonate. Team Free Love is eliminated due to the death of both racers. Earlier, Samantha distracted the bugbears while Carl, in Oozy Form, swapped one of the peach beers in their cooler for the one they had given him, drilled out and fitted with a hidden explosive. The cooler teleports back into their van after every race.

relations.note: the can itself

tagline.text: The Tome of Gatekeeper is Donut's spell book from the floor prize, a paperback Advance Reader Copy that can be installed now and works from the twelfth floor. It strips a target of their class skills and abilities for a while, and a deity of most of its spells.

description.text: Tome of Gatekeeper. This is an Advance Reader Copy. Street date: 12th floor. Cost: 75 Mana. Target: Any opponent or NPC or deity or OI entity. Duration: (5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell) × [Your Intelligence / (Target's Constitution + Charisma)] Ahh, Gatekeepers. I hate Gatekeepers. … This spell removes the target's ability to use any skills or abilities associated with their class for a short period. If this spell is cast on a deity, they will temporarily lose access to their Worshipper Base Associated skill and spell set. You probably don't know what that means yet. It's basically most of their spells and skills, but if it's a god made of lava, they'll probably still be able to fuck you up with lava. …

beats.headline: An advance reader copy
beats.text: Donut insisted on claiming her spell book from the floor prize, and she has not read it yet: she thinks it is a good spell, but she is not allowed to use it, and its duration is in nerd math. She zaps it into Carl's hand. It is, strangely, a paperback, the first he has seen, and looks nothing like a spell book, with a drawing on the cover of an angry woman standing in front of a gate. Its description rants about gatekeepers for a while and then explains itself. Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is. Mordecai has no clue.

tagline.text: Gurkha hats come with Donut's Elite Gurkha Warrior class: wide-brimmed, camel-coloured hats worn at an angle that reshape to fit whoever wears them. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels, and Donut's raises several skills by five.

beats.headline: Hats for the parade
beats.text: Donut's new Gurkha class has given her mercenaries and pets some pretty wild clothes. For the parade, the hats are the hit. Rosetta, riding Onikuma the bear, wears hers with pride and a glittering red gown. Bigs's is the size of a thimble on one eyestalk, Jamal's reshapes itself to fit a shark's head, and Samantha's brim stops her rolling properly. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels; Donut's raises several skills by five, and there is no time to drain it into her tiara. Mongo gets kukri claw caps, and the mounts black-and-gold blankets worth twenty percent constitution and Steady Charge.

tagline.text: Petey Motteux's Little Secret is a large, thick nipple ring from the jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside from earlier crawlers. It gives its wearer the Oxygenated benefit, marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on the map, and is now through one of Penelope's nipples.

beats.headline: A ring for a pig
beats.text: The chamber inside Scolopendra has no air, and the splooge does not help. Penelope struggles and a health bar appears. Carl applies an anti-oxygen-deprivation potion to himself but stops before giving her one: her constitution is three, and a second potion too soon would poison her. Then an item in his inventory catches his eye, from the pile of jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside, taken from previous crawlers. A nipple ring called Petey Motteux's Little Secret. He did not want it, and Donut refused it; it was too big for her to eat. It grants Oxygenated, and Bawdy, which marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on a map.

beats.headline: Pierced, and too late
beats.text: It is the only choice they have. Carl shoves the empty gun into the fancy holster, reaches forward until he feels a nipple on the pig, and installs the ring by piercing her flesh. A new achievement flashes as Penny squeals in surprised pain. Then Mordecai writes that splooge is a type of potion but is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply. Now you tell me, says Carl. I just pierced a pig's nipple.

relations.note: the splooge gave no air; the ring did

tagline.text: A Tracking Tag is a dart Carl finds sticking out of his leg after the last fight in the arena, with no idea when or how it got there. Its text says the Kyryap has claimed him.

description.text: Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. Fucked = you.

beats.headline: A dart in his leg
beats.text: Carl takes Emberus's memorial crystal into his inventory, and then he notices something odd: a dart sticking out of his leg. He did not feel it and cannot feel it now, and he does not know when he got it or how. He gently pulls it out. Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. Fucked = you. He jumps into his debuffs to see whether it has left anything there. There is something new, but it concerns his Emberus ring, not this. His hope is that the Kyryap, whatever it is, dies in the floor collapse.

relations.note: the tag says the Kyryap has claimed him
